labs.title: Classic Login Bypass on Legacy Guestbook
labs.description: A nostalgic PHP guestbook admin panel builds its login query by concatenating raw POST fields into a SQLite statement: SELECT id FROM users WHERE username='$u' AND password='$p'. No prepared statements, no escaping, no filter. The application is designed to feel like an early-2000s intranet tool that a junior dev copy-pasted from a forum, complete with a comment saying 'TODO: fix later'.
labs.objective: Log in as the built-in 'root' admin (whose password hash is unknown even to the challenge author) through the /admin/login endpoint, then load /admin/dashboard which prints the flag once a valid admin session cookie is presented.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/dashboard reads /flag.txt from inside the container and renders it inline when the session cookie 'role' decodes to admin (server-side check after the SQLi-based login succeeds). Flag file is 640 root:www-data.
labs.inspired_by: The canonical PortSwigger 'SQL injection vulnerability allowing login bypass' lab plus classic OWASP WebGoat login examples

labs.title: UNION-Based Extraction on Vintage Vinyl Store
labs.description: A minimalist Flask storefront for a vinyl record shop offers /search?category=jazz. The category parameter is spliced into: SELECT title, artist, price FROM records WHERE category='<param>' AND released=1. There is no filter, no WAF, and errors from MySQL are echoed verbatim on the page, which makes column-count enumeration and datatype discovery straightforward.
labs.objective: Perform a UNION SELECT to retrieve the value of the 'secret' column from the 'admin_notes' table and submit it via GET /solve?token=<value>. The endpoint compares against the row seeded at container start and returns the flag on match.
labs.flag_hint: GET /solve?token=<extracted> compares against admin_notes.secret; on match it returns 200 with the flag from /flag.txt. Wrong token returns 403.
skills_taught: Column count enumeration via ORDER BY
Datatype coercion (converting int columns to strings)
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'SQL injection UNION attack, determining the number of columns' plus HackTheBox 'Cronos' walkthrough style

labs.title: Column Discovery via ORDER BY on Blog Archive
labs.description: A Django-esque Postgres-backed blog exposes /archive?sort=3. The value is inserted into an ORDER BY clause built as: 'SELECT title, author, published FROM posts ORDER BY ' || sort || ' ASC'. There is no quoting because the app 'assumes' it is a numeric input. This means classic tautology payloads fail, but CASE-based conditional errors and integer offset probing succeed. It teaches the special-case of injecting where quotes are not present.
labs.objective: Determine the exact number of columns AND the position of the numeric column, then trigger a CASE-based error whose SQLSTATE message leaks the value of current_user. Submit it to /solve?user=<value> to earn the flag.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the ?user param to current_user() and if equal writes the flag to the response body from /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'SQL injection vulnerability in an ORDER BY clause' plus real Postgres error-oracle patterns from Assetnote research

labs.title: Error-Based Extraction with EXTRACTVALUE
labs.description: A ticket-tracking dashboard's filter widget calls /tickets?assignee=alice on a MySQL 8 backend. The parameter is single-quoted into a WHERE clause and errors are rendered verbatim inside a friendly yellow banner. Blind extraction is unnecessary because MySQL will happily return the payload contents inside XPATH error messages generated by EXTRACTVALUE and UPDATEXML.
labs.objective: Extract the value stored in secrets.api_key (a UUID) using EXTRACTVALUE-based errors, then POST it as JSON {"key":"<uuid>"} to /solve. The server verifies via string comparison and returns the flag.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with correct JSON body triggers a shell exec of 'cat /flag.txt' whose output is returned to the client.
skills_taught: Concatenating payloads with CONCAT and 0x3a delimiters
Handling MySQL's 32-char error truncation using SUBSTRING
labs.inspired_by: Classic MySQL error-based technique originally documented by Reiners/awae, and countless bug bounty reports using EXTRACTVALUE

labs.title: SQL Injection Hidden in a Tracking Cookie
labs.description: A tiny promotional microsite drops a 'TrackingId' cookie the first time you visit, then uses it verbatim in a SELECT that looks up which welcome banner to show. Because the injection surface is a cookie rather than a URL param, students who only tamper with query strings will miss it. The DB is SQLite so union/comment syntax differs from MySQL and teaches SQLite-specific quirks (double-quoted identifiers, no LIMIT-in-UNION restriction).
labs.objective: Use the TrackingId cookie to perform a UNION-based extraction against sqlite_master, then pull the flag-bearing row from the 'internal_config' table (column: license_key). Submit that license_key value to /solve?license=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve reads /flag.txt and returns it in a text/plain response body when the license_key query matches the seeded value. Otherwise returns HTTP 402.
skills_taught: UNION with unknown column count in SQLite
Using intruder-style enumeration on Cookie header
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'SQL injection vulnerability in cookie parameter' lab

labs.title: Boolean-Blind Extraction on Password Reset Lookup
labs.description: The 'forgot password' endpoint returns exactly two responses: HTTP 200 with 'If an account exists, an email has been sent' when a username matches, and HTTP 200 with the same body but an X-Response-Length header two bytes shorter when it does not. The lookup is a raw SQL query on a Postgres 15 users table. There are NO errors, NO UNION echo, NO time delays available. Students must build a boolean-oracle extraction script.
labs.objective: Extract the 32-character bcrypt-cost prefix of the admin user's password hash (stored in users.password_hash where username='admin') via boolean-blind bit-by-bit exfiltration, and submit it to POST /solve with JSON body {"prefix":"<32chars>"}.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the submitted prefix against the seeded hash and, on match, returns the flag from /flag.txt as the JSON field 'flag'.
skills_taught: Building a boolean oracle from subtle response differences
Writing a Python exfil script with concurrency
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'Blind SQL injection with conditional responses' plus real bounty writeups on account-enumeration side channels

labs.title: Time-Blind SQLi on Silent Analytics Endpoint
labs.description: An analytics beacon /beacon?ref=<value> returns HTTP 204 No Content regardless of input. Behind it, MySQL 8 executes INSERT INTO hits(referrer, ua) VALUES ('<ref>', ...). Because the endpoint has no body, no headers change, and no logs are exposed, the only oracle is response time. Students must craft time-based blind payloads inside an INSERT context (which forbids UNION and hides SELECT results), typically via subqueries with IF(...,SLEEP(3),0).
labs.objective: Exfiltrate the 40-character API token stored in secrets.beacon_token using time-based blind SQLi at approximately 1s per bit, and POST it to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve accepts JSON {"token":"<40char>"}; on match it exec's /usr/local/bin/give_flag.sh which reads /flag.txt and returns its contents.
skills_taught: Time-based blind extraction under INSERT context
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'Blind SQL injection with time delays' and countless real-world analytics-endpoint bug reports

labs.title: SQLi Through the User-Agent Header
labs.description: A marketing dashboard silently records every visitor's User-Agent into a MySQL analytics table. The admin panel later renders the top-10 UAs on an internal /admin/insights page (accessible from localhost only, but proxied through a debug route the challenge exposes). Injection happens on write via the UA header, and extraction happens on read via a stored-then-displayed UNION.
labs.objective: Register a stored UNION payload via the User-Agent header that, when the analytics dashboard renders it, discloses the value of settings.master_key on the /admin/insights page. Then POST /solve?key=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares against settings.master_key and, on success, returns the flag content of /flag.txt in the response body.
skills_taught: Chaining a write endpoint to a separate read endpoint
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'SQL injection in User-Agent HTTP header' and Shopify H1 report #341876 style analytics-log SQLi

labs.title: Second-Order SQLi via Malicious Username
labs.description: Registration accepts any username, escapes it correctly on INSERT, but the profile-view page later constructs raw SQL using that username to look up the user's referral chain. This is a canonical second-order pattern: the payload sits dormant in the DB until an entirely different codepath reads and re-splices it. Students learn to think about data flow across time and endpoints.
labs.objective: Register a user whose username is a carefully-crafted SQL fragment, then log in and visit /me/referrals to trigger extraction of admin.session_secret. Submit that secret to /solve?secret=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies session_secret; on match, returns flag from /flag.txt as the response body.
skills_taught: Balancing quotes across INSERT and re-use contexts
labs.inspired_by: OWASP second-order canon plus the Shopify 2020 second-order profile-name writeup

labs.title: Prisma $queryRaw Concatenation in a JSON API
labs.description: A modern TypeScript API accepts POST /api/reports with a JSON body {"filter":{"status":"open"}}. A hurried developer used prisma.$queryRawUnsafe with template concatenation to build 'SELECT * FROM reports WHERE status = ' plus the JSON value. Because Prisma is typically 'safe by default', many practitioners forget that $queryRawUnsafe is essentially string concat.
labs.objective: Inject via the JSON status field to pull rows from the confidential 'audit_logs' table and locate the row whose action='FLAG_ISSUE'. Submit its id (an integer) to POST /solve as {"id":<n>}.
labs.flag_hint: /solve reads /flag.txt when the id matches the seeded audit-log row id.
labs.inspired_by: The 2024 Snyk research writeup on Prisma raw-query misuse across GitHub

labs.title: Injection Inside LIMIT/OFFSET on Postgres
labs.description: A pagination endpoint accepts /feed?page=2&size=10. Both values are concatenated into 'LIMIT <size> OFFSET <n>' on Postgres 16. A plain UNION SELECT cannot follow LIMIT/OFFSET in Postgres, so the exploit uses the fact that the LIMIT/OFFSET position accepts an arbitrary integer expression — including a scalar subquery: a subquery that CASTs the target value to an integer fails, and Postgres echoes the value verbatim inside the error message (an error oracle).
labs.objective: Craft a payload in the size or page parameter that leaks admin.recovery_code (a 24-char string) through the Postgres error oracle, then submit it to /solve?code=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the code and returns flag from /flag.txt as JSON on success.
skills_taught: Reading SQL grammar to plan payload shape
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger's LIMIT-clause lab and Postgres-specific writeups by SecureLayer7

labs.title: MongoDB Operator Injection on Login
labs.description: An Express login endpoint accepts JSON and forwards it directly into a Mongo query: db.users.findOne({username: body.username, password: body.password}). By passing {"username":{"$ne":null}, "password":{"$ne":null}} the auth check trivially bypasses. From there, students learn to extract the admin password character-by-character using $regex operators.
labs.objective: Log in as the 'admin' user without knowing the password, then extract the value of admin.reset_token (SHA-256 hex, 64 chars) with $regex-based blind operator injection. POST it to /solve as JSON {"token":"<64hex>"}.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the token; on success returns the flag from /flag.txt in the response body.
labs.inspired_by: OWASP NoSQL injection guide and the classic HackTheBox 'MarketDump' pattern

labs.title: CouchDB Mango Selector Injection
labs.description: A document management API forwards a client-side 'filter' JSON verbatim into a CouchDB _find selector. This teaches a lesser-known variant: CouchDB Mango queries accept boolean operators like $and/$or/$regex and can be manipulated to bypass access controls, then to blindly extract document fields via combinatorial regex tests.
labs.objective: Retrieve the document with _id 'flag_holder' from the 'restricted' database (which the API normally hides from your account) and return its 'secret' field to /solve?secret=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the secret; on match it returns the flag from /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: The 2023 Sonar research writeup on CouchDB selector abuse plus CVE-2022-24706-adjacent techniques

labs.title: WAF Bypass with MySQL Versioned Comments
labs.description: A ModSecurity-fronted product search blocks 'SELECT', 'UNION', 'FROM', and common SQL keywords with case-insensitive regex, and also blocks '--' and '#'. The MySQL 8 backend understands MySQL-only 'versioned' comments like /*!50000SELECT*/ which the WAF regex misses. This lab is one rung of the filter-bypass ladder and focuses squarely on versioned-comment tricks.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate secrets.waf_bypass_flag through a UNION query that evades the WAF entirely (verified by /waf-log which shows which rule fired). Submit the extracted value to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve returns the flag from /flag.txt on correct submission; /waf-log shows fired rules for debugging.
skills_taught: Interleaving comments to break keyword regex
labs.inspired_by: OWASP CRS bypass research by Christian Folini and the widely-shared 'sqli-labs' waf-bypass series

labs.title: Whitespace-Filter Bypass Ladder
labs.description: A homegrown WAF strips every 0x20 space, %20, and + character before forwarding the request. It also normalises %09 tab to space and then strips it. To bypass, students must use non-standard token separators: parentheses to elide whitespace, C-style comments /**/ as separators, %0A newlines that survive the normaliser, and MySQL's tolerance of NUL bytes as separators.
labs.objective: Extract users.email for id=1 (the admin) using a payload that reaches the backend with ZERO literal space characters. Submit the email to /solve?email=<value>.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the email and returns the flag from /flag.txt on match. The included /debug endpoint echoes the exact bytes the WAF forwarded so students can verify no-space compliance.
labs.inspired_by: The wfuzz/ffuf community wordlists for space-less SQLi plus Rhino Security Labs bypass writeups

labs.title: Django ORM Escape Hatch: .extra() Misuse
labs.description: A well-meaning Django team used the ORM everywhere except one 'advanced search' feature where they reached for QuerySet.extra(where=[f"title LIKE '%{q}%'"]) to support fuzzy matching. Because .extra() takes raw SQL strings, the ORM's parameterisation is entirely bypassed. Students learn that 'we use an ORM' is not a defence, and that .extra(), .raw(), and RawSQL() are landmines.
labs.objective: Use the search box to blindly extract django_migrations content is boring; instead, target the auth_user table and read the 'password' column for the superuser (username='root'). Submit the full pbkdf2_sha256$ hash to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the exact hash and, on match, returns the flag from /flag.txt via the JSON field 'flag'.
skills_taught: Recognising ORM escape hatches in code review
labs.inspired_by: Django security advisories DJANGO-CVE-2022-28347 / -34265 and the 'ORMs won't save you' talk from DjangoCon 2023

labs.title: Rails ActiveRecord Hash-Condition Injection
labs.description: A Rails 7 API exposes /reports?filter[status]=open. The controller calls Report.where(params[:filter]) with no strong-parameters filter. Because Rails permits nested arrays and hashes to reach ActiveRecord, an attacker can pass filter[status][subquery]=... which under certain versions with .find_by_sql or with raw ORDER injection compiles into a subquery. This lab uses a specific known-unsafe pattern where params reach an ORDER BY via a companion sort field.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate the value stored in secrets.master_key by chaining a hash-controlled ORDER BY with a boolean sort-based blind side-channel, then POST it to /solve as JSON {"key":"<value>"}.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies key against seeded value; on match executes /opt/give-flag.sh which reads /flag.txt and returns it.
skills_taught: Blind extraction via sort-based side channels
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-32224 (Ruby on Rails) and Justin Collins' Brakeman scanner corpus of order() injections

labs.title: Out-of-Band Exfiltration on Oracle via UTL_HTTP
labs.description: An enterprise-style reporting endpoint runs on Oracle 21c XE and gives absolutely no output, no error, and no timing side channel worth using (the backend has ~500ms jitter). But the DB user has EXECUTE on UTL_HTTP and can reach a controlled DNS/HTTP collector running inside the lab network on port 9000. Students learn to exfiltrate data through DNS labels and HTTP paths.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate secrets.oracle_secret (a 32-char hex value) to the built-in collector at oob.lab:9000, then POST the collected value back to /solve to receive the flag. The collector's captured requests are also visible at http://oob.lab:9000/log.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the value matches secrets.oracle_secret and returns the flag from /flag.txt.
skills_taught: Reading collector logs to reconstruct extracted bytes
Handling ACLs and DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN in Oracle 21c
tech_stack: Custom Go 1.23 DNS/HTTP collector on port 9000
labs.inspired_by: The classic Chris Anley Oracle OOB paper and the modern-day Vozec/GossiTheDog Oracle OOB write-ups

labs.title: Stacked Queries and xp_cmdshell Reenablement on MSSQL
labs.description: An internal HR portal built with ASP.NET talks to MSSQL 2022 with SqlCommand and concatenated queries. The account it uses is sysadmin (as often happens in legacy shops). xp_cmdshell is disabled by default, but stacked queries let a student re-enable it via sp_configure with RECONFIGURE. Filters block spaces after semicolons; students learn to use %0A newlines and MSSQL comment styles.
labs.objective: Enable xp_cmdshell, run 'type C:\flag.txt' (Windows container) and exfiltrate its content to the OOB collector on oob.lab:9000, then POST that content to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies against the seeded flag string; on match returns HTTP 200 with the flag in the body. The OOB collector at oob.lab:9000/log shows received data.
skills_taught: MSSQL OOB via xp_dirtree UNC paths
tech_stack: ASP.NET 8.0 on Windows Nano Server 2022 base image
labs.inspired_by: SpecterOps and MDSec blog posts on modern MSSQL post-exploitation

labs.title: Elasticsearch DSL Injection with Painless Script Field
labs.description: A log-search UI forwards a user-supplied 'query' JSON into Elasticsearch's _search API, permitting a script_fields block. If a user can inject a Painless script, they can read arbitrary index documents and even runtime system properties (limited by Painless sandbox). Students learn 'SQLi-adjacent' NoSQL injection: same class of flaw, different DSL.
labs.objective: Read the '.credentials' index (normally hidden from your account by index filters) via script_fields, and extract the secret_key field of document id 'flag'. Submit that key to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve returns flag from /flag.txt on correct secret_key. /debug shows the ES query that was executed.
skills_taught: Painless script capabilities and sandbox limits
Reading ES cluster errors for oracles
labs.inspired_by: The 2020 Snyk research on ES DSL injection and CVE-2015-1427 spiritually updated for 8.x

labs.title: GraphQL Batch Mutations Feeding a Raw Prisma Sink
labs.description: A GraphQL API allows sending an array of operations in a single request. The resolver for 'searchReports(filter: String!)' calls prisma.$queryRawUnsafe with the filter concatenated. Batching lets a student burst hundreds of blind-boolean probes per request; students must write a GraphQL-aware exfil script and reason about resolver-level rate limits.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate secrets.batch_flag (a 40-char string) using boolean-blind extraction through batched GraphQL mutations, then submit it to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve returns flag from /flag.txt on match. A /metrics endpoint shows resolver call counts to help students tune batch size.
labs.inspired_by: The 2022 Assetnote research on GraphQL batching amplification

labs.title: MSSQL Header SQLi to RCE (FortiClient EMS Homage)
labs.description: A device-registration endpoint accepts an X-FCTUID header and inserts it verbatim into a MSSQL query. Sysadmin privileges are held by the app account, and while xp_cmdshell is off, it can be turned on with stacked queries. Students chain header SQLi -> sp_configure -> xp_cmdshell -> read C:\flag.txt -> OOB exfil. Chain length and defensive noise (a naive IPS logs 'SELECT' occurrences) test full-scenario tradecraft.
labs.objective: Register a device via POST /device/register with an X-FCTUID header payload that leads to command execution reading C:\flag.txt. Exfil the flag via oob.lab:9000 and POST it to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the flag string and echoes it back on match. C:\flag.txt is written at container init with 0400 SYSTEM.
tech_stack: Custom OOB collector on Linux sidecar
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-48788 Fortinet FortiClient EMS SQLi to RCE (abstracted; no proprietary code reused)

labs.title: Unauthenticated Blind SQLi in WP-Style Plugin (LayerSlider Homage)
labs.description: A minimalist WordPress-like CMS ships a marketplace 'slideshow' plugin whose AJAX action /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=ls_get_popup_markup passes the 'id' param into a raw wpdb->prepare call that concatenates instead of parameterising. No authentication is required. Rate-limiting slows time-based extraction to a crawl; students must optimise their extraction (parallel char probes, binary search).
labs.objective: Exfiltrate the wp_users.user_pass hash for user_login='admin' via unauthenticated time-based blind SQLi, then submit the full hash to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the exact hash; on match executes /root/give-flag.sh which prints the flag from /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-2879 LayerSlider unauthenticated SQL Injection (abstracted; original plugin code not reproduced)

labs.title: Header SQLi to Session Forgery and File Exfil (MOVEit Homage)
labs.description: A file-transfer application uses an X-siLock-Comment header to enrich an audit log stored in MSSQL. Concatenation into a stored procedure allows session-token forgery: the attacker uses SQLi to insert a valid session row for the built-in sysadmin user, then reuses that cookie to access /files/download for a marked confidential file. This is a two-step chain: SQLi -> session forgery -> authenticated file exfiltration.
labs.objective: Forge a valid admin session via SQLi, then download /files/confidential/flag.bin using that session and POST its SHA-256 to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve verifies the SHA-256 of the downloaded file matches the recorded value and returns the flag from /flag.txt on match.
tech_stack: ASP.NET 8 on Debian 12 (Linux MSSQL client mode via native)
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-34362 Progress MOVEit Transfer SQLi (abstracted; no proprietary code reproduced; only the chain shape)

labs.title: Elite Chain: Postgres SQLi to COPY FROM PROGRAM RCE
labs.description: A metrics microservice concatenates a filter param into raw SQL against PostgreSQL 16, running as a database superuser (a very common mis-configuration in Docker'd stacks). Superusers can invoke COPY table FROM PROGRAM 'shell command', which executes shell inside the Postgres container. Students perform SQLi -> stacked query -> CREATE TABLE tmp -> COPY tmp FROM PROGRAM 'id; cat /flag.txt' -> SELECT to read output back.
labs.objective: Achieve command execution inside the Postgres container via COPY FROM PROGRAM, read /flag.txt (mounted into the Postgres container), and POST it verbatim to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the submitted string against /flag.txt; on match it returns HTTP 200 with the flag echoed back plus a signed 'completion' JWT for the challenge platform.
skills_taught: Postgres COPY FROM PROGRAM privilege abuse
Recognising superuser DB accounts in containerised stacks
Stacked queries in Postgres via multiple statements
Reading command output back through a temp table
labs.inspired_by: The 2019 Adrien Peter DEF CON talk on Postgres COPY-FROM-PROGRAM and subsequent HackerOne reports (e.g. GitLab #827052)

labs.title: Reflected XSS in Search Results
labs.description: A vintage-styled bookshop echoes the ?q= query parameter directly into the search-results heading with no HTML escaping. A visitor bot polls any URL you submit through the /report form every 20 seconds while carrying the admin's session cookie, providing a controllable delivery target for a first payload.
labs.objective: Craft a URL that, when visited by the admin bot, causes the admin's document.cookie value (specifically the 'session' cookie) to arrive at the out-of-band collector listening on http://collector:9000/report?c=... on the shared docker network.
labs.flag_hint: The OOB collector container logs every /report?c=... request; when the value of c= matches the admin session cookie currently issued by the app, the app's /solve endpoint returns the flag string. The flag is also written to /flag.txt inside the collector container for direct exec inspection.
skills_taught: using an OOB channel for exfiltration
tech_stack: Jinja2 3.1 (autoescape disabled on the search template)
labs.inspired_by: the canonical PortSwigger 'Reflected XSS into HTML context' lab pattern, abstracted for local Docker use

labs.title: Stored XSS in Blog Comments
labs.description: A minimal Django blog stores comment bodies verbatim and renders them with the |safe filter. An administrator polls the moderation queue every 30 seconds to approve new comments and, in doing so, loads them fully rendered.
labs.objective: Post a comment whose payload exfiltrates the admin's csrftoken cookie value to http://collector:9000/report?t=<token>.
labs.flag_hint: The /solve endpoint on the app inspects the collector's request log via an internal socket; when the admin's currently-issued csrftoken value appears there, /solve returns the flag. The flag file /flag.txt is created inside the collector container the first time /solve succeeds.
labs.inspired_by: generic bulletin-board stored-XSS bug class seen in dozens of open-source CMS advisories

labs.title: DOM XSS via document.write(location.hash)
labs.description:
A static single-page marketing site reads location.hash on load and calls document.write('

Welcome ' + decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)) + '

') to personalise the greeting. No sanitisation is performed and the sink runs before the DOM has finished parsing.
labs.objective: Craft a URL whose #fragment causes the page, when opened by the admin bot, to fetch /flag.txt from the same origin and POST its body to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt is served from the app root but is only useful once the admin bot has fetched it and shipped the value to the OOB collector. /solve returns the completion flag when the collector has recorded the exact /flag.txt content.
labs.inspired_by: textbook DOM XSS pattern described in the DOM-XSS wiki and OWASP DOM-XSS cheat sheet

labs.title: Reflected XSS in a JavaScript String Literal
labs.description: A checkout page reflects the ?promo= value inside a single-quoted JS string in an inline <script> block: var promo = 'REFLECTED_HERE'; document.getElementById('promo').innerText = promo;. Angle brackets are stripped server-side but single quotes and backslashes pass through untouched.
labs.objective: Break out of the JS string context to execute code that fetches /api/whoami with credentials and POSTs the JSON body to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: The /solve endpoint checks the OOB collector for a POST whose body contains the exact JSON returned by /api/whoami for the admin session; on match it emits the flag.
skills_taught: breaking out of quotes without new tags
understanding why HTML-only filters fail in JS contexts
labs.inspired_by: very common promo-code / referrer-code reflection pattern found across e-commerce triage tickets

labs.title: DOM XSS via jQuery .html() on hashchange
labs.description: A tabbed dashboard uses jQuery 3.4.1. On every hashchange event it runs $('#panel').html(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1))). Modern innerHTML will not execute inline <script>, but event-handler attributes on freshly-parsed elements execute normally.
labs.objective: Deliver a hash payload that runs arbitrary JS in the admin bot's browser and exfiltrates document.cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector logs incoming requests; /solve compares captured cookie against the app's live admin session and returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: jQuery html() as a DOM sink
labs.inspired_by: generic legacy jQuery dashboard XSS pattern documented in DOM-XSS Wiki and Snyk advisories

labs.title: Filter Bypass Ladder — Blocked <script> Tags
labs.description: A Go-based support form single-pass strips the substrings '<script', '</script', 'javascript:', and 'onerror=' (case-insensitive) from ?subject= before echoing it into HTML. The single-pass replacement means recursive constructions survive, and the incomplete event-handler list leaves many vectors open. This lab expects the solver to climb multiple rungs of the bypass ladder.
labs.objective: Bypass the substring filter to execute JavaScript in the admin bot's context and exfiltrate the admin session cookie to http://collector:9000/report?c=.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 receives the cookie; /solve compares against the live admin cookie and prints the flag.
skills_taught: non-script event handlers such as ontoggle on <details>
labs.inspired_by: abstracted from dozens of HackerOne reports on naïve server-side blocklists (e.g. Shopify H1 #423876 pattern)

labs.title: Stored XSS via SVG Avatar Upload
labs.description: A Rails user-profile app accepts SVG avatars. It validates that the Content-Type is image/svg+xml and that the file begins with '<svg' but does not strip embedded <script> or event handlers. Uploaded avatars are served from the same origin under /avatars/<uuid>.svg with Content-Type: image/svg+xml, and the admin bot views your profile page (which embeds the avatar via <object>).
labs.objective: Upload a malicious SVG so that when the admin bot views your profile page the SVG script executes, fetches /admin/token, and POSTs the JSON body to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the token value posted to the OOB endpoint against the current /admin/token; on match returns the flag.
skills_taught: same-origin file uploads as an XSS vector
why images belong on a separate origin
labs.inspired_by: GitLab CVE-2023-5009 style SVG XSS patterns and multiple HackerOne SVG-upload writeups (Uber, Grammarly)

labs.title: Markdown Renderer — javascript: URI Filter Bypass
labs.description: A wiki uses markdown-it 13 with a custom link sanitiser that removes matches of /javascript:/gi from any href. The single-pass regex fails on unicode whitespace, HTML entities, and tab characters embedded in the scheme. The admin bot reviews new wiki pages and clicks the primary link in each page.
labs.objective: Post a wiki page whose rendered link, when clicked by the admin bot, executes JS and exfiltrates the admin's session cookie to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector captures cookie; /solve validates the value matches the current admin session and returns the flag.
skills_taught: javascript: URI variants (control chars, entities, unicode)
labs.inspired_by: GitLab wiki markdown XSS class of bugs (CVE-2022-2185 pattern) and Discourse markdown pipeline advisories

labs.title: postMessage XSS via startsWith Origin Check
labs.description: A chat-widget host page embeds an iframe from https://widget.chatco.internal and handles messages with if (e.origin.startsWith('https://widget.chatco.internal')) target.innerHTML = e.data.html. The lab ships a wildcard DNS resolver so the attacker can register look-alike hostnames such as widget.chatco.internal.evil.lab that satisfy the naive prefix check.
labs.objective: Register a look-alike host under the lab's wildcard DNS, host a page that embeds the target and postMessages an HTML payload; when the admin bot visits your attacker URL, exfiltrate document.cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives cookie; /solve returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: why startsWith on origin is broken
look-alike hostname registration to defeat prefix checks
tech_stack: Express 4 for both target and attacker vhosts
second nginx 1.27 vhost for the widget origin
labs.inspired_by: recurring postMessage bugs on major SaaS platforms 2022-2024 (Slack #H1-1234567 style, Grammarly, HackerOne #1073518)

labs.title: jQuery(location.hash) Selector-to-HTML Coercion
labs.description: A legacy help-centre scrolls to a section on load with $(location.hash). When jQuery < 3.5 is passed a string that looks like HTML it constructs elements instead of selecting them, thanks to htmlPrefilter regex quirks that also let payloads survive.
labs.objective: Craft a URL whose hash coerces jQuery into constructing a new element with an event handler that fires; use it to steal the admin's session cookie via the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve prints the flag when the value matches the current admin session cookie.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-11022 and CVE-2020-11023 (jQuery htmlPrefilter/regex regressions)

labs.title: Blind XSS in Admin User-Agent Log Viewer
labs.description: An operations admin console renders the raw User-Agent string of every request in an HTML table cell using Jinja's |safe filter. The admin visits the log panel every 60 seconds; the panel is protected behind auth so blind delivery is the only option.
labs.objective: Send an HTTP request whose User-Agent header contains a blind-XSS payload; when the admin next visits the log panel the payload must fetch /admin/apikey and POST the response to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the API key; /solve compares against the current /admin/apikey value and prints the flag on match.
skills_taught: HTTP header injection as a stored sink
chaining blind XSS to authenticated internal API reads
tech_stack: Jinja2 3.1 with |safe on the log-cell template
labs.inspired_by: XSSHunter methodology (Matt Bryant) and countless admin-panel blind-XSS writeups on HackerOne 2020-2024

labs.title: Self-XSS Chained via CSRF
labs.description: A Laravel profile-bio field is stored HTML-escaped for other viewers but rendered raw when the owning user views their own profile — the classic self-XSS shrug. The profile-update endpoint accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded and has no CSRF token because 'it's a low-severity self-XSS anyway'.
labs.objective: Host an attacker page that CSRF-submits a malicious bio for the admin account; when the admin bot next visits its own profile, the self-XSS executes and exfiltrates the admin's session cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve returns the flag when the captured value matches the live admin cookie.
skills_taught: chaining separate low-severity bugs into critical impact
labs.inspired_by: recurring 'we downgraded self-XSS then it became RCE' HackerOne narratives (e.g. Frans Rosén's writeups)

labs.title: HTML5 formaction Attribute Injection
labs.description: A CMS lets you insert one <button> inside an existing <form> that has no action attribute (submitting to the current URL by default). The sanitiser allows <button> with a formaction attribute — a HTML5 override that changes the form's submit target.
labs.objective: Use a formaction-bearing <button> to redirect the admin's next form submission to your attacker origin; capture the POST body (which includes the CSRF token and edited-page content) at the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 receives the POST body; /solve returns the flag when the current admin CSRF token value appears in a captured POST.
skills_taught: sanitiser allowlists that miss attribute semantics
exfil via form redirect (no JS required)
labs.inspired_by: Michal Bentkowski / Cure53 formaction research and the DOMPurify hooks documentation examples

labs.title: iframe srcdoc Attribute Injection Bypass
labs.description: A rich-post renderer using Bleach with a misconfigured allowlist permits <iframe> with the srcdoc attribute. The sanitiser inspects iframe children but forgets that srcdoc is itself an HTML/JS document parsed in an inherited-origin about:srcdoc context.
labs.objective: Post content that produces an <iframe srcdoc='...'> whose inner document runs script and exfiltrates the admin's document.cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve prints the flag on match.
tech_stack: Bleach 6 with iframe + srcdoc in allowed_attributes
labs.inspired_by: Bleach and DOMPurify configuration pitfalls documented in the Mozilla and Cure53 advisories 2022-2024

labs.title: BBCode [img] Attribute Smuggling
labs.description: A vintage-forum-inspired app renders [img]URL[/img] as . The URL is not attribute-encoded, so a URL containing a double quote breaks out into new HTML attributes such as onerror.
labs.objective: Post a topic whose rendered tag carries an onerror handler that exfiltrates the admin's session cookie to http://collector:9000/report when the admin bot loads the topic list.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector; /solve returns the flag when the cookie matches the current admin session.
skills_taught: why URL contexts need distinct attribute encoding
labs.inspired_by: long history of BBCode parser bugs in vBulletin, phpBB and MyBB forks (multiple CVEs 2019-2023)

labs.title: Mutation XSS via HTML Namespace Confusion
labs.description: Comments are sanitised server-side with sanitize-html, then serialised into JSON, then re-parsed on the client via elem.innerHTML = safeHTML. HTML namespace confusion between svg, math and foreignObject means the second parse produces a different tree than the first, resurrecting script-executing constructs the sanitiser thought it had eliminated.
labs.objective: Post a comment that survives the server-side sanitiser but executes JavaScript after the client re-parses it, then exfiltrate the admin cookie.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve returns the flag on match.
tech_stack: client renderer that writes safe HTML via innerHTML
labs.inspired_by: Mario Heiderich mXSS papers (2013) and Masato Kinugawa / Michał Bentkowski follow-on mXSS research 2020-2024

labs.title: DOMPurify Bypass via Nested Form Elements
labs.description: A Next.js commenting feature sanitises user HTML with a specific pinned DOMPurify version vulnerable to a documented namespace/nesting bypass. Sanitised output is stored and re-rendered on the admin's dashboard.
labs.objective: Craft input that survives DOMPurify's parse-serialise-parse cycle to execute JavaScript in the admin's context and read /internal/secret, then post the response body to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the /internal/secret body; /solve compares against the live value and returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: reading DOMPurify changelogs for hint patterns
identifying which sanitiser version is deployed
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-45801 and the Kevin Mizu / SonarSource 2024 DOMPurify bypass writeups

labs.title: CSP Bypass via JSONP Endpoint in Allowlist
labs.description: The app enforces script-src 'self' https://accounts.trusted.lab. The trusted host exposes /api/jsonp?callback=... which echoes the callback name into a JS function invocation. A reflected HTML injection exists on the target but 'unsafe-inline' is not permitted; the CSP only allows scripts loaded from allowlisted hosts.
labs.objective: Combine the HTML injection with the trusted-host JSONP callback abuse to execute arbitrary JavaScript under the app's CSP and exfiltrate the admin's session cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: hunting JSONP endpoints inside allowlisted third parties
tech_stack: Node 20 + Express 4 mock trusted-host on second nginx 1.27 vhost
labs.inspired_by: Michele Spagnuolo / Lukas Weichselbaum 'CSP Is Dead, Long Live CSP' (2016) research and its 2022-2024 replays against GitHub / Salesforce

labs.title: CSP Bypass via Missing base-uri Directive
labs.description: The app's CSP restricts script-src to 'self' but omits base-uri. A single-tag HTML injection is available inside <head>. Every legitimate script on the page is loaded via a relative path such as /assets/main.js.
labs.objective: Inject a <base href='//attacker.lab'> so that when the admin bot next loads a legitimate page, the relative-path script is fetched from the attacker origin under a URL that satisfies the same policy; hijack script execution and exfiltrate the admin cookie.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: relative URL script hijacking under CSP
minimising markup injections to a single tag
tech_stack: second attacker origin served by nginx 1.27
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger research on base-uri and Google Bughunter University CSP allowlist articles

labs.title: AngularJS 1.7.2 Sandbox Escape (Client-Side Template Injection)
labs.description:
A checkout confirmation page uses AngularJS 1.7.2 and interpolates a query parameter as an ng-bind expression:
{{name}}
. AngularJS 1.7 removed the sandbox and famously exposes constructor-based gadgets even in earlier versions.
labs.objective: Deliver a URL that, when opened by the admin bot, escapes the AngularJS expression sandbox and exfiltrates the admin's cookie to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve prints the flag on match.
skills_taught: why the AngularJS team abandoned the sandbox
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger's AngularJS sandbox-escape series by Gareth Heyes and Mario Heiderich (2015-2018)

labs.title: Vue 2 Template Injection via Runtime Vue.compile
labs.description: A Nuxt 2 dashboard uses v-html for one field (sanitised) and Vue.compile() at runtime on another field so that customers can supply custom templates for a widget. The compile-time surface accepts full Vue expressions.
labs.objective: Deliver content that triggers Vue.compile on user input, executes a template expression, and POSTs the /me API response to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the /me body; /solve returns the flag when the admin's /me content is received.
skills_taught: difference between v-html and runtime template compilation
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-6783 (Vue 2 template-compiler XSS) and PortSwigger's Vue.js CSTI research

labs.title: CSS Injection — Exfiltrating a CSRF Token via Attribute Selectors
labs.description: A newsletter-preview page accepts arbitrary user-supplied stylesheets via <link rel=stylesheet href=...> whose href passes a permissive sanitiser. Inline scripts and other tags are blocked by a strict CSP. A hidden <input name='csrf' value='...'> lives in the same document.
labs.objective: Using only CSS attribute selectors and background-image callbacks, exfiltrate the admin's CSRF token character-by-character to the OOB collector; then submit a state-changing request bearing the leaked token so the checker validates the completed chain.
labs.flag_hint: /solve requires a POST to /admin/action containing the leaked CSRF token; only after that POST succeeds does /solve return the flag.
skills_taught: bootstrapping a chain from a leaked secret
labs.inspired_by: Pepe Vila / Sebastian Lekies scriptless-attack research and the HackerOne 'CSS Injection Primitives' 2023 writeup

labs.title: Dangling Markup — Stealing a CSRF Token Without Executing JS
labs.description: The app strips angle brackets from every user input but you can inject inside an existing HTML attribute (a URL context) that precedes a hidden CSRF token further down the DOM. The template renders unquoted attributes in one branch. Strict CSP blocks all inline and remote scripts.
labs.objective: Inject dangling markup that causes the browser to include the trailing DOM (containing the CSRF token) inside a resource URL sent to the OOB collector.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the token; /solve returns the flag when the value matches the current admin CSRF token.
skills_taught: recognising when JS is not required
using resource fetches as an exfil channel
tech_stack: html/template with inconsistent quoting on one attribute
labs.inspired_by: Michał Zalewski dangling-markup research and Krzysztof Kotowicz's 'Reverse Tabnabbing / dangling markup' 2016 talk

labs.title: Elite Chain: Content-Type Sniffing + Stored HTML + CSP Nonce Leak
labs.description: Three sub-primitives compose the exploit: (a) the file-upload endpoint returns text files with Content-Type: text/plain and without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a path-normalisation quirk lets the file be fetched under a route that omits the plain header; (b) the main app enforces strict CSP with per-request nonces but a separate profile page reflects the nonce inside a comment-like construct that leaks via dangling markup; (c) once the nonce is known, a nonce-bearing <script> can be injected into a stored HTML fragment.
labs.objective: Read /internal/keystore (admin-only) and POST its exact JSON body to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares the collected keystore body against the live /internal/keystore response; on match returns the flag and writes it to /flag.txt inside the collector container.
skills_taught: CSP nonce reuse and leakage patterns
multi-page exploit orchestration on an attacker page
tech_stack: strict CSP with per-request nonce middleware
labs.inspired_by: Cure53 pentest report patterns and Michał Zalewski's classic MIME-sniffing writeups combined with 2023 nonce-leak advisories

labs.title: Elite Chain: Self-XSS + CSRF + Blind XSS in Admin Console
labs.description: A helpdesk app carries three composable low-severity bugs: (a) a self-XSS in the user's own notes field, (b) an unauthenticated CSRF on user-note update, and (c) a blind XSS in the admin console when it renders any user's notes. Each in isolation is triage-closed as informational; composed, they achieve admin session compromise.
labs.objective: From an unauthenticated attacker page, CSRF a victim user's browser into saving a malicious note that self-XSSes and then submits a support ticket whose payload lodges into an admin-visible field; when the admin next opens the queue the blind XSS fires and exfiltrates the admin session cookie to http://collector:9000/report.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 must record all three chain stages (marked by unique tags in the payload); /solve returns the flag only when the admin cookie value appears in a stage-3 capture.
skills_taught: chaining low-severity bugs into critical impact
orchestrating multi-hop payloads across user roles
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne 'One Little Bug' style chained-XSS writeups and Frans Rosén's 'Account hijacking using dirty dancing' 2022 research

labs.title: Elite Chain: HTTP Header Injection → Cache Poisoning → Mass XSS
labs.description: A Varnish CDN in front of the app caches by URL + Accept-Language. The origin reflects the X-Forwarded-Host header into a <link rel='canonical'> without escaping. By poisoning the cache with a malicious canonical link that also embeds a script vector, every subsequent visitor to /home — including the admin bot — is served attacker HTML.
labs.objective: Poison the /home cache such that when the admin bot fetches /home its browser executes attacker JavaScript and exfiltrates the admin session cookie to http://collector:9000/report with a Referer pointing at the poisoned /home path.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the cookie; /solve returns the flag only when the capturing request's Referer indicates the poisoned /home path (proving the vector was through the cache, not a direct URL).
skills_taught: chaining infrastructure-level bugs to client-side XSS
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle / PortSwigger 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' (2018) and its 2022-2024 follow-on research on unkeyed headers

labs.title: Username Enumeration via Timing and Verbose Errors
labs.description: A login form returns two different error strings ("unknown account" vs "wrong password") and also runs a full bcrypt(cost=12) hash comparison only when the account exists, leaking a ~380 ms timing side channel on top of the response oracle. A wordlist of 50 candidate usernames is bundled in /challenge/users.txt inside the container; three of them are real and one is the admin.
labs.objective: Identify the three real usernames from /challenge/users.txt using response text and/or response timing, then POST them as JSON body {"valid":["u1","u2","u3"]} to http://target/solve to retrieve the flag.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint POST /solve compares the submitted set against the seeded valid set and returns the flag string in the JSON response only on exact match.
labs.inspired_by: OWASP WSTG-IDNT-04 and the classic Django/Rails contact-form enumeration pattern surfaced in recurring HackerOne P4 reports 2022-2024

labs.title: Password Reset with Guessable Token and No Rate Limit
labs.description: The forgot-password flow issues a 6-digit numeric token derived from int(time.time()) modulo 1e6 and emails it via a bundled Mailhog. The /reset endpoint has no rate limit, no attempt cap, and no per-token binding to the requester's IP or session.
labs.objective: Trigger a reset for admin@lab.local, brute-force the numeric token against /reset (or predict it from the request timestamp), set the password to PwnedByYou!, log in, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: The flag lives in /flag.txt inside the container. GET /admin/flag reads and returns it when the caller's session is authenticated as the admin user.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger Academy "password reset broken logic" pattern plus recurring 2023 disclosure.com writeups on time-seeded reset tokens

labs.title: JWT alg=none Accepted for Backward Compatibility
labs.description: A profile API validates JWTs with jsonwebtoken 8.5.x invoked without an explicit algorithms allowlist, so tokens whose header sets alg to none (and any casing variant such as NoNe) are accepted with an empty signature. A valid low-privilege JWT is issued at login and printed to the response.
labs.objective: Strip the signature and rewrite the header to alg:none, promote the payload role claim to admin, then GET /admin/flag with the tampered token in the Authorization header.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the decoded token's sub is admin and role is admin, regardless of signature.
labs.inspired_by: The 2015 Auth0 alg=none disclosure, kept relevant by CVE-2022-23529 (jsonwebtoken RCE) and the 2024 wave of npm audit reports on ancient jsonwebtoken pins

labs.title: Two-Factor Check Enforced Only in the SPA
labs.description: A Vue 3 SPA gates the /vault route behind a TOTP prompt, but the server-side endpoint /api/vault only checks a boolean twofa_verified flag on the session that is flipped to true by any POST to /api/2fa/verify regardless of the code submitted. The lab hands you valid password credentials for user alice.
labs.objective: Authenticate as alice with the provided password, POST any body to /api/2fa/verify to satisfy the server-side flag, then GET /api/vault to retrieve the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /api/vault returns the flag in the JSON body when the session has authenticated=true and twofa_verified=true; both are set purely by server endpoints that do no real verification.
skills_taught: direct API invocation bypassing SPA UI
labs.inspired_by: The recurring 2FA-in-JS-only pattern documented in PentesterLab's Serialize section and echoed by several 2023 Grab and Shopify hacktivity reports

labs.title: Server-Side Session Never Invalidated on Logout
labs.description: Django's LogoutView is overridden to only delete the cookie in the response but leave the server-side session row alive in the database. A debug endpoint /debug/last-session (left in during a fake staging cutover) returns the most recent session id for demonstration purposes.
labs.objective: Read the most recent admin session id from /debug/last-session, wait for the seeded bot to hit /accounts/logout, then replay the captured sessionid cookie against /vault/flag to receive the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /vault/flag returns the flag when the request carries a valid sessionid cookie bound to the admin user, regardless of whether the corresponding browser has "logged out".
skills_taught: distinction between client cookie clearing and server session revocation
labs.inspired_by: OWASP ASVS 3.3.1 and repeated 2022-2024 bug bounty writeups where SPA logouts orphaned server sessions (e.g., recurring Shopify Partner API reports)

labs.title: JWT with Weak HMAC Secret Crackable Offline
labs.description: A Go API signs session JWTs with HS256 and the secret "banana2024!" which appears in the top-500 of the SecLists 2023 leaked-passwords wordlist. Any valid token can be captured from a normal login. The API validates only HS256 tokens signed with that secret.
labs.objective: Log in as the low-privilege user seeded in the README, capture the JWT, crack the secret offline with hashcat mode 16500 (or jwt_tool), forge a JWT with role=admin, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the token verifies under the app's HMAC secret and the payload's role claim equals admin.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger "JWT weak secret" lab family and the July 2023 rash of HackerOne triage reports against Go microservices leaking short JWT_SECRET env values

labs.title: Login Rate Limiter Keyed on X-Forwarded-For
labs.description: A FastAPI login endpoint sits behind nginx which sets the client key from the first entry of the X-Forwarded-For header without validating it against a trusted proxy allowlist. The lockout is 5 failed attempts per key per hour. The victim account alice uses a 4-digit PIN.
labs.objective: Brute-force alice's 4-digit PIN by rotating a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header across each attempt, then POST the winning credential pair to /solve to receive the flag.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with valid alice credentials returns the flag; the endpoint verifies session state established by the successful login.
labs.inspired_by: Numerous 2022-2024 Bugcrowd disclosures against Cloudflare-fronted apps that keyed rate limiters on unvalidated XFF, plus the 2023 Detectify write-up on Rails::Attack throttles

labs.title: Password Reset Link Built From Host Header
labs.description: The reset endpoint builds the reset URL by concatenating request.headers.host with a random token. An automated Puppeteer bot inside the container polls Mailhog for reset emails addressed to victim@lab.local and clicks the link every 20 s. A collector service listens on http://collector:9000.
labs.objective: Trigger a reset for victim@lab.local with Host header set to collector:9000, wait for the bot to click the poisoned URL, capture the token from collector logs, reset victim's password, log in, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when authenticated as victim (who holds admin role) using the freshly reset password.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle's 2013 host-header injection research, refreshed by the 2022 Django CVE-2022-41323 and multiple 2023-2024 SaaS reset-link poisoning HackerOne reports

labs.title: Session ID Not Rotated on Login
labs.description: A Symfony app sets a PHPSESSID cookie on first visit and reuses the same identifier after login. The app additionally honors a ?PHPSESSID= query parameter for legacy support, letting an attacker prime an id on the victim's browser via a crafted link. A Puppeteer bot seeded as admin polls a public message board and clicks any absolute URL posted there.
labs.objective: Post a URL to /board/new that primes a chosen PHPSESSID on the admin bot, wait for the bot to log in, then reuse that same PHPSESSID from your own client to GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag whenever the caller's PHPSESSID cookie is bound server-side to the admin account.
labs.inspired_by: The evergreen OWASP Session Fixation pattern plus the 2022 Adobe Magento CVE-2022-24086-adjacent session handling reports

labs.title: Remember-Me Cookie With Predictable Structure
labs.description: A Rails 7.1 app issues a remember_me cookie of the form base64(sha1(user_id + ":" + short_secret + ":" + yyyy-mm-dd)). The 8-character short_secret is exposed via a debug /rails/info/routes-style leak reachable at /_debug/env. The lab gives you a low-privilege account whose cookie you can capture through normal login.
labs.objective: Recover short_secret from /_debug/env, forge a remember_me cookie for user_id 1 (the admin), set it in your browser, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the app auto-logs the request in as user_id 1 via the forged remember-me cookie.
labs.inspired_by: The 2010 Django persistent-cookie disclosure and the 2023 GitHub Advisory on Devise plaintext remember tokens

labs.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion: HS256 Verified With RS256 Public Key
labs.description: A Spring Boot API validates JWTs with jjwt 0.9 configured to accept whatever algorithm the token declares. The RS256 public key is served publicly at /.well-known/jwks.json. An HS256 token whose HMAC secret equals the DER-encoded public key bytes verifies successfully as if signed by the private key holder.
labs.objective: Fetch the RS256 public key from the JWKS endpoint, sign an HS256 token whose payload sets sub=admin using the exact PEM bytes as the HMAC secret, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the verified JWT payload's sub equals admin.
skills_taught: PEM byte-exact secret construction with jwt_tool
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger's 2022 "JWT algorithm confusion" research and CVE-2022-21449 style asymmetric key trust bugs recurring in Java shops

labs.title: JWT kid Header Used as File Path for HMAC Key
labs.description: A Flask API loads its HMAC secret from disk using the token's kid header as a relative path: open(f"/app/keys/{kid}").read(). Traversal is not filtered, so pointing kid at a file with predictable contents (or /dev/null for an empty key) lets an attacker choose the secret used for verification.
labs.objective: Forge a token with kid=../../../../dev/null, sign with the empty string as the HMAC secret, set the payload role to admin, GET /admin/read?f=/flag.txt to read the flag file.
labs.flag_hint: The flag lives at /flag.txt inside the container. GET /admin/read?f=/flag.txt returns file contents when the caller's JWT verifies and role=admin.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger Academy's kid header lab and CVE-2019-7644 (samlify) family of key-loader path bugs

labs.title: OAuth redirect_uri Validated With startsWith
labs.description: A mock OAuth provider validates redirect_uri by checking whether the submitted value startsWith the registered value https://client.lab.local/callback. Both https://client.lab.local/callback.attacker.lab and https://client.lab.local/callback/../@attacker.lab satisfy that check. The provider issues authorization codes in the redirect and the client exchanges them for tokens.
labs.objective: Craft an authorize URL whose redirect_uri smuggles the code to http://attacker.lab:9000/log, wait for the seeded admin bot to click the login link on the noticeboard, capture the code from attacker.lab logs, exchange it at the token endpoint, and GET /me/admin.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me/admin on the client returns the flag when the presented access token belongs to the admin user.
labs.inspired_by: Salt Security's February 2023 "Sign in with Google" research on Booking.com and the recurring Detectify OAuth redirect writeups

labs.title: TOTP Backup Codes Brute-Forceable, No Lockout
labs.description: django-otp is configured with 6-digit numeric backup codes. The primary TOTP endpoint enforces a 5-attempt lockout, but the /2fa/backup fallback endpoint has no throttling and no per-user attempt counter. Alice's password is given; her 2FA secret is not.
labs.objective: Log in as alice with her password, then brute-force the 6-digit backup code at /2fa/backup, complete authentication, and GET /vault/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /vault/flag returns the flag when the session belongs to alice and the OTP challenge has been marked satisfied via a valid backup code.
labs.inspired_by: The 2023 recurring HackerOne pattern against Slack-style backup-code endpoints and the November 2023 GitHub Advisory on django-two-factor-auth throttling gaps

labs.title: Email Change TOCTOU Race Enables Admin Hijack
labs.description: The change-email flow performs three non-transactional steps: uniqueness check, verification-token issuance, and, after the token is clicked, commit of the new email to the user row. Racing two verification clicks lets an attacker's account bind to admin@lab.local. Once bound, the standard forgot-password flow delivers admin's reset token to the attacker.
labs.objective: Register an attacker account, kick off a change-email to attacker+temp@lab.local, then race a second change-email to admin@lab.local and click both verification links so the DB write orders as attacker.email=admin@lab.local; trigger password reset for admin, complete it, log in, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the session is authenticated as user_id=1 (the seeded admin) with the freshly reset password.
labs.inspired_by: The July 2023 GitLab email-change race disclosure and multiple Salesforce Community Cloud takeover reports 2022-2024

labs.title: OAuth Account Linking Without state Parameter
labs.description: The app supports "Link Google account" for logged-in users but omits the state parameter and does not bind the callback to the initiating session. An attacker who begins an OAuth flow, pauses at the callback URL with their code, and lures the admin to visit that callback link will have their Google identity linked to the admin's account, after which "Sign in with Google" as attacker lands as admin.
labs.objective: Start a Google-linking flow with your attacker Google identity, deliver the callback URL to the admin bot via /board/new, then log in via Google and reach /admin/flag as admin.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the OAuth-driven login lands the session on the admin account.
skills_taught: state parameter role in CSRF defense
labs.inspired_by: Egor Homakov's 2013 GitHub OAuth CSRF research, refreshed by the 2023 Descope disclosures on account linking gaps in AAD-integrated SaaS

labs.title: JWT jku Header Points to Attacker-Controlled JWKS
labs.description: A resource server dereferences the jku header URL to fetch signing keys without allowlisting the host. The container ships an attacker HTTP server on attacker.lab:80 that serves any JWKS document you write into /www.
labs.objective: Generate an RSA keypair, publish the JWK on attacker.lab, forge an RS256 token whose header sets jku to http://attacker.lab/jwks.json and whose payload sets role=admin, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the token's signature verifies against a key retrieved from the jku URL and role=admin.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger's 2022 JKU labs and Snyk's 2024 disclosure round on Node JOSE libraries accepting unbounded jku hosts

labs.title: JWT Verifier Trusts Embedded jwk Header
labs.description: A FastAPI service uses python-jose in a code path that, if the token header contains a jwk claim, uses that key to verify the signature. No comparison is made against a trusted JWKS.
labs.objective: Generate a keypair, embed the public JWK in the token header, sign with the matching private key, set the payload sub to admin, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the token's embedded jwk verifies the signature and sub equals admin.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-29217 (PyJWT) and the follow-on 2023 advisories showing embedded-JWK trust re-emerging in wrappers around python-jose

labs.title: SQL Injection Through JWT kid Parameter
labs.description: A PHP resource server resolves the HMAC secret via a raw query: SELECT secret FROM signing_keys WHERE kid = '<kid>'. The kid string comes straight from the token header. Union-based injection lets the attacker make the query return an attacker-chosen secret, with which they then sign a forged token.
labs.objective: Inject a UNION SELECT in kid to have the lookup return the constant "attacker_secret", sign a fresh HS256 token with that string as the secret, set role=admin, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the token verifies under the secret returned by the (injected) SQL query and role=admin.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger's "JWT kid header SQL injection" research and multiple 2023 HackerOne submissions against custom Node key-resolver middleware

labs.title: Public OAuth Client Downgrades PKCE to None
labs.description: A mobile-style public client is registered with method=S256 required, but the token endpoint treats absent code_verifier as "PKCE not in use" and issues tokens anyway. An attacker who intercepts an authorization code (leaked through a poisoned redirect on a companion lab, or supplied via a sibling capture endpoint here) exchanges it without knowing the verifier.
labs.objective: Capture the seeded victim's authorization code from /capture/last-code, POST it to /oauth/token with no code_verifier field, obtain an access token, and GET /me/admin.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me/admin returns the flag when the presented access token maps to the admin user.
labs.inspired_by: RFC 9700 (OAuth 2.0 Security BCP, 2024) and Google VRP 2023 disclosures on Android PKCE downgrade in third-party OIDC brokers

labs.title: OIDC id_token With Unchecked aud and Replayed nonce
labs.description: A relying party accepts any id_token issued by the trusted IdP without verifying that aud equals its own client_id and without validating nonce against the value it originally sent. An attacker who controls a second registered client on the same IdP obtains an id_token containing sub=admin@lab.local (issued to the attacker's client) and replays it against the target RP.
labs.objective: Register an attacker client at the mock IdP, drive an OIDC flow as admin@lab.local through that client (using seeded lab helpers), then POST the resulting id_token to the victim RP's /oidc/token-login endpoint and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the RP's session is authenticated as admin@lab.local via the accepted (cross-audience) id_token.
labs.inspired_by: The 2023 Silverfort research on OIDC audience confusion and the 2024 Ping Identity CVE-2024-27295 advisory on inconsistent id_token validation

labs.title: SAML Assertion Signature Wrapping (XSW1-XSW8)
labs.description: A python3-saml consumer verifies the XML signature by resolving the Reference URI, then extracts the NameID by walking a different XPath. Wrapping the signed assertion inside an outer assertion whose NameID is admin yields a document that passes verification while presenting admin to the application.
labs.objective: Capture a legitimate signed SAMLResponse from the seeded IdP login, transform it into an XSW1 (or any of XSW2-XSW8) variant with NameID admin, POST it to /sso/acs, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the SP session is authenticated as admin.
skills_taught: XPath extraction vs Reference URI resolution
labs.inspired_by: Somorovsky et al. XSW research and CVE-2024-22024 (Ivanti SAML) which re-exposed the family in 2024 enterprise gateways

labs.title: SAML NameID Hijack via XML Comment Truncation
labs.description: A ruby-saml consumer pinned to a pre-CVE-2024-45409 release canonicalizes the document for signature check but extracts the NameID by concatenating text nodes only up to the first XML comment. Injecting <NameID>admin<!---->@attacker.lab</NameID> passes the signature (because the IdP signs the whole element) while resolving to admin on the SP.
labs.objective: Obtain a signed SAMLResponse for an attacker-controlled email admin<!---->@attacker.lab, post it to /saml/consume, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the SP session's NameID equals admin.
labs.inspired_by: Duo Security's CVE-2017-11428 disclosure, refreshed by CVE-2024-45409 (ruby-saml, September 2024) which re-broke the same class in the wild

labs.title: WebAuthn rpId Downgrade Across Subdomains
labs.description: A @simplewebauthn/server 10 deployment sets rpId to the eTLD+1 lab.local and does not restrict where credentials may be created. An attacker who owns attacker.lab.local can register a passkey with rpId lab.local and later assert it against victim.lab.local's /login/passkey endpoint, matching the seeded admin's credential id via account-linking replay.
labs.objective: Register a passkey on attacker.lab.local with rpId lab.local, chain it via the seeded credential-linking endpoint so it becomes attached to the admin account, authenticate against victim.lab.local, and GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the passkey assertion authenticates the session as the admin user on victim.lab.local.
labs.inspired_by: The 2023 W3C WebAuthn WG discussion on rpId scoping and Cloudflare's 2024 write-up on passkey RP misconfiguration

labs.title: nOAuth-Style Account Takeover via Mutable Email Claim
labs.description: Multi-step chain: the mock IdP lets tenant admins set any email on their user (mutable, unverified). The target SaaS accepts Sign in with the IdP and matches accounts by email claim alone. The attacker registers an attacker tenant at the mock IdP, sets the attacker user's email to admin@lab.local, initiates OIDC to the SaaS, and lands as admin. To retrieve the flag, the attacker must then rotate the admin's downstream API token and use it against the internal microservice /internal/flag which enforces its own JWT scope check.
labs.objective: Take over admin@lab.local on the SaaS via nOAuth email hijack, log in, POST /api/rotate-token to mint a new admin API token, then present it to the internal microservice and GET /internal/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /internal/flag on the internal microservice returns the flag when the presented bearer token has scope admin:read.
labs.inspired_by: nOAuth by Descope (June 2023), the Microsoft Entra ID cross-tenant vulnerability affecting apps that trusted the mutable email claim from AAD id_tokens

labs.title: JKU URL-Parser Confusion Chains Into Cross-Service Admin
labs.description: Multi-step chain: service-a validates jku URLs by checking url.Host against an allowlist of trusted.lab but uses Go's net/url which parses userinfo permissively, so http://trusted.lab@attacker.lab/jwks.json reports Host trusted.lab while fetch actually hits attacker.lab. The attacker poisons the JWKS, forges a token accepted by service-a, and observes that service-b (behind an internal ingress) shares the same issuer and reuses tokens signed by any key present in the shared JWKS cache. Priming the cache from service-a lets the attacker replay the token to service-b's /internal/flag.
labs.objective: Poison the JWKS cache via jku URL-parser confusion on service-a, forge an admin token, replay it against service-b, and GET /internal/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /internal/flag on service-b returns the flag when the presented token verifies against a key currently in the shared JWKS cache and role=admin.
skills_taught: URL parser semantics as a security boundary
labs.inspired_by: Snyk's 2024 disclosures on Node/Go URL parser mismatches, the CVE-2023-42282 (ip package) class of parser-confusion bugs, and PortSwigger's JKU research

labs.title: SAML XSLT Canonicalization Chained With IdP-Initiated CSRF
labs.description: Multi-step chain: the SP uses OpenSAML 4.3 with an unsafe XSLT-based transform allowed inside the SignedInfo, so an attacker can craft a Transform that outputs different bytes than the parsed assertion (assertion says NameID=attacker; XSLT-derived signature input says NameID=attacker to make the signature verify against a legitimately signed base). The SP additionally accepts unsolicited IdP-initiated responses with no RelayState binding. Combining the two, the attacker forges an admin assertion, submits it unsolicited to /sso/acs, gains an admin session, and pivots to the internal /admin/rotate-secret endpoint to unlock /admin/flag.
labs.objective: Forge a SAMLResponse whose signature verifies under XSLT-c14n divergence with NameID admin, POST it unsolicited to /sso/acs, use the resulting admin session to POST /admin/rotate-secret, then GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns the flag when the admin session has completed the rotate-secret step within the same session window.
labs.inspired_by: Mainka and Somorovsky's XML Signature Wrapping and XSLT canonicalization research, the CVE-2024-45409 ruby-saml family (2024), and CVE-2024-22024 Ivanti SAML abuse in the wild

labs.title: First Contact: Basic Outbound SSRF
labs.description: A tiny 'link preview' service accepts any URL in a ?url= parameter and returns the response body verbatim. There is no allowlist, no scheme filter, and no host check. Inside the same Docker network runs an unauthenticated internal admin service on http://internal:8080/ that exposes /flag. The task teaches the fundamental SSRF primitive: the server's HTTP client sees a different network than the attacker's browser.
labs.objective: Use the /preview?url= endpoint on port 8000 to fetch http://internal:8080/flag from the internal Docker network and read the returned flag.
labs.flag_hint: Static flag file baked into the internal service at /app/flag.txt served by GET /flag; the flag is the response body, matched by regex FLAG\{[a-z0-9_]+\} by a bundled checker.sh.
skills_taught: reading response body from a fetcher
labs.inspired_by: Generic link-preview SSRF pattern seen across dozens of HackerOne reports (introductory)

labs.title: Loopback in Disguise: Bypassing a Naive 127.0.0.1 Blocklist
labs.description: The image-loader endpoint blocks any URL whose hostname string equals 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1'. The validator uses simple string equality on urlparse().hostname. Learners discover that 127.1, 127.0.1, 0x7f000001, 2130706433, and [::1] all resolve to the loopback interface, and that Python's socket layer happily accepts them.
labs.objective: Fetch http://<loopback-variant>/admin/flag from the /load-image?src= endpoint on port 8080 using at least one non-'127.0.0.1' loopback representation and read the flag from the response.
labs.flag_hint: Flag served at http://127.0.0.1:5000/admin/flag inside the container (bound only to lo); checker.sh inspects the last-response.json log written by the app and looks for the FLAG token being returned to the client.
labs.inspired_by: Repeated pattern in bug-bounty reports where allowlists check only literal 127.0.0.1 (introductory)

labs.title: Metadata Heist: Stealing IAM Credentials via IMDSv1
labs.description: A screenshot service running 'inside AWS' (a mock IMDS server on 169.254.169.254 provided by a sidecar container) allows an unauthenticated URL fetch. IMDSv1 is enabled, so a plain GET reveals the instance role and temporary credentials. Learners walk the metadata tree: /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ then /<role-name>.
labs.objective: Fetch http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/webapp-role via the /screenshot?url= endpoint on port 8000 and submit the returned SessionToken value to POST /solve to unlock the flag.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP checker endpoint /solve on the main app validates the submitted SessionToken against the mock IMDS's currently issued token; on match it returns the flag from FLAG env var.
labs.inspired_by: Capital One breach (2019) — the canonical IMDSv1 SSRF (educational reproduction)

labs.title: Wrong Scheme, Right Answer: file:// LFI via URL Fetcher
labs.description: A PDF-download 'proxy' uses Python's urllib.request.urlopen() with no scheme allowlist. The fetcher happily handles file:// URLs, letting learners read arbitrary files from the container filesystem. The flag is not web-served — it lives on disk at /flag.txt with mode 0644.
labs.objective: Use the /download?url= endpoint on port 8000 with a file:// URL to read /flag.txt from the container and return the FLAG token.
labs.flag_hint: Static file /flag.txt in the container root; solving is verified by the shipped checker.sh which does 'curl -s localhost:8000/download?url=file:///flag.txt | grep -Eo FLAG\{...\}'.
skills_taught: difference between HTTP client and generic URL opener
path-based file reads without directory traversal
labs.inspired_by: Recurring finding in Python microservices; abstract pattern (introductory)

labs.title: Silent Fetcher: Confirming Blind SSRF with Out-of-Band DNS
labs.description: A webhook-registration form fetches the submitted URL server-side but discards the response and only shows 'Webhook registered'. Learners must confirm the SSRF exists using an out-of-band collaborator: a bundled 'oob.local' DNS+HTTP server on port 9000 that logs any DNS lookup or HTTP hit under a unique subdomain. The lab teaches OOB confirmation without any response feedback.
labs.objective: Trigger a DNS lookup for <yourtoken>.oob.local from the webhook fetcher and then POST that token to /solve on port 8000 to receive the flag.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint /solve on the app checks the OOB server's SQLite log (shared volume) for a matching subdomain hit in the last 60 seconds; on match returns the flag.
skills_taught: why blind SSRF is still exploitable
labs.inspired_by: Burp Collaborator and interact.sh operating model (educational, self-hosted equivalent)

labs.title: The @ Trick: Parser Confusion Between Validator and Fetcher
labs.description: The app validates URLs with a hand-rolled regex that checks the first hostname it finds is 'trusted.com'. It then hands the raw string to Go's net/http, which honors the userinfo form user:pass@realhost. The classic http://trusted.com@internal:8080/flag bypass applies. Ladder rung 1 of the parser-confusion series.
labs.objective: Bypass the allowlist check on /fetch?url= (port 8000) using userinfo trickery to reach http://internal:8080/flag and print the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag served by the internal service at http://internal:8080/flag; checker.sh greps FLAG from the response body returned by /fetch.
skills_taught: difference between validator and fetcher parsers
labs.inspired_by: Orange Tsai's 'A New Era of SSRF' talk (Black Hat USA 2017), evergreen pattern

labs.title: Fragment Games: # and // Parser Splits
