labs.flag_hint: User(id: 'User:1337').secretNote contains the flag once 2FA verification succeeds.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne pattern popularized by reports against Shopify, GitLab, and HackerOne itself; see also 'GraphQL Batching Attacks' write-ups (2022-2024).

labs.title: Server-Side Template Injection in Handlebars Email Preview
labs.description: A merchant dashboard lets shop owners preview transactional emails. The preview endpoint compiles a Handlebars template with the {{lookup}} helper enabled, then renders it in a Node.js worker. The lab intentionally leaves __proto__ accessible via lookup, letting learners walk from a template to process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync. Learners must land RCE and read /flag inside the worker container.
labs.objective: Escape the Handlebars sandbox from the email preview and execute a command that prints the container's /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Render must produce a page containing the contents of /flag (a single line starting FLAG{).
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne reports against Shopify (Handlebars SSTI in email preview, 2022-2023) and multiple Rails/Liquid SSTI reports against Shopify/GitLab; also PortSwigger Academy SSTI labs.

labs.title: SSRF via URL Parser Discrepancy to Cloud Metadata
labs.description: A webhook tester validates outbound URLs with Python's urllib.parse (checking that hostname is not in a blocklist including 169.254.169.254, localhost, and RFC1918 ranges) but then fetches with an HTTP client that reparses. Learners must find a URL that urllib.parse thinks points to example.com but the fetcher resolves to 169.254.169.254 (userinfo tricks, IPv6-mapped IPv4, decimal IP, DNS rebinding, or the '\r\n' host trick). Successfully retrieving the IMDSv1 role credentials from the mocked metadata service yields the flag.
labs.objective: Bypass the SSRF filter to fetch http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/lab-role and print the returned JSON.
labs.flag_hint: Mock IMDS returns credentials whose SessionToken field is the flag.
skills_taught: URL RFC 3986 edge cases (userinfo, brackets, encoded @)
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne reports against GitLab (multiple SSRF via URL parser discrepancies, e.g. h1 #827052 class), Grafana CVE-2022-21702-style patterns, and Orange Tsai's 'A New Era of SSRF' research.

labs.title: Blind SSRF via Headless-Chrome PDF Generator
labs.description: An invoicing feature renders user-supplied HTML to PDF using headless Chrome. The HTML strips
labs.objective: Get the internal /flag response embedded (or side-channel-leaked) into the generated PDF and read it.
labs.flag_hint: The rendered PDF must contain the FLAG{...} string on some page.
skills_taught: internal service discovery from a render sandbox
exfil via image dimensions / CSS timing
labs.inspired_by: Recurrent HackerOne pattern (reports against Airbnb, Shopify, GitLab); see also NahamCon/DefCon talks on 'Server Side Browsers'.

labs.title: Prototype Pollution in Express Merge to RCE
labs.description: An Express app parses querystrings via qs and passes user objects into a hand-rolled deep-merge for a 'preferences' endpoint. The lab also uses ejs render options that respect an 'escapeFunction' property. Learners must pollute Object.prototype so that a subsequent unrelated render call picks up an attacker-controlled escapeFunction that shells out. The lab includes a rendered profile page that triggers the render after pollution.
labs.objective: Chain prototype pollution in POST /preferences to gain RCE when the profile page renders, and read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: The profile page must contain the contents of /flag when rendered by the polluted template engine.
skills_taught: gadget hunting in popular libs (ejs, lodash, Handlebars)
labs.inspired_by: Public HackerOne reports on Kibana (CVE-2019-7609 lineage), and 2022-2024 PP reports against Shopify, HackerOne, and multiple GitLab endpoints (h1 pattern well-documented in Snyk / PortSwigger).

labs.title: XXE in SVG Avatar Upload with Blind OOB Exfil
labs.description: Avatar upload accepts image/svg+xml and rasterizes with librsvg-based tooling that has external entities enabled (lab intentionally uses an old libxml build). The response strips entity content, so learners must chain to an out-of-band DTD hosted on their attacker box to exfiltrate /etc/hostname of the image worker (which contains the flag). Includes Burp Collaborator-style lab collector.
labs.objective: Perform blind OOB XXE via SVG upload and receive the contents of /etc/hostname at the lab collector.
labs.flag_hint: The image-worker container's /etc/hostname is set to the flag; observe it at the collector's /oob/<team> endpoint.
labs.inspired_by: Frans Rosen and others' HackerOne reports against Facebook, Shopify (avatar SVG XXE), 2015-2024; regularly re-disclosed. See also multiple GitLab XXE reports.

labs.title: Client-Side Path Traversal to Same-Origin ATO
labs.description: A SPA has a share widget that fetches /api/messages/${id} where id comes from window.location.hash unfiltered. It also has a legitimate /api/csrf-bypass?to=/api/transfer&amount=... endpoint (a JSON POST) protected only by a Referer check. Learners craft a hash like #../csrf-bypass?to=/api/transfer&amount=1000&recipient=attacker that causes the fetch() to send an authenticated POST to a state-changing endpoint from the victim's origin, transferring funds.
labs.objective: Trick the victim bot into loading a page whose hash-driven fetch causes a state-changing transfer, then read the attacker balance/flag.
labs.flag_hint: Attacker /wallet returns the flag once balance is credited from the victim.
labs.inspired_by: Doyensec 'CSPT2CSRF' research and HackerOne reports leveraging CSPT on Zoom, Basecamp, and Slack widgets 2023-2024.

labs.title: postMessage XSS on Embeddable Chat Widget
labs.description: An embeddable chat widget accepts postMessages from any origin and dispatches on message.type. The 'setTheme' handler does el.innerHTML = message.themeCSS. Learners host an embedding page that posts a crafted message causing script execution in the widget's origin, exfiltrating the visitor's authentication cookie to the lab collector.
labs.objective: Trigger XSS in the widget's iframe via postMessage and exfiltrate the visitor's cookie.
labs.flag_hint: Collector receives victim cookie; the cookie value is the flag.
skills_taught: fixing with event.origin allowlists and textContent
labs.inspired_by: Recurrent HackerOne pattern (Slack widget, HackerOne Rooms, PayPal chat, 2022-2024). See also 'The pain of postMessage' write-ups.

labs.title: NoSQL Injection via Type Juggling on Login
labs.description: A Node/Express + MongoDB login uses body-parser JSON and passes req.body.user and req.body.password directly into a Mongo find. Learners must send {"user":{"$ne":null},"password":{"$ne":null}} to bypass auth as the first user, and then use $regex to enumerate the admin password character-by-character until the admin dashboard reveals the flag.
labs.objective: Log in as admin without knowing the password and read /admin/dashboard.
labs.flag_hint: Admin dashboard contains a card whose data-note attribute is the flag.
skills_taught: prevention: strict input validation / mongoose casting
why casting to String is not enough
labs.inspired_by: Long-standing pattern; 2022-2024 HackerOne reports against multiple startups and one Verizon Media asset. Also see NahamCon workshops.

labs.title: SameSite=Lax GET-based CSRF via OAuth Callback
labs.description: A password-change endpoint is a POST protected by SameSite=Lax cookies. However, an OAuth 'linking' flow accepts the linkage decision via GET /oauth/link?provider=X&token=... and issues a 302 to POST /account/password-change with the pre-filled password from the token. Because top-level GET navigation sends Lax cookies, and the 302 is same-site, the follow-up POST also carries cookies. Learners craft the linking URL, host it on their page, and get the victim bot to click it, resulting in password change.
labs.objective: Change the victim bot's password via the OAuth-linking-plus-redirect chain and log in.
labs.flag_hint: After login as the victim, /me returns the flag.
skills_taught: chaining OAuth linking flows with state-changing GETs
distinguishing Lax vs Strict vs None
labs.inspired_by: Class of chained CSRF-via-OAuth ATOs on HackerOne against Facebook (2022 chained account-linking bug), Grammarly, and GitHub-adjacent apps 2023-2024.

labs.title: Second-Order SQLi via Username in a Reporting Query
labs.description: Registration accepts usernames validated only for length; storage is parameterized (safe). A separate weekly reporting job builds a raw SQL query by string-concatenating usernames into a WHERE-IN clause. Learners must register a benign-looking account whose username contains SQL syntax that lies dormant until the report runs (which the lab triggers every 20s), then read exfiltrated rows from the report output endpoint.
labs.objective: Register the right username so the next report cycle exfiltrates the users.secret column into the public report output.
labs.flag_hint: Report output page must show a row containing the admin.secret value (the flag).
skills_taught: identifying safe vs unsafe query builders
labs.inspired_by: Pattern rewarded on HackerOne against Basecamp, GitLab (raw ActiveRecord in reporting), and internal DoD assets 2022-2024.

labs.title: Business Logic: Negative-Quantity Refund Stacking
labs.description: A checkout accepts POST /order/refund with an items array. Each item has quantity: number. The refund logic sums qty*price and credits the wallet, but never enforces qty > 0 or qty <= originally_purchased. Learners must construct a refund request that stacks positive and negative quantities to net a wallet credit exceeding the order value, unlocking the flag.
labs.objective: Manipulate the refund payload so wallet balance exceeds $10,000 and read /wallet.
labs.flag_hint: GET /wallet returns the flag once balance_cents > 1000000.
labs.inspired_by: Public HackerOne reports of price/quantity manipulation against Shopify Plus, Uber Eats, and PayPal 2022-2024 (many privately closed but publicly summarized on H1 hacktivity).

labs.title: Race Condition on Refund + Wallet Withdrawal
labs.description: Refund credits and wallet-withdrawal debits both read balance, mutate, then write, using separate transactions without row-level locking. The lab exposes /wallet/refund (credits) and /wallet/withdraw (debits) and enforces daily withdraw caps. Learners must race concurrent withdraws so the cap check passes twice with the same 'seen' balance, draining more than the daily cap. Withdraw-past-cap unlocks the flag endpoint.
labs.objective: Drain more than the daily withdrawal cap via a race between two concurrent /wallet/withdraw calls.
labs.flag_hint: GET /vault returns the flag once the audit log shows a withdrawal in excess of the daily cap.
skills_taught: row-level locking vs advisory locks vs serializable isolation
using single-packet or last-byte-sync for close races
labs.inspired_by: Multiple HackerOne payments-race disclosures (Coinbase, Kraken, PayPal, Airbnb Payments) 2022-2024; also PortSwigger single-packet race material.

labs.title: Predictable Password Reset Token via UUIDv1 Timestamp Leak
labs.description: Password reset tokens are UUIDv1s generated on the reset-request endpoint. UUIDv1 embeds a timestamp and MAC. Learners must request a reset for their own account to observe the MAC and timestamp cadence, then predict the target user's token by knowing they requested a reset in a narrow window (the lab bot requests one every 10s). Predict, use, log in as target.
labs.objective: Reset the target user's password by predicting their UUIDv1 token and reading /me.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me as the target returns the flag.
skills_taught: brute-forcing within a narrow time window
why UUIDv4 (or v7 with sufficient entropy) matters
labs.inspired_by: Historical HackerOne reports (HackerOne #257953-class) and 2023-2024 predictable-token reports against several SaaS via UUIDv1.

labs.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution to Auth Bypass
labs.description: An auth proxy checks that ?role=user in the querystring, using Python's request.args.get('role') which returns the first occurrence. The origin (a Java Spring app) uses request.getParameter('role') which, when duplicate names exist, returns the last. Learners craft a URL with ?role=user&role=admin so the proxy sees 'user' and the origin sees 'admin', granting access to /admin/config, which returns the flag.
labs.objective: Access /admin/config through the proxy using HPP.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin/config returns JSON with a config.flag field.
skills_taught: creative use of arrays vs scalars
tech_stack: Python Flask proxy + Java Spring origin
labs.inspired_by: Class of proxy-vs-origin discrepancies reported on HackerOne against Verizon Media, US DoD, and multiple gov programs 2022-2024.

labs.title: XSLT SSRF via User-Supplied Stylesheet in Report Generator
labs.description: A report-export feature lets users upload an XSLT to style their XML report. The XSLT processor (Saxon in a lab config) permits document() and doc() functions, and the container can reach internal admin.internal:8080/flag. Learners must craft an XSLT that uses document() to pull the internal /flag and embed its content in the styled output.
labs.objective: Retrieve http://admin.internal:8080/flag into the exported report via XSLT document().
labs.flag_hint: The exported HTML must contain the FLAG{...} string from admin.internal.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne reports against Salesforce-adjacent report pipelines, and older but instructive Netflix Genie / gov reports (2022-2024).

labs.title: Zip Slip to RCE via Plugin Import
labs.description: A CMS lets admins install .zip plugins. Extraction uses Node's tar/zip package with a hand-rolled path join that concatenates the target dir with the archive-supplied filename without normalizing '..' Learners must craft a zip whose entry name is '../../app/routes/hijack.js' so extraction overwrites a live route file with attacker code, which is hot-loaded and returns the flag.
labs.objective: Escape the extraction directory via zip slip, overwrite a live route, and read /flag through the injected route.
labs.flag_hint: GET /pwn returns the contents of /flag once the injected route is loaded.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 'Zip Slip' vulnerability class; HackerOne reports against multiple SaaS plugin systems 2022-2024.

labs.title: YAML Deserialization RCE via CI Import
labs.description: A CI dashboard imports pipeline definitions via yaml.load (PyYAML, unsafe) from an authenticated file upload. Learners must craft a YAML file using !!python/object/apply:os.system to execute a command and read /flag. The lab includes a rate-limited endpoint and cleanup-timer that makes it non-trivially blind.
labs.objective: Achieve RCE via unsafe YAML deserialization in the CI dashboard and read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: The command's stdout appears in the import-error log accessible at /ci/logs/latest; include /flag output there.
skills_taught: blind RCE via log side channels
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2017-18342-class YAML deserialization; HackerOne reports against multiple CI/CD SaaS (2022-2024) and against internal Uber tooling.

labs.title: WebSocket Origin Bypass to Cross-Origin Chat Takeover
labs.description: A chat backend exposes wss://chat.lab/ws that authenticates via the browser's cookie jar and enforces no Origin allowlist (assuming CORS covers it, which it does not for WebSockets). Learners host a page that opens a WebSocket to the chat backend from any origin, then send messages as the victim and read the victim's DMs (which include the flag).
labs.objective: Read the victim bot's DMs via a cross-origin WebSocket connection.
labs.flag_hint: One victim DM contains the flag.
skills_taught: why CORS does not cover WS
using browser DevTools to snoop WS frames
labs.inspired_by: Christian Schneider CSWSH lineage; HackerOne reports against Slack, Zoom, and Snap 2022-2024.

labs.title: DNS Rebinding to a Localhost Developer Agent
labs.description: A locally-running developer agent binds to 127.0.0.1:31337 and trusts any request from a browser origin (no auth token). Learners must craft a page whose script fetches http://rebind.attacker.lab/ (initially resolves to attacker IP, then after TTL flips to 127.0.0.1) so the fetch hits the local agent under the attacker's origin. The agent exposes /exec that returns the output of a shell command including /flag.
labs.objective: Rebind DNS to reach the local dev agent from a hostile page and print the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The page must POST a captured /flag string to the lab collector.
skills_taught: DNS rebinding mechanics (short TTL, dual-A tricks)
why localhost binding is not enough
safe patterns: token per session, PSL checks
labs.inspired_by: Tavis Ormandy / Project Zero patterns; HackerOne reports against Zoom local agent (2022), Discord updater, and Grammarly desktop 2022-2024.

labs.title: Dependency Confusion Against a Private npm Scope
labs.description: A CI job runs `npm install` with a .npmrc that lists both the public registry and a private one, but not with strict scope routing. Learners must publish a higher-version tarball to a mock public registry under the same scoped name as an internal package used by the app, then trigger a CI rebuild that fetches the attacker version. The malicious postinstall reads /flag inside the CI container and posts it to the lab collector.
labs.objective: Cause CI to install the attacker-published scoped package instead of the private one and exfiltrate /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Collector receives the flag string in a POST from the CI container.
skills_taught: npm scope routing / always-auth / registry pinning
detection: monitoring public registries for internal names
labs.inspired_by: Alex Birsan's dependency-confusion research (2021) and follow-on HackerOne reports against Apple, PayPal, Yelp, Uber, and Shopify 2021-2024.

labs.title: HTTP/2 Header Smuggling / CRLF Injection to Cache Poison
labs.description: An HTTP/2 frontend does not validate that pseudo-header and regular header values are free of CR/LF (older library). The origin is HTTP/1.1. Learners must inject '\r\n' bytes into an H2 header value that, after downgrade, becomes a header split at the origin, letting them poison the cache for /pricing with attacker-controlled content served to future visitors.
labs.objective: Achieve cache poisoning on /pricing via an H2 CRLF-in-header primitive.
labs.flag_hint: Any subsequent GET /pricing must return an HTML page containing 'FLAG{...}' the learner injected.
skills_taught: safe patterns: strict header validation everywhere
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle HTTP/2 research; CVE-2021-33193 / CVE-2023-44487 lineage; HackerOne reports against Netflix and multiple gov programs 2023-2024.

labs.title: OIDC JWKS Manipulation via kid Path Traversal
labs.description: An SSO relying party uses the JWT header 'kid' to select a public key by reading a file path 'keys/{kid}.pem'. No sanitization. Learners upload an arbitrary attacker-controlled file via an existing avatar-upload endpoint (which stores under uploads/avatars/{userid}.pem) and then set kid='../uploads/avatars/{userid}' so the RP verifies signatures with the attacker's public key. Forge admin JWT, read /admin.
labs.objective: Chain avatar upload + kid path traversal to forge an admin-signed JWT and read /admin.
labs.flag_hint: GET /admin returns the flag once verified against the attacker-controlled key.
skills_taught: safe patterns: allowlist kids, use a JWKS URL only
labs.inspired_by: Class of JWT kid-injection bugs (CVE-2018-0114 lineage); HackerOne reports against multiple SSO products 2022-2024.

labs.title: GraphQL Aliased-Mutation 2FA Brute in One Request
labs.description: Complement to the earlier alias-batching lab: here, the target is specifically the 2FA mutation. The endpoint has a global 5-attempts-per-minute limiter counted per HTTP request. Learners must submit a single GraphQL document with 1,000,000 aliased verifyTotp mutations covering the full 6-digit space, then observe which alias returned success and use that code to complete login.
labs.objective: Brute 2FA in one HTTP request and log in as the target.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me as the target returns the flag after 2FA completion.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #1109311-class reports (aliased batching 2FA brute) against multiple GraphQL-backed SaaS 2022-2024.

labs.title: CSP Bypass via JSONP Endpoint + Same-Origin Trust
labs.description: A page has a strict-ish CSP: script-src 'self' 'nonce-XYZ'. However, the origin hosts an old /jsonp?callback=fn endpoint that reflects the callback name into JS. Learners must find an HTML-injection sink (a Markdown preview that permits <script src>) and use the JSONP endpoint to smuggle arbitrary code past CSP, exfiltrating the visitor's session cookie.
labs.objective: Chain Markdown HTML injection + JSONP callback reflection to execute JS under the CSP.
labs.flag_hint: Collector receives victim cookie; the value is the flag.
skills_taught: chaining injection + gadget to bypass CSP
labs.inspired_by: Michele Spagnuolo / Lukas Weichselbaum CSP-bypass research; HackerOne reports against Google-owned properties and Yahoo/Verizon Media 2022-2024.

labs.title: SMTP Header Injection to Redirect 2FA Codes
labs.description: The account-update endpoint accepts a display name that is later interpolated into an outgoing email's 'From' header for 2FA code emails. The mailer does not filter CR/LF from the display name. Learners must inject Bcc: attacker@lab into the header stream via the display name so that when the victim bot requests a 2FA email, a copy is delivered to the attacker mailbox. Learners then use the code to log in as the victim.
labs.objective: Inject a Bcc header via SMTP header injection and receive a copy of the victim's 2FA code, then log in as the victim.
labs.flag_hint: GET /me as the victim returns the flag after 2FA completion.
skills_taught: safe patterns: strict validation + libraries that pre-encode
labs.inspired_by: Recurrent HackerOne pattern (Uber, Snap, GitLab, DoD) 2022-2024; also see Mattermost CVE-2023-32565-class header-injection cases.

labs.title: Telco Billing Portal — SSRF to Cloud Metadata
labs.description: A mock European telecom's self-service billing portal offers a 'preview invoice logo from URL' feature that fetches remote images server-side. The fetcher uses a naive allowlist (checks the hostname before resolving DNS) and follows redirects. Backend runs on a mock IMDSv1 endpoint (169.254.169.254) reachable only from the app pod.
labs.objective: Bypass the URL allowlist via DNS rebinding or a 302 redirect to the internal metadata service, exfiltrate the IAM role token from the mock metadata endpoint, and use it to read the flag stored in a mock S3 bucket exposed only to that role.
labs.flag_hint: Flag lives in mock-s3://internal-invoices/flag.txt, readable only with the metadata role's STS token.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-14243 (SSRF via URL fetcher) + Capital One 2019 postmortem pattern; YesWeHack Dojo SSRF track

labs.title: Music Streaming GraphQL — Introspection to Playlist IDOR
labs.description: A mock music-streaming SPA exposes a GraphQL endpoint with introspection enabled in production. Playlist queries authorize on the JWT's user_id claim only for a top-level 'me' resolver, but the nested 'playlistById(id)' resolver forgot the ownership check. Private playlist names, notes, and share links are readable by any authenticated user who knows or guesses a numeric ID.
labs.objective: Use introspection to map the schema, enumerate playlists of the admin user by sequential ID, and read the private note field of admin's playlist that contains the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is the 'privateNote' field on admin's playlist id=1337.
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #980511 (GraphQL IDOR pattern) + Intigriti 'Bug Bytes' GraphQL series

labs.title: Retail Bank API — JWT Algorithm Confusion (RS256 to HS256)
labs.description: A mock retail bank exposes a customer API that validates JWTs with a library which accepts the alg header without pinning. The RSA public key is published at /.well-known/jwks.json for legitimate RS256 verification. An attacker can re-sign a forged token using the public key as an HMAC secret and set alg=HS256, promoting themselves to the 'privateBanker' role.
labs.objective: Fetch the public JWK, forge an HS256 token signed with the PEM-encoded public key, escalate to privateBanker, and read the /api/vault/flag endpoint.
labs.flag_hint: Flag returned by GET /api/vault/flag with role=privateBanker in the token.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-29217 (PyJWT alg confusion) + numerous YesWeHack fintech reports

labs.title: Insurance Claim SVG Upload — Blind XXE to Local File Read
labs.description: A mock EU insurer accepts SVG uploads for damage-claim illustrations and rasterises them server-side with a vulnerable XML parser. External entities and parameter entities are enabled. The rasteriser echoes rendering errors, enabling an out-of-band exfiltration channel via a controlled DNS/HTTP listener bundled in the lab.
labs.objective: Craft an SVG with an OOB XXE payload that reads /etc/passwd and /opt/app/secrets/flag.txt, exfiltrating via the lab's built-in collaborator.
labs.flag_hint: Contents of /opt/app/secrets/flag.txt exfiltrated via the OOB channel.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-40899 (lxml XXE) + YesWeHack Dojo XXE challenges

labs.title: Retail Checkout — postMessage Origin Bypass to Session Theft
labs.description: A mock EU retailer's checkout page opens a payment-provider iframe and listens for postMessage without validating event.origin, using a loose 'startsWith' check. A malicious page hosting an iframe with a spoofable origin substring can send a message that triggers the parent to dump the CSRF token and cart total into a callback URL controlled by the attacker.
labs.objective: Host an attacker page (served on a lab domain) that opens the checkout, triggers the vulnerable handler via postMessage, and captures the CSRF token to use against the checkout endpoint.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is returned by the checkout confirmation endpoint when called with a valid stolen CSRF token.
labs.inspired_by: Intigriti XSS Challenge 0722 (postMessage) + numerous H1 retail reports

labs.title: Coupon Redemption — Concurrent Race to Infinite Discounts
labs.description: A mock e-commerce coupon service checks 'remaining uses' then decrements, without an atomic transaction or row-level lock. With sufficient parallel requests, one coupon can be redeemed dozens of times, driving order totals negative. The admin monitoring dashboard exposes a flag when a specific single-use 'VIP2026' coupon is redeemed more than 10 times.
labs.objective: Send parallel HTTP requests to redeem the VIP2026 coupon at least 11 times to trigger the admin alert and reveal the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag surfaces in the /admin/alerts feed once redemption count exceeds threshold.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger single-packet race technique + multiple YesWeHack retail race-condition reports

labs.title: Enterprise SSO — OAuth redirect_uri Open Redirect to Token Leak
labs.description: A mock enterprise SSO honors the OAuth2 authorization code flow but validates redirect_uri by prefix match. Any client-side open redirect on the whitelisted domain (a mock intranet page with a naive ?next= parameter) can be chained to smuggle the auth code to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
labs.objective: Chain the redirect_uri prefix match with the intranet's open redirect to receive an authorization code, exchange it for tokens, and read the /me endpoint of the victim account whose session is preseeded in a headless victim bot.
labs.flag_hint: Flag lives on GET /me for the victim account once you hold their access token.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2020-1731 (Keycloak open redirect) + Intigriti OAuth writeups

labs.title: Federated Login — SAML XSW to Admin Impersonation
labs.description: A mock federated login accepts SAML assertions but the SP uses an XPath that selects the first Assertion, while signature verification runs over the second. Classic XML Signature Wrapping (XSW3) lets the attacker keep a valid signed assertion while injecting an unsigned assertion that claims NameID=admin.
labs.objective: Take the provided legitimately signed 'user' SAML response, transform it via XSW3, and log in as admin to reach the /admin/flag page.
labs.flag_hint: Flag rendered on /admin/flag after successful admin login.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2017-11427 / python-saml XSW + Ruby-SAML CVE-2024-45409 pattern

labs.title: Ticketing ORM — Second-Order SQL Injection via Stored Comment
labs.description: A mock ticketing app uses parameterised inserts (safe) but a background reporting job builds a raw SQL query by interpolating the stored 'ticket.tag' field into an ORDER BY clause. Attacker writes a crafted tag, waits for the nightly (or lab-accelerated) job, and injects.
labs.objective: Poison a ticket tag with a payload that, when the report runs, exfiltrates the admin_secrets table via a stacked or time-based technique, then read the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is stored in admin_secrets.value where key='FLAG'.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-32224 (Rails YAML+SQL) + YesWeHack ORM injection writeups

labs.title: Delivery App Login — NoSQL Operator Injection
labs.description: A mock food-delivery API accepts JSON login payloads and passes them directly into a Mongo find() query. Sending an operator object like {'$ne': null} for password bypasses authentication for any known email. The admin email is exposed via a public 'meet the team' page.
labs.objective: Log in as the admin without knowing their password by injecting a Mongo operator, then read the admin-only /orders/reports endpoint that contains the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag appears in JSON body of /orders/reports when authenticated as admin.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-10768 + PortSwigger NoSQLi labs; recurring pattern in Intigriti reports

labs.title: GDPR Data Export — CSV Formula Injection
labs.description: A mock analytics dashboard's 'export subscribers to CSV' feature reflects user-provided fields (name, note) directly. Cells starting with =, +, -, @ or tab become formulas when opened in Excel/LibreOffice. An admin bot in the lab opens exported CSVs; a payload calling WEBSERVICE() exfiltrates content to a collaborator.
labs.objective: Sign up with a payload in your display name that, when the admin exports and opens the CSV, exfiltrates the admin's session cookie value to the lab collaborator.
labs.flag_hint: The flag is the cookie value delivered to your collaborator.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2014-3524 (LibreOffice) + OWASP CSV injection guidance; common EU GDPR-export finding

labs.title: GDPR Data Portability Endpoint — IDOR Leaking Other Data Subjects
labs.description: A mock EU SaaS implements a 'Download my data' endpoint per Article 20 GDPR. The endpoint accepts ?subject_id=... in the URL and checks authentication but not that the ID belongs to the caller. Enumerating IDs returns other users' full profile exports (mock synthetic data only).
labs.objective: Enumerate subject_ids, find the export whose 'notes' field contains the flag string, and submit it.
labs.flag_hint: One of the synthetic subjects has notes='FLAG{...}'.
labs.inspired_by: Multiple public YesWeHack disclosures on EU SaaS 'right to access' endpoints (2023-2024)

labs.title: Retail CDN — Web Cache Deception on Account Page
labs.description: A mock retailer sits behind a CDN that caches by path suffix (.css, .js, .png). The origin ignores the extension for authenticated routes, so /account/profile.css returns the personalised profile HTML but the CDN caches it. Next visitor to the same URL sees the previous user's data.
labs.objective: As the victim (via a lab bot that periodically browses their account), have the attacker request /account/profile.css after the victim, then read the cached response containing the victim's tokenised loyalty number that is the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is the loyalty number rendered on the victim's cached profile page.
labs.inspired_by: Omer Gil's WCD research + numerous Intigriti/BB retail reports 2023-2025

labs.title: Load Balancer + Backend — HTTP Request Smuggling (CL.TE)
labs.description: A mock front-end HAProxy uses Content-Length while the backend Gunicorn honors Transfer-Encoding. Smuggle a request that hijacks the next legitimate user's request, forcing it into an attacker-controlled endpoint that logs the smuggled headers (including the victim's session cookie).
labs.objective: Perform a CL.TE smuggle that captures the periodic admin health-check request, extract its Authorization header, and use it against /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag returned by /admin/flag with the smuggled Bearer token.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger 2019 smuggling paper + Kettle disclosures affecting EU CDNs

labs.title: Password Reset — Predictable Token Based on Timestamp
labs.description: A mock forum generates password reset tokens as md5(email + unix_timestamp_seconds). Attackers who trigger a reset for a known email can brute the +/- 5 second window offline to derive the token.
labs.objective: Trigger reset for admin@lab.local, precisely brute the token in a small time window, and log in as admin to read the flag on the admin dashboard.
labs.flag_hint: Flag on GET /admin after successful password reset and login.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2017-9805-adjacent patterns + Intigriti disclosures on reset flows

labs.title: Account Takeover via Email Verification Race
labs.description: A mock SaaS lets users change their email; verification is sent to the new email, but the account's login email is updated before verification completes if two concurrent 'change email' requests are sent with different targets. Attacker sets email to victim's, wins the race, and gains login access.
labs.objective: Take over the pre-seeded victim account by exploiting the change-email race and log in to read /me containing the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag returned by /me for the victim account after takeover.
labs.inspired_by: Multiple YesWeHack ATO disclosures 2023-2024 + Slack 2021 ATO writeup pattern

labs.title: Node API — Prototype Pollution via Query Parser to Auth Bypass
labs.description: A mock Node API uses an old version of qs and merges query into config objects with a naive recursive merge. Sending ?__proto__[isAdmin]=1 pollutes Object.prototype so that all subsequent requests treat the caller as admin until process restart.
labs.objective: Trigger prototype pollution, then call /admin/flag which reads req.session.isAdmin.
labs.flag_hint: Flag on /admin/flag once req.session.isAdmin is truthy via pollution.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-10744 (lodash) + CVE-2022-24999 (Express qs) + Intigriti PP writeups

labs.title: HR Portal ZIP Upload — Zip Slip to RCE
labs.description: A mock HR portal accepts a ZIP of CV attachments and extracts them into a per-user directory using a naive loop that trusts entry names. A crafted ZIP with entries like ../../var/www/app/plugins/rce.php writes to a directory that is auto-loaded on the next request, giving RCE.
labs.objective: Craft a Zip Slip archive that drops a PHP webshell into the plugins directory, execute it, and read the flag at /opt/flag.
labs.flag_hint: Contents of /opt/flag readable via the webshell.
labs.inspired_by: Snyk 'Zip Slip' 2018 + CVE-2018-1002200 + EU HR-tech reports on YesWeHack

labs.title: Newsletter Builder — SSTI in Twig Sandbox Escape
labs.description: A mock newsletter editor lets users write Twig templates for personalisation. The sandbox extension is enabled but a whitelisted filter can be chained to reach dangerous methods, enabling RCE. Classic sandbox-escape gadget.
labs.objective: Escape the Twig sandbox, execute a shell command, and read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Contents of /flag exfiltrated via SSTI-driven command execution.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-23614 (Symfony/Twig sandbox) + YesWeHack Symfony writeups

labs.title: Legacy Portal — Java Deserialization to RCE
labs.description: A mock legacy Java web app persists workflow state in a base64-encoded serialised object cookie. The classpath contains commons-collections 3.2.1, giving a full ysoserial CommonsCollections1 gadget chain.
labs.objective: Forge a serialised payload that runs 'cat /flag > /tmp/out', then retrieve /tmp/out via a follow-up request.
labs.flag_hint: Contents of /flag written to a public directory by the payload.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2015-4852 pattern + CVE-2023-46604 (ActiveMQ) EU banking impact

labs.title: SPA API — CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null Exploited via Sandboxed iframe
labs.description: A mock SaaS API reflects the Origin header and, when Origin is 'null', responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. A sandboxed iframe (or data: URL) produces a 'null' origin, letting an attacker page read credentialed API responses.
labs.objective: Host an attacker page with a sandboxed iframe that reads /api/me from the victim's session and exfiltrates the account's API key, which is the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The victim's API key returned by /api/me.
labs.inspired_by: PortSwigger CORS labs + numerous YesWeHack CORS reports on EU SaaS

labs.title: Marketing Subdomain Takeover to Cookie Tossing
labs.description: A mock corp has *.corp.lab pointed at an abandoned SaaS. The attacker 'claims' the subdomain in the lab-provided mock SaaS panel, hosts JS that sets a Domain=.corp.lab cookie that overrides the app's session cookie ordering, exploiting cookie ambiguity to fix a session on the victim.
labs.objective: Take over marketing.corp.lab, set a tossing cookie so the victim's next login binds to your session, then read /account to reveal the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag rendered on /account when the fixated session is used.
labs.inspired_by: Detectify subdomain-takeover research + Intigriti disclosures on abandoned CNAMEs

labs.title: Debug Endpoint Leak — PII and Secrets in Stack Traces
labs.description: A mock Django app was deployed with DEBUG=True. Triggering an unhandled exception (invalid UUID in a query parameter) renders a full debug page including local variables containing the DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, and (synthetic) subscriber emails.
labs.objective: Craft a request that triggers the traceback, then extract the FLAG environment variable displayed in the settings dump.
labs.flag_hint: FLAG env var visible in the debug settings pane.
labs.inspired_by: Long-tail YesWeHack reports on EU orgs shipping DEBUG=True; CWE-209

labs.title: 2FA Verification — Timing Attack on Non-Constant-Time Compare
labs.description: A mock banking app verifies TOTP codes with a byte-by-byte '==' comparison. Response time leaks the number of correct leading digits, enabling a digit-by-digit recovery over a stable network. The lab pins the app to a low-jitter loopback with a measurable delay to make the attack tractable.
labs.objective: Recover the victim's current 6-digit TOTP via timing measurements, submit it within its validity window, and log in to read the flag on /vault.
labs.flag_hint: Flag on /vault after successful 2FA login as the victim.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2018-11235-style timing bugs + academic timing-attack literature; recurring in fintech reports

labs.title: Marketing Site Cache Poisoning via Unkeyed X-Forwarded-Host
labs.description: A mock marketing site reflects X-Forwarded-Host into absolute URLs in the HTML (canonical link, JS bundle src). The CDN does not key on that header. An attacker poisons a popular page so subsequent visitors load a JS bundle from attacker.lab, achieving stored-XSS-like reach on victims.
labs.objective: Poison /pricing so the next victim bot loads an attacker JS that posts document.cookie to the collaborator; the flag is the victim bot's session cookie value.
labs.flag_hint: Victim's cookie captured at the collaborator endpoint.
labs.inspired_by: James Kettle 'Practical Web Cache Poisoning' + Intigriti/YWH cache reports

labs.title: CSP Bypass via Whitelisted JSONP Endpoint
labs.description: A mock news portal has a reflected XSS injection point but a Content-Security-Policy that only allows scripts from cdn.lab. That CDN, however, hosts a JSONP endpoint that reflects a callback parameter as executable JS. Chaining these bypasses CSP.
labs.objective: Craft a payload that uses the whitelisted JSONP endpoint to execute arbitrary JS in the origin, exfiltrating document.body of /admin/flag which is XHR-fetched by the victim bot.
labs.flag_hint: Flag is the content of /admin/flag as read by injected JS.
labs.inspired_by: CSP-bypass research (Weichselbaum et al.) + Intigriti CSP-bypass challenges

labs.title: Webhook Configuration — Blind SSRF to Internal Admin Panel
labs.description: A mock SaaS lets tenants configure outbound webhooks. There is no allowlist, no response returned to the user, and no timeout tuning. An attacker points a webhook at http://internal-admin:8080/create-token and, using request-smuggling-style body crafting, causes the internal panel to mint an admin token that is emailed to a lab inbox.
labs.objective: Craft a webhook that hits the internal admin API, causing it to issue a token to the attacker's registered email; use the token to read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: Flag returned by /flag with the minted admin token.
labs.inspired_by: OVH-style webhook SSRF reports + CVE-2022-4886 pattern (Ingress SSRF)

labs.title: CI/CD — Typosquatted Dependency Publishes Secrets to Attacker
labs.description: A mock internal npm project's install script fetches a package whose name is a subtle typo of a real one. The typosquat exfiltrates env vars from CI at postinstall. The lab ships a local npm registry with both real and typosquat packages; the player must identify the malicious one from lockfile drift and stop it, then answer a forensic question that yields the flag.
labs.objective: Detect the typosquat via lockfile audit, inspect its postinstall, and recover the exfiltrated secret from a mock 'attacker' listener; the recovered secret is the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The exfiltrated env var value captured at the attacker listener.
labs.inspired_by: event-stream 2018 + ua-parser-js 2021 + CVE-2022-24439 (GitPython); numerous EU CI incidents

labs.title: Prototype Pollution to RCE via Config Merge
labs.description: A Node/Express admin dashboard imports uploaded JSON snippets and deep-merges them into a runtime config object. The deep-merge implementation walks nested keys without filtering __proto__, and downstream code path uses child_process spawn with an options object whose shell flag is looked up dynamically. A malicious upload can pollute Object.prototype.shell = '/bin/sh -c ...' and turn the next admin action into command execution.
labs.objective: Craft a JSON payload that pollutes Object.prototype so the next scheduled maintenance task spawns a shell reading /flag.txt into the response HTML.
labs.flag_hint: flag{proto_shell_gadget_via_maintenance_job}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2022 'prophecy' + DiceCTF 2023 'unfinished' + CVE-2019-10744 lodash defaultsDeep prototype pollution class

labs.title: DOMPurify Mutation XSS via SVG Namespace Confusion
labs.description: A note-sharing app runs an outdated pinned DOMPurify (with hooks enabled) server-side for storage and client-side for render. Because the server uses jsdom while the client uses a real browser, the two parse the same HTML into different DOM trees. An attacker crafts markup that survives sanitisation on the server but mutates into executable script inside <svg><style> when the browser reparses. Solving requires understanding the HTML parser algorithm and DOMPurify's SANITIZE_DOM assumption.
labs.objective: Post a note that fires alert(document.domain) in the admin bot session and exfiltrates its cookie to /collect.
labs.flag_hint: flag{mxss_svg_style_reparse_admin_cookie}
labs.inspired_by: DiceCTF 2023 'sanity' + Cure53 DOMPurify bypass writeups (CVE-2024-45801 class)

labs.title: CSS Injection Exfiltration via Font Ligatures
labs.description: A blog lets users style their profile page with a scoped <style> block but strips angle brackets and quote characters. Cookies for the admin path are HttpOnly, but a CSRF token is rendered into an inline <meta> tag. With no attribute selectors allowed, the attacker abuses a custom @font-face ligature table plus scroll-triggered background-image URLs to leak the token one character at a time via unique network requests.
labs.objective: Exfiltrate the admin's per-request CSRF token character by character using only CSS, then use it to POST /admin/read_flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{css_ligature_scroll_leak_csrf_admin}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2022 'modernblog' + PlaidCTF 2020 'contacts' + d0nut CSS-exfil research

labs.title: Server-Side XSLT Injection with EXSLT File Read
labs.description: A legacy corporate reporting endpoint accepts a user-supplied XSLT stylesheet and transforms an internal XML feed. The libxslt build has EXSLT extensions and document() enabled. The player must escape the transform sandbox with xsl:value-of using the document() function on file:// URIs, then pivot via exsl:node-set to read the flag file mounted read-only inside the container.
labs.objective: Submit an XSLT that reads /var/secrets/flag.xml and embeds its contents in the rendered PDF report.
labs.flag_hint: flag{xslt_document_file_uri_exsl_pivot}
labs.inspired_by: HITCON 2021 'oShell' + RealWorldCTF 2022 XSLT class + CVE-2019-11068

labs.title: HTTP/2 CL.TE Downgrade Request Smuggling
labs.description: A two-tier stack terminates HTTP/2 at a caddy front-end and forwards HTTP/1.1 to a Node backend. The front-end strips pseudo-headers but forwards a client-supplied Content-Length verbatim, while the backend honours Transfer-Encoding: chunked. The player must smuggle an admin-only POST /internal/rotate_flag request in front of another user's queued request and read the rotated flag from the response cache.
labs.objective: Poison the backend queue so a victim GET /home receives the response body of the smuggled /admin/dump_flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{h2_cl_te_downgrade_smuggle_admin_dump}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2023 'smuggler' + PortSwigger 'HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse' by James Kettle

labs.title: JWT RS256 to HS256 Algorithm Confusion
labs.description: A microservice publishes its RSA public key at a well-known JWKS endpoint and validates tokens with a permissive verifier that trusts the alg header. The player fetches the public key, switches alg to HS256, and signs an admin token using the PEM bytes as the HMAC secret.
labs.objective: Forge a token with role=admin and read /flag via GET /api/admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{alg_confusion_pem_bytes_as_hmac_key}
labs.inspired_by: SekaiCTF 2022 'jwtwt' + CVE-2022-21449 style + classic auth0 disclosure

labs.title: PostgreSQL COPY FROM PROGRAM via Report Import
labs.description: A DevOps portal lets analysts import CSVs directly through a raw psql session exposed behind an auth wall the player has already bypassed via a stacked-query SQLi in a preview endpoint. The player must escalate to shell using COPY table FROM PROGRAM with a superuser role obtained by pg_read_server_files then reading /flag.
labs.objective: Get RCE as postgres, cat /flag, and exfil via a table read.
labs.flag_hint: flag{copy_from_program_pg_superuser_shell}
labs.inspired_by: RealWorldCTF 2022 'ezpop' + PayloadsAllTheThings PG cheat + HackerOne #1288848 style

labs.title: WebAssembly Bounds-Check Bypass Oracle
labs.description: The player is given a small custom WASM binary compiled from C that manages an in-memory 'vault'. Signed 32-bit arithmetic on the offset lets a crafted request compute a negative index that wraps past the linear memory bound and returns arbitrary bytes from the module's data segment, where the flag key material is baked in. The player must reverse the WASM (no debug info) with a decompiler, spot the missing unsigned cast, and script the leak.
labs.objective: Reverse the WASM, find the sign bug, and dump the flag string from linear memory.
labs.flag_hint: flag{wasm_signed_offset_underflow_linear_leak}
labs.inspired_by: Google CTF 2022 'compression' + PlaidCTF 2023 'wasm-safe' + CVE-2022-2294 class

labs.title: SQL Transaction Race for Double-Spend
labs.description: An in-app credit ledger uses SELECT balance / IF / UPDATE without SELECT FOR UPDATE and with READ COMMITTED isolation. Sending 30 concurrent 'buy flag' requests with turbo-intruder-style parallelism lets the player pay once but receive multiple flags, and the flag delivered on race-win contains a distinct suffix.
labs.objective: Trigger a TOCTOU on the balance check to receive the premium-tier flag with only 1 credit.
labs.flag_hint: flag{toctou_read_committed_no_row_lock}
skills_taught: SELECT FOR UPDATE and advisory locks
labs.inspired_by: HackTM 2023 'premium' + PortSwigger 'Smashing the state machine' by James Kettle + corCTF 2022 race set

labs.title: XS-Leak via Cross-Origin Frame Count
labs.description: A one-shot direct-message app exposes an /inbox page that renders 1 iframe per unread thread. Same-origin policy blocks reading content, but window.length is not opaque. By embedding /inbox?search=<guess> in a cross-origin frame, the attacker uses window[0].frames.length as a boolean oracle and binary-searches the admin bot's private message that contains the flag.
labs.objective: Extract the flag character-by-character from the admin bot's private inbox using only cross-origin oracles.
labs.flag_hint: flag{xsleak_window_length_binary_search}
labs.inspired_by: hxp CTF 2022 'valentine' + Google CTF 2023 'under-construction' + XSLeaks wiki entry 'frame-count'

labs.title: Cookie Tossing via Sibling Subdomain
labs.description: An admin panel at admin.lab.local reads a session cookie without checking __Host- prefix and without SameSite=Strict. The player controls user content on user.lab.local, plants a cookie scoped to .lab.local that shadows the admin session, then triggers a stored-XSRF that runs with the shadowed identity to trigger a privileged export.
labs.objective: Toss a session cookie from user.lab.local so admin.lab.local trusts the attacker session for the /export?flag=1 request.
labs.flag_hint: flag{cookie_toss_leading_dot_domain_shadow}
labs.inspired_by: PlaidCTF 2021 'carmen sandiego' + TokyoWesterns 2019 'j2j' + CVE-2023-27536 curl cookie scoping

labs.title: CRLF Injection in Node HTTP Client via Header Split
labs.description: A URL shortener stores user-supplied metadata in a header it forwards to an internal analytics service using an older Node http.request. The header value is not validated for CR/LF, allowing the player to split the request and inject an arbitrary internal POST that hits the flag microservice which trusts a fixed Authorization header injected by the reverse proxy.
labs.objective: Inject a smuggled POST /internal/flag with the trusted Auth header and reflect the response.
labs.flag_hint: flag{node_http_header_crlf_smuggle_internal}
skills_taught: node http client hardening (Node >= 18 rejects CR/LF)
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-32213 + CVE-2022-32215 llhttp + hxp CTF 2022 'sqlite-userland' side-channel infra

labs.title: EJS SSTI via outputFunctionName
labs.description: A marketing site renders per-tenant landing pages with EJS and passes user-controlled tenant options to render(). The tenant.outputFunctionName field is unsanitised, letting an attacker close the auto-generated JS function and inject arbitrary code that runs at template compile time inside the Node process.
labs.objective: Inject an outputFunctionName that reads /flag and returns it as the rendered page.
labs.flag_hint: flag{ejs_outputFunctionName_compile_time_rce}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2022 'prophecy' + CVE-2022-29078 EJS RCE + BlackHat EU 2021 SSTI research

labs.title: Flask Session Pickle Deserialization
labs.description: A custom Flask app rolls its own session backend that pickles user data, HMAC-signs it, and stores it in a cookie. The HMAC key is derived from an app-config value the player leaks via a debug endpoint. Once the key is known, the player forges a pickle payload whose __reduce__ spawns os.system to read the flag.
labs.objective: Leak the HMAC key, forge a session with a __reduce__ payload, and exfil the flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{pickle_reduce_hmac_leaked_key_pwn}
skills_taught: why itsdangerous is not enough with pickle
labs.inspired_by: PicoCTF 'session' + DiceCTF 2022 'blazingfast' + numerous HackerOne reports

labs.title: GraphQL Batching to Skip Rate Limits and Auth
labs.description: A GraphQL gateway enforces auth and rate limits per HTTP request via middleware, but a legacy /batch endpoint accepts an array of queries and executes them concurrently on the resolver layer. Individual resolvers do not re-check auth. The player packages a 2FA-brute-force plus a mutation to read the flag inside one batched call.
labs.objective: Bypass rate limits with batched queries, brute the 6-digit 2FA, and call flag { value }.
labs.flag_hint: flag{graphql_batch_bypass_rate_limit_and_auth}
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #1224660 GraphQL batching + SekaiCTF 2023 'noteshare' + PortSwigger GraphQL cheat

labs.title: MongoDB Operator Injection via JSON Login
labs.description: A login endpoint accepts JSON credentials and passes the body straight into a Mongo find(). The player replaces the password field with { "$gt": "" } to bypass auth, then chains to a $where JS injection on a search endpoint to enumerate the admin-only flag collection.
labs.objective: Log in as admin using operator injection, then dump the flag via $where JS.
labs.flag_hint: flag{nosql_gt_and_where_js_pivot}
labs.inspired_by: TSJ CTF 2022 'nim-notes' Mongo variant + RealWorldCTF 'noSchool' + OWASP NoSQL cheatsheet

labs.title: vm2 Sandbox Escape via Proxy Handler
labs.description: A snippet-runner lets users execute short JavaScript inside a pinned vulnerable vm2 (pre-3.9.18). Solving requires abusing the known Proxy-based host-object leak to obtain a reference to a host Error constructor, then walking prototypes to require('child_process') outside the sandbox and reading /flag.
labs.objective: Escape the vm2 sandbox and execute host-side node code to print the flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{vm2_proxy_gadget_host_prototype_leak}
labs.inspired_by: DiceCTF 2023 'vm-me-baby' + CVE-2023-37903 vm2 + Oxeye disclosure

labs.title: wkhtmltopdf HTML-to-PDF file:// SSRF
labs.description: An invoicing app renders customer-supplied HTML through a legacy wkhtmltopdf binary with --enable-local-file-access. The player embeds an <iframe src="file:///flag"> and downloads the generated PDF, which contains the flag text.
labs.objective: Inject an HTML payload that pulls file:///flag into the rendered PDF.
labs.flag_hint: flag{wkhtml_local_file_iframe_pdf_leak}
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #226756 wkhtmltopdf + RealWorldCTF 2021 'InvoiceMaker' + CVE-2022-35583 class

labs.title: Blind XXE via OOB DNS Callback
labs.description: A B2B API accepts XML uploads and swallows all parser errors. External DTD loading is enabled. The player defines a parameter entity that reads /etc/passwd, embeds it in a subdomain, and reads DNS logs from a dedicated attacker box (also shipped in-lab) to exfil the flag.
labs.objective: Perform blind XXE with an external DTD to exfiltrate /flag via the lab's DNS collector.
labs.flag_hint: flag{blind_xxe_parameter_entity_dns_channel}
labs.inspired_by: HITCON 2022 'BabyXXE' + CVE-2021-33813 jdom + PayloadsAllTheThings XXE

labs.title: Nginx Alias Traversal on Missing Trailing Slash
labs.description: The reverse proxy config has 'location /static { alias /var/www/static/; }' (note the missing trailing slash on the location). Requesting /static../secrets/flag.env resolves to /var/www/secrets/flag.env. A simple path recon plus reading the misconfig from an exposed /nginx-status page teaches the player to hunt this class in the wild.
labs.objective: Read /var/www/secrets/flag.env via the alias misconfiguration.
labs.flag_hint: flag{nginx_alias_trailing_slash_traversal}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2023 'static-pastebin' + Detectify nginx misconfig research + numerous H1 reports

labs.title: CSP Bypass via Trusted JSONP Endpoint
labs.description: The app enforces a strict CSP but whitelists a legacy /api/jsonp?callback= endpoint on the same origin for backwards compatibility. Because the callback parameter is reflected verbatim into an executable JS response, the player uses it as an arbitrary-code oracle bypassing script-src.
labs.objective: Achieve XSS on the admin bot despite the CSP by leveraging the JSONP callback.
labs.flag_hint: flag{csp_jsonp_callback_arbitrary_js}
labs.inspired_by: DiceCTF 2023 'recursive-csp' + Google CTF 2018 'JiT' + CSP evaluator research

labs.title: Spring Expression Language Injection via Error Page
labs.description: A Spring Boot app has a custom @ControllerAdvice that renders unhandled errors through a template resolving ${...} against SpelExpressionParser. User input reaches the error message. The player crafts a request that triggers a controlled exception, injects an SpEL payload that resolves T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec, and reads /flag.
labs.objective: Trigger an error whose message evaluates a SpEL payload spawning a reverse shell / cat /flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{spel_runtime_exec_via_error_advice}
labs.inspired_by: SekaiCTF 2023 'frog-waf' + CVE-2022-22963 Spring Cloud Function + CVE-2018-1273

labs.title: SQLite ATTACH DATABASE File-Write Primitive
labs.description: A read-only analytics viewer builds SQL from user-supplied JSON filters but forgets to disable the ATTACH DATABASE statement. The player attaches a new database to a writable path served by the same host, populates it with a webshell payload delivered as a table, and requests the file to trigger PHP execution reading /flag.
labs.objective: Use ATTACH DATABASE + INSERT to drop a webshell into the docroot and cat /flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{sqlite_attach_docroot_php_shell}
labs.inspired_by: hxp CTF 2022 'sqlite-userland' + PayloadsAllTheThings SQLite + CVE-2019-8457 heap OOB context

labs.title: DNS Rebinding to a Localhost Admin API
labs.description: A desktop-companion service exposes an unauthenticated JSON API on 127.0.0.1:9999 that trusts Origin: null and same-site checks. The player hosts a page that resolves rebind.lab.local first to their attacker IP (loading JS), then to 127.0.0.1 (fetching the flag via XHR). A ship-in-lab pdnsd sells the rebind TTL trick.
labs.objective: Trick the admin bot into pointing rebind.lab.local at 127.0.0.1 and reading /flag from the local API.
labs.flag_hint: flag{dns_rebind_low_ttl_localhost_json_api}
labs.inspired_by: RealWorldCTF 2022 'chatUWU-lite' + Tavis Ormandy's Transmission RCE + numerous IoT disclosures

labs.title: OAuth Authorization Code Theft via redirect_uri Bypass
labs.description: A first-party OAuth server matches redirect_uri by prefix rather than exact match. The player registers an OAuth client with https://app.lab.local/cb as the exact URI, then requests authorization with redirect_uri=https://app.lab.local/cb.attacker.local/cb. The victim admin bot clicks the crafted /authorize link, the code lands on the attacker origin, and the player exchanges it for a token that reads /flag.
labs.objective: Steal the admin's authorization code via redirect_uri bypass and use it to call /api/flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{oauth_redirect_prefix_match_code_steal}
labs.inspired_by: HackerOne #1101877 GitLab OAuth + PortSwigger OAuth 2.0 authentication vulnerabilities + LakeCTF 2023 'sso'

labs.title: JSON vs Form-Encoded Content-Type Confusion
labs.description: A Rack-based API uses one middleware that parses application/json and another that parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The auth check runs on the JSON body but the business logic reads the form-parsed body. Sending a request with both bodies (JSON as advertised, form-encoded as fallback) lets the attacker present role=user to auth and role=admin to the flag handler.
labs.objective: Craft a dual-body request that passes auth as user but is executed as admin.
labs.flag_hint: flag{content_type_dual_parse_role_shadow}
labs.inspired_by: DiceCTF 2024 'funnylogin' + James Kettle 'HTTP Desync Attacks' parser-differential + HackerOne #813012

labs.title: Regex ReDoS as a Timing Oracle for Password Recovery
labs.description: A password-reset endpoint validates the answer with a regex whose backtracking cost depends on how many leading characters of the answer are correct. The response is generic on mismatch, but request time leaks per-character correctness. The player builds a differential timing oracle to recover the 32-char reset token used to read the admin's flag mail.
labs.objective: Recover the admin reset token character by character via ReDoS timing signals.
labs.flag_hint: flag{redos_backtracking_timing_reset_token}
labs.inspired_by: hxp CTF 2022 'valentine' + Google CTF 2019 'BnBnBn' + Snyk ReDoS research

labs.title: Web Cache Deception via Static-Suffix Path Confusion
labs.description: A CDN in front of the app aggressively caches responses whose URL ends with .css, .js, or .png regardless of Content-Type. The origin uses framework routing that ignores the suffix ('/account/settings/foo.css' still returns the personalised /account/settings HTML). The player tricks the admin bot into visiting /account/flag_page.css, the CDN caches the admin's page, and the attacker fetches it.
labs.objective: Bait the admin bot into caching /account/flag_page.css then fetch the cached HTML to read the flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{cache_deception_static_suffix_admin_cache}
labs.inspired_by: Omer Gil web cache deception (BlackHat 2017) + SekaiCTF 2024 'cachestory' + PortSwigger cache research

labs.title: Nim strformat Compile-Time Injection
labs.description: A note server written in Nim uses the strformat macro on user input at compile-time via a hot-reload mechanism that recompiles a per-note template. Because strformat evaluates arbitrary Nim inside &, the player writes a note whose payload runs code that opens /flag and stores it in another note they can read.
labs.objective: Post a note whose strformat payload reads /flag and stores it back into the notes table.
labs.flag_hint: flag{nim_strformat_ampersand_compile_time}
labs.inspired_by: TSJ CTF 2022 'nim-notes' + Nim strformat security advisory + polyglot-lang CTF class

labs.title: Obsolete Chunked Encoding Smuggling (Node llhttp)
labs.description: A stack pairs a lax Go frontend with a stricter (but still-flawed) Node llhttp backend. The player smuggles requests using invalid chunk-extension parsing that the Go proxy tolerates but llhttp treats as body. This poisons the response queue so the next unauthenticated user receives the admin's session and can call /api/flag.
labs.objective: Poison the socket queue to receive the admin session on the follow-up request and dump the flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{chunk_ext_lax_go_strict_node_smuggle}
labs.inspired_by: corCTF 2023 'smuggler' + CVE-2022-32215 llhttp + PortSwigger 'browser powered desync'

labs.title: Prototype Pollution to XSS via Express Render Layout
labs.description: An express+ejs app uses res.render(view, req.body) with a body-parser that recursively assigns nested keys. Polluting Object.prototype.layout to an attacker-controlled template that pulls user content lets the player achieve stored XSS on the admin bot and steal a session token bound to /flag.
labs.objective: Pollute Object.prototype.layout so the admin bot renders an attacker template, capture the session, read /flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{proto_layout_ejs_render_xss_admin}
labs.inspired_by: HackTM 2023 'premium' + CVE-2023-26136 tough-cookie prototype pollution class + POSIX Snyk research

labs.title: PHP Phar Deserialization via Metadata-Only File Op
labs.description: An old PHP gallery app rejects .phar uploads by extension but accepts .jpg. A separate 'preview' endpoint calls file_exists on user-supplied paths and supports the phar:// stream wrapper. The player uploads a polyglot JPG+PHAR whose metadata contains a serialized gadget chain, triggers deserialization via file_exists('phar://...'), and gains RCE to read /flag.
labs.objective: Upload a phar polyglot, trigger deserialization via phar://, RCE, and cat /flag.
labs.flag_hint: flag{phar_stream_wrapper_metadata_gadget_rce}
labs.inspired_by: hxp CTF 2022 'phar-in-jpg' + Sam Thomas BlackHat 2018 phar research + CVE-2023-22809 sudoedit context

labs.title: Next.js Image Optimizer SSRF to Internal Metadata
labs.description: An outdated Next.js image optimizer allows arbitrary remote URLs (a common misconfig of images.domains vs images.remotePatterns). The player abuses /_next/image?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/... on a lab that ships a fake IMDS containing the flag as an IAM role token.
labs.objective: Fetch the fake IMDS through the image optimizer and decode the flag from the returned bytes.
labs.flag_hint: flag{next_image_optimizer_ssrf_fake_imds}
skills_taught: response-body based leaks through image handlers
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-46298 Next.js image + SekaiCTF 2024 'imgcdn' + numerous cloud SSRF reports

labs.title: Logger of Doom: JNDI Lookup Injection
labs.description: A minimal Java (Javalin) web app logs every incoming User-Agent through a homegrown formatter that expands ${…} placeholders. One placeholder resolver naively dispatches jndi: lookups to a bundled InitialContext, allowing a hostile LDAP referral to load a class from an attacker-controlled endpoint. A stub RMI/LDAP server is bundled inside the container network so the exploit is fully self-contained and cannot reach the outside internet.
labs.objective: Trigger remote code execution by crafting a User-Agent with a JNDI lookup that points at the in-container mock LDAP server, deliver a serialized Java gadget, and read /flag.txt off the app's filesystem.
labs.flag_hint: Flag lives at /flag.txt inside the app container; only root's process (the app) can read it because of a discretionary ACL.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) — Apache Log4j2 JNDI lookups

labs.title: OGNL Echo: Header-Driven Expression Injection
labs.description: A wiki-style Kotlin/Ktor app renders a status banner from an X-Atlassian-Token style header via a naive OGNL evaluator that does not enforce SecurityMemberAccess. Any header sent to /status/echo is compiled and evaluated, giving arbitrary Java method invocation.
labs.objective: Craft an OGNL expression in the header that invokes Runtime.exec, exfiltrate the container hostname, and read the flag from /srv/wiki/attachments/flag.txt.
labs.flag_hint: Attach a payload that pipes command output back through the response body; grep for CTF{ in the response.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-26134 — Atlassian Confluence OGNL injection

labs.title: Class Loader Roulette: Data Binder RCE
labs.description: A Spring-style form binder maps HTTP parameters onto a POJO's nested properties without a deny-list. Given the right chain of names, an attacker walks class.module.classLoader.* into the container's Tomcat-like access log valve, retargeting the log file into the webroot as a JSP.
labs.objective: Rewrite the access-log valve to drop a JSP shell into /app/webroot, then request it to execute commands and print the flag.
labs.flag_hint: JSP shell will run as the app user; flag is under /var/lib/app/secrets/flag.txt.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2022-22965 (Spring4Shell)

labs.title: Managed Transfer SQLi to Session Forge
labs.description: A .NET-style file-transfer portal exposes a guest download endpoint that concatenates a folderId into a raw T-SQL query on a SQLite backing store. Successful UNION-based extraction yields the server-side machine key used to sign the auth cookie.
labs.objective: Extract the HMAC signing key via UNION SELECT, forge an authenticated admin session cookie, then list private transfers and read the flag from a locked folder.
labs.flag_hint: Look for a folder named 'restricted-2024-q3' after logging in as admin.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-34362 — Progress MOVEit Transfer SQLi

labs.title: Nested Archive Preview Traversal
labs.description: A Rails-like Ruby web app renders previews for uploaded zip archives. The unzipper resolves entries relative to /tmp/preview but a nested .tgz inside the zip is expanded through a helper that forgot to sanitize member paths, letting an attacker escape into the app's config directory.
labs.objective: Craft a zip-in-tar-in-zip archive whose innermost entry writes over /opt/app/config/routes.rb to expose /debug, then curl /debug for the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The flag is served by the newly exposed /debug/flag route.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-2825 — GitLab arbitrary file read via nested archives

labs.title: PHP-CGI Argv Injection via Best-Fit Glyph
labs.description: An nginx→php-cgi (fastcgi) container mimics the historical php-cgi query-string-as-arguments bug. A locale conversion step maps a soft-hyphen character into a literal '-', which becomes '-d' allowing runtime ini overrides such as allow_url_include=1.
labs.objective: Send a request whose query string contains the best-fit glyph so php-cgi enables auto_prepend_file, then include /flag.php.
labs.flag_hint: auto_prepend_file:///flag.php on a php://input request will echo the flag in the response body.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-4577 — PHP-CGI argument injection

labs.title: VPN Session Cookie Command Injection
labs.description: A Go-based SSL-VPN portal telemetry endpoint feeds the raw session cookie into a shell script through system() without quoting. The cookie is normally opaque and set by the same server, so no attacker validation exists—but the /global-protect/portal/ pre-auth handler accepts any client-supplied SESSID cookie for the first hit.
labs.objective: Send a crafted SESSID cookie carrying a shell substitution that writes /tmp/flag.copy readable by the low-priv user, then read it via a second unauthenticated file-serve endpoint.
labs.flag_hint: The chained file endpoint is /global-protect/pub/;/tmp/flag.copy.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-3400 — Palo Alto GlobalProtect command injection

labs.title: Response Buffer Bleed
labs.description: A C-based tiny HTTP server (bundled with a safe libmicrohttpd fork) mishandles Content-Length on a hostname endpoint. The response buffer's uninitialized tail includes the last-N bytes of a rotating session token pool, letting an attacker cyclically collect valid SESSIONIDs.
labs.objective: Repeatedly hit /oauth/idp with an overlong Host header and reassemble a live admin session token from response tails, then use it to fetch /admin/flag.
labs.flag_hint: You need ~40 requests to reconstruct a valid token; look for pattern SESS- followed by 32 hex chars.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-4966 (Citrix Bleed)

labs.title: Appliance Diagnostic Command Injection
labs.description: A Python Flask 'network appliance' admin API exposes a /api/v1/totp/user-backup endpoint that calls tar with a user-controlled username interpolated into an f-string. The endpoint requires only a boolean 'trust-token' cookie that is set client-side.
labs.objective: Set the trust cookie, inject shell metacharacters into username to run a reverse-style command that writes /tmp/pwn, then verify via /api/v1/health that the file exists and read it back.
labs.flag_hint: Chained health endpoint reflects any file whose path is passed as ?log=.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-21887 — Ivanti Connect Secure command injection

labs.title: Router Normalization Auth Skip
labs.description: An express-like Node app protects /admin/* with an auth middleware, but the router normalizes /%2e%2e/admin/panel after the middleware fires. A downstream file server accepts the normalized path and serves the admin panel unauthenticated.
labs.objective: Craft the encoded traversal URL to reach the admin dashboard without credentials and pull the flag from the /admin/api/settings JSON.
labs.flag_hint: The settings JSON has a 'motd' field seeded with the flag.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-46805 — Ivanti Connect Secure auth bypass

labs.title: CI Suffix Auth Bypass
labs.description: A Kotlin CI server has a servlet filter that skips authentication for static resources by checking whether the URI ends with '.jsp'. The internal dispatcher, however, matches only the servlet prefix, so /app/rest/users;.jsp reaches the REST API unauthenticated.
labs.objective: Create a new admin user via the unauth REST endpoint, log in, then execute a build step that prints the flag from /var/lib/ci/flag.
labs.flag_hint: Build agent logs contain the flag after your custom step runs.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-27198 — JetBrains TeamCity auth bypass

labs.title: AJP Smuggle Behind Reverse Proxy
labs.description: A container ships an HAProxy front-end that speaks HTTP to a Tomcat-like backend, but with an AJP connector exposed on localhost. A crafted request from the front pushes attributes that impersonate a trusted internal client, granting admin routes.
labs.objective: Use HTTP request smuggling to poison a connection so the backend sees a spoofed remote_user of 'admin', reach /manager/status, and dump the flag from the JMX bean.
labs.flag_hint: JMX bean 'com.example:type=Flag' getContent() returns the flag.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-46747 (F5 BIG-IP TMUI) and CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat)

labs.title: Setup Flag Revival
labs.description: A wiki-style app tracks 'setup-complete' in a mutable config file. The setup wizard checks the flag on every request, but a race window and unauth /setup/lifecycle/reset endpoint let an attacker roll the flag back to false and then create a fresh admin account.
labs.objective: Reset the setup flag, register the first admin, log in, and read the flag from the admin console's site-info page.
labs.flag_hint: The admin console site-info textarea stores the flag as a 'welcome banner'.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-22515 — Confluence broken access control

labs.title: CLI @-File Arbitrary Read
labs.description: A Jenkins-style automation server exposes an HTTP CLI channel. Its argument parser, borrowed from an old args4j, expands any token beginning with '@' by reading the referenced file and splicing its contents in as arguments. An unauthenticated who-am-i command echoes any parse errors.
labs.objective: Send a CLI invocation whose arg is @/etc/app/secret.key and read the leaked key from the error, then reuse it to sign an admin cookie and pull the flag.
labs.flag_hint: The cookie signs a JWT read by /me; admin user's profile.about contains the flag.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-23897 — Jenkins arbitrary file read via CLI

labs.title: Remote Setup Race
labs.description: A remote-desktop management app leaves its SetupWizard.aspx reachable via a path-normalization quirk (/SetupWizard.aspx/anything). Hitting it re-initializes the identity store, letting an attacker set a new admin password without knowing the old one.
labs.objective: Reach the setup wizard through the path suffix, seed a new admin, log in to the console, and download the audit log — the flag is one of its records.
labs.flag_hint: Audit log line prefixed with SEED: contains the flag.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-1709 — ConnectWise ScreenConnect auth bypass

labs.title: Multipart Filename Traversal to OGNL
labs.description: A Struts-like MVC framework passes the multipart filename parameter through OGNL when populating a form-backing bean. A leading '../' walks the upload out of /tmp and into the app's classes directory, and a follow-up include triggers the newly dropped class as a servlet filter.
labs.objective: Upload a JSP whose filename traverses into /WEB-INF/classes, force it to be picked up by the reload watcher, then request the filter path to run and get the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Filter dumps env vars; the FLAG env var is set for the app process.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-50164 / CVE-2024-53677 — Apache Struts2 file upload

labs.title: VFS Preview SSTI Escape
labs.description: A file-transfer app's file preview renders text files with a mini template engine that resolves ${env:X} tokens. A user in the sandboxed VFS can request a preview of a file they uploaded whose contents include ${script:javascript:...}, executing on the server outside the sandbox.
labs.objective: Upload a payload file, request its preview through /preview/<hash>, run a JS command that reads /host/flag.txt, and echo it into the preview response.
labs.flag_hint: Look at the rendered response body after the preview request; the script output replaces the token.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-4040 — CrushFTP VFS/SSTI

labs.title: Unauth Screen Render Groovy
labs.description: An e-commerce framework's screen-rendering endpoint accepts a screen name plus arbitrary groovyProgram parameter. Auth is enforced by a decorator that checks a session flag but only after the render kicks off, so pre-render Groovy still evaluates.
labs.objective: POST to /webtools/control/main with a groovyProgram that executes 'cat /flag' and captures stdout into the rendered response's error slot.
labs.flag_hint: The Groovy 'throw new Exception(output)' pattern surfaces stdout in the error page.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2024-38856 — Apache OFBiz screen render RCE

labs.title: JDBC H2 INIT to RCE
labs.description: A data-tool app lets admins configure new database connections. During validation, it opens a JDBC URL supplied by the user. The H2 driver on the classpath honours INIT= to run SQL, and CREATE ALIAS lets that SQL define a Java function that executes arbitrary code.
labs.objective: Submit a crafted H2 JDBC URL to /api/database/test-connection whose INIT clause creates an alias running Runtime.exec, then trigger it to write the flag into a public /uploads path.
labs.flag_hint: Copy /flag to /app/uploads/leak.txt, then GET it.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-38646 — Metabase H2 JDBC RCE

labs.title: WDDX Deserialization File Read
labs.description: A ColdFusion-like scripting server accepts WDDX packets on a public /CFIDE-like endpoint. The deserializer builds a wrapper object whose accessor reflectively calls FileInputStream — enough to read arbitrary files as the service account.
labs.objective: Craft a WDDX payload that reads /opt/app/security/password.properties, then use the admin password inside to log in and pull the flag.
labs.flag_hint: Admin dashboard 'Server Info' widget stores the flag as its 'note' field.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2023-26360 — Adobe ColdFusion deserialization

labs.title: Predictable Machine Key Deserialization
labs.description: A .NET file-handler simulates a Telerik-style Web UI dialog handler. It expects an AES-encrypted, HMAC-signed payload but derives both keys from a hardcoded seed shipped with every build. Any client can encrypt a BinaryFormatter gadget and get code execution.
labs.objective: Encrypt a small serialization gadget with the shipped seed, POST it to /Telerik.Web.UI.DialogHandler.aspx, and read the flag written to /var/log/dialog.log.
labs.flag_hint: Gadget writes the flag to a log file the app reads back via /debug/log.
labs.inspired_by: CVE-2019-18935 & CVE-2024-4358 — Progress Telerik UI

labs.title: Upload Handler .NET Deserialization
labs.description: A managed file-transfer web app posts multipart uploads with a hidden serialized 'state' blob (LosFormatter-like). Because the machine key is derivable from static build metadata, an attacker can forge state that carries a serialization gadget.
labs.objective: Forge a state blob that executes 'id > /tmp/who', trigger it via /Upload/State, then read who via a debug page.
